# SP3d — Editable density and surface rules, inspector and slice viewer: Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the terrain editable as data. The default density expression and the default surface-rule tree become two schema leaves of a new `json` kind (`density.defs`, `surface.rules`). Their defaults are today's trees written as data, and their numbers can reference the existing parameters, so every slider keeps working on an edited tree. An edited tree is validated as untrusted JSON before it reaches the generator. It travels through the session (undo, URL, presets, live preview) like any other parameter, and it is inspected in a new **Density** drawer tab of `?map`:
- a node tree with tap mutes;
- a node form;
- a JSON editor with its own printer and parser;
- a slice viewer of the final density, any selected node, the blocks or a rule node's mask, on a vertical or horizontal plane, re-rendered on every edit, with up to 3 pinned slices side by side.

With the defaults the world is bit-identical: no voxel, tile, metric or golden changes, and `GENERATOR_VERSION` stays 5. SP3e then designs the three draft presets on this tooling.

**Architecture:**
- **The `json` leaf kind (`core/params`).** `jsonLeaf(def, format)` with `merge: 'atomic'`. Tier 1 (`core/params/json.ts`, inside `checkLeaf`) guarantees a canonical-safe, bounded JSON value: a budgeted iterative walk, a 50-issue cap, and an identity-preserving deep-frozen clone registered in a `WeakSet`, whose canonical text is cached. The default trees are data in `core/params/defaultTrees.ts`. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes to 2 with an identity migration.
- **Tier 2 and resolution (`gen`).**
  - `gen/density/source.ts` and `gen/surface/source.ts` hold the source model (parameter refs in every numeric field, `recip`, tap mutes), the semantic validation (per node, whole-tree bounds, the def graph, costs, a static magnitude analysis) and the resolvers, which fold refs into numbers and deep-freeze the result. Both are memoised by frozen tree.
  - `gen/trees.ts` `validateParamTrees` runs both on a params document, with issue paths prefixed by the leaf path.
  - The interval bounds propagate UNKNOWN instead of NaN, and the surface scan clamps its depth noise (the fast-path contract).
- **Rejection everywhere.** The session takes an injected validator (constructor, `setProfile`, `commitPatch`, `load`, `restore`); the page's session comes from `openMapSession`; the worker's configure replies `BAD_PARAMS`. History keys are hashed, the URL hash is capped at 64 KiB with a notice, and `fnv1a64` streams its UTF-8 bytes so a commit with two capped trees stays within 4 ms.
- **Slices (`gen/inspect`, `workers`, `engine`).**
  - `gen/inspect/fieldSlice.ts` evaluates the `density`, `node`, `blocks` and `rule` fields over sample columns: vertical planes from full ColumnSamples, horizontal planes from four-corner point samples.
  - `gen/inspect/cost.ts` charges every slice a deterministic, op-weighted work cost, acquisition included.
  - `workers/protocol.ts` `planFieldSlice` splits a request into parts under `PART_BUDGET`, or refuses it with a limit (the one implementation, shared by workers, engine and UI). The pool runs the parts on all workers, cancels queued parts on supersession and probes single voxels (`fieldProbe`).
- **Inspector (`ui/inspector`).** Pure models for the tree, the form, the editor, the slice drawing (colormap, contour, histogram) and the hover and request streams, with thin DOM modules (`densityTab.ts`, `jsonEditor.ts`, `sliceView.ts`) wired into `mapPage.ts`.
- **Metrics and tools.** DT2 gains two parts over edited trees; U2 perturbs both json leaves (68 leaves); U4 gets the version-1 fixtures; an untrusted-JSON mutation fuzz runs on the unit tier. The bench gains four rows and three absolute gates; uiSmoke gains eight Density steps and five review shots.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript 7 (tsgo, strict, erasableSyntaxOnly, verbatimModuleSyntax), Vite 8, Vitest 5, Node 24 (`worker_threads`), Bun 1 for the JavaScriptCore golden check, headless Chrome over CDP for the browser tools. No new dependencies.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-sp3d-editable-dag-inspector-design.md`, revised by this plan's dry run (§16). Master: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-architecture-design.md`. Previous SPs: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-sp3b-density-terrain-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-sp3c-surface-rules-palette-design.md` and the SP3c plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-sp3c-surface-rules-palette.md`.

**Dry run.** Every task below was executed before this plan was written, as one commit per task on a scratch branch (`dry/sp3d`), test first: each task's tests failed on its parent and passed on its commit, with `npm run typecheck && npm test` green.
- **Phase 0** (Tasks 1-4) ran on `dry/sp3d`. Task 4's stop condition did not fire: all 19 `COL_FIELD_BOUNDS` are bounded, and no default, U2 variant, uiSmoke tree or default-sized rule tree without a fast path exceeds a column-cost maximum.
- **Phase 1** ran four chains in parallel: density (Tasks 5-8), surface (9-10), engine (11-12) and UI (13). **Phase 2** (Tasks 14-15) ran on `dry/sp3d`. **Phase 3** ran three chains: fuzz (16), slice (17-19) and inspector (20-23). **Phase 4** (Tasks 24-30) ran in order.
- **Joins.** Each phase's chains were joined into `dry/sp3d` in plan order by cherry-pick, with no textual conflict. Every joined commit was then re-checked (`npm run typecheck && npm test` at each one, 9 of 9 and 8 of 8 green), with the goldens check and the compared-set diff at the tip.
- **The calibration** (Task 19) ran with the machine idle, after every other chain had finished. Neither stop condition fired: the work unit is 12.6 ns on the default tree and 7.4 ns on the worst-case tree, every part at `PART_BUDGET` takes ≤ 98.4 ms p50 (gate 250), and every acquisition cost is within 2 × of its constant.
- **Pins built.** The pinned slices (the spec's cut line) were built in Task 27, before the bench and the smoke so both cover them; the cut line was not taken.
- **Review Focus.** Five scenarios were then pinned by tests in their owning tasks (below). All five were real bugs, fixed in Tasks 17 (items 1 and 5) and 25 (items 2-4); item 1's fix re-pinned `CORNER_STEEP_COST` from 2^13 to its measured 5,120.
- **The spec revision.** The spec was revised on `main` from the dry run (§16, then the Review Focus corrections), and the branch was rebased onto it.
- **Where the content comes from.** Code blocks and diffs are copied from the final commits. Every `Expected:` line is what the replay printed: each task's tests applied over its parent fail, the commit passes, and then the whole suite passes.

Results:
- **Tests:** `npm test` passes 2,671 tests (188 files; 2 skipped files, 1 expected fail, 6 skipped tests).
- **Metric tiers:** fast, quick and full are green. The compared set (DT1, DT2's existing parts, T1-T8, T1lowland, S1-S3, B1, B2, B4, B5, N1-N6, M1) is identical to `main`'s on the quick and full tiers, seconds excepted. The only changes are the expected ones outside it: DT2's two edited-tree parts (all 0; full: 128 + 128 trees), U2 1 over 68 leaves (`density.defs` and `surface.rules` live on the land column), U4 0.
- **Determinism:** `GENERATOR_VERSION` stays 5, and `test/goldens.json` is byte-identical to `main`'s after every goldens check. The 54 goldens match in V8 (`?selftest=1` in Chrome and Firefox) and in Bun (JavaScriptCore).
- **Bench:** against the re-recorded baseline (26 rows), `slice.vertical128` p50 140.4 ms (gate 300), `slice.horizontal128` p50 504.4 ms (reported), `slice.partWorst` p50 63.3 ms (gate 250), `session.commitMaxTree` p50 3.165 ms (gate 4) and `terrain.real` p50 2.437 ms (gate 4). Before the record, every non-exempt row was within +30 % of SP3c's baseline.
- **UI smoke test:** 125/125, with the eight Density steps. In the browser on 6 workers, a fresh vertical 128² slice takes about 76 ms after a tree edit and a horizontal one at extent 8192 about 160-175 ms.
- **Review assets:** five Density screenshots in `docs/superpowers/specs/assets/sp3d/`: `density-vertical-hover.png`, `density-muted-terrain.png`, `density-broken-json.png`, `density-horizontal-8192.png` and `density-stacked-800.png`.

The task notes give the details.

## Global Constraints

- **Language and tooling:** TypeScript strict, `erasableSyntaxOnly` (no enums, namespaces or constructor parameter properties), `verbatimModuleSyntax`; ES2022 modules. **No new runtime or dev dependencies.**
- **Determinism rules.** They apply to `gen/**` (so all of `gen/inspect/**`, `gen/density/source.ts`, `gen/surface/source.ts` and `gen/trees.ts`), `core/**` (so `core/params/json.ts` and `defaultTrees.ts`), `world/blocks/**` and the `DET_FILES`:
  - only the Math allowlist (no `Math.fround`, no `**`, no `Math.pow`), with transcendentals through `core/detMath`;
  - no `Intl`, `localeCompare`, `toLocale*`, `normalize`, `TextEncoder` or `TextDecoder`;
  - no `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now` or `console`;
  - no `new Function` and no `eval`.
- **Import aliasing.** In `gen/**`, `core/noise/**`, `core/spline/**`, `metrics/**` and `world/blocks/**`, imported values are used only through top-level `const X = binding;` aliases. Types come in through `import type`, and namespace imports are not used. An aliased assertion function cannot keep its assertion signature (TS2775): call the validator and throw yourself.
- **No numeric exports from gen.** `gen/**` exports no numeric constants and no numeric data (`test/arch/rules/banned.ts`; both gen `defaults.ts` files disappear in SP3d, and Task 14 removes their dead exemption). Every number shared with the UI, the workers or the tests lives in `core/constants.ts`: `TREE_LIMITS`, `COL_FIELD_BOUNDS`, the column-cost maxima, `SLICE_NS`, `SLICE_EXTENTS`, the acquisition costs and the three budgets, `SLICE_RULE_NA`. The form's defaults live in `ui/inspector/form.ts`, and the editor's caps (512 KiB, 50 lines) in `ui/inspector/editorModel.ts`. Gen's own weights and factors stay module-private.
- **Layer imports** (`test/arch/rules/imports.ts`):
  - `core` value-imports only `core` (not even gen types);
  - `gen` value-imports only `core`, `gen` and `world/blocks/**` (type-only `world/store/api.ts`), **never `metrics/` nor `workers/`**;
  - `workers` may import gen and metrics; `engine` value-imports only core, world, engine and `workers/protocol.ts` (gen and metrics as types); `ui` may import anything but `*.worker.ts`;
  - `src/` never imports `test/**`, and only `engine/` spawns workers.

  Consequences: the vertical sample points come from `metrics/crossSection.ts`'s `segmentPointAt` and reach gen as input (Task 11); the acquisition costs and budgets live in `core/constants.ts`, re-exported by `workers/protocol.ts` (Tasks 17-18); the split and refusal math is one pure function, `planFieldSlice` in `workers/protocol.ts`, used by the workers, the engine and the UI (Task 18).
- **Own-property lookups.** `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf` and the like are valid def and tap names: every lookup keyed by tree content uses a `Map`, a `Set` or `Object.hasOwn`, never `obj[name]` or `in`.
- **Coordinates.** colKeys are numeric only. The world window is half-open, `[−2^19, 2^19)` (`core/coords.ts` `WINDOW_HALF`). North is −z and east is +x. World height y −64 … 319 and sea level 63 are fixed constants.
- **The world does not change.** `GENERATOR_VERSION` stays 5 and `test/goldens.json` stays byte-identical (54 keys, `sp1.params` included). Never bump to 6.
  - **Goldens check.** Every task that touches generation, hashing or the schema (Tasks 2, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 17, 28 and the exit, 30) runs `npm run test:goldens` as a check, then `git diff --exit-code main -- test/goldens.json`, which must be empty. If the run rewrote anything, it is a bug: restore the file with `git checkout main -- test/goldens.json` and find it.
  - **Compared set.** Spec §11's compared set is DT1, DT2's existing parts, T1-T8, T1lowland, S1-S3, B1, B2, B4, B5, N1-N6 and M1 (seconds excepted). Task 1 records `main`'s metric outputs outside the repository. Tasks 7, 8, 9, 10, 14 and 16 diff the quick tier's `test/metrics/.out/*.json` against them, and the exit task diffs both tiers. The compared set must stay equal. Outside it, the expected changes are U2's leaves (66 → 68, Task 14) and DT2's two new parts (Task 16).
- **Governance.**
  - `test/thresholds.lock.json` changes exactly twice (Task 1: `startedSps`; Task 16: the two DT2 parts), each time through `npm run test:accept-thresholds`, and each such commit appends one line to the SP3d spec's `## Threshold log` (CI checks this per push).
  - `test/schema-shape.lock.json` changes once, in Task 14, through `npm run test:accept-schema` (schemaVersion 2, `json:density` and `json:surfaceRules`).
  - The README params block changes only through `npm run docs:params` (Task 14).
  - `test/stateIds.lock.json` never changes.
  - `test/baselines.json` changes once, in Task 28, through `npm run bench:record`, in the same commit as its rows (`benchGates.test.ts` requires every row to be recorded).
  - Master amendments land in the commit spec §12 assigns them; the arch-checked ones (`test/arch/masterSpec.test.ts`) land with what they describe.
- **TDD.** Write the test, run it and see it fail for the stated reason, implement, run it and see it pass. `npm run typecheck && npm test` must be green before every commit (`npm test` runs the unit, arch, metrics-fast and integration projects).
- **Processes.** Never kill, signal or touch processes you did not start (the user may be running other programs, such as a game). Never use `pkill`, `killall` or pattern kills; stop only the PIDs you started, and stop every server and browser you launch. The browser tools start their own `vite preview` on a free port (never 5183) and their own headless Chrome with a short `--profile-dir $(mktemp -d /tmp/wi10-XXXX)` (a hand-launched Chrome gets a short `--user-data-dir` likewise).
- **Quiet machine.** The calibration (Task 19) and the bench (Task 28) need a quiet machine: nothing else may load the CPU while they run. If the load stays high because of other programs, record the evidence (`uptime`, `top -bn1 | head -15`) and say so rather than committing a loaded baseline.
- **Outward-facing actions.** Pushes and merges happen only with the user's go-ahead.
- **Commit trailer** on every commit: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JbkJNEMpTrQS68LobuogBc`.
- **Staging.** `git add` takes explicit paths only.

## Review Focus

1. **A horizontal slice of any tree that reads `col steep`.** The input is a `density.defs` tree whose evaluated expression reads `col steep`, for example the default with the islands const replaced by add(const −1e6, col steep) (work cost 571, about the default's), or any `col` node switched to the field `steep` in the form, sliced on the horizontal plane with the field `density` or a node that reaches steep. Nothing tested it: `sliceCost.test` only checked that the column cost uses `CORNER_STEEP_COST` per sample, and no test sent a steep-reading horizontal request through `planFieldSlice` or the request stream; the refusal tests used trees that do not read steep, and the calibration's 0.63 × for the steep acquisition looked harmless. A reasonable person expects the 32² draft and then the 128² slice of a tree of ordinary weight, a steep-reading tree to have a non-zero refusal limit like any other, and never a notice that says "limit 0". It was a bug, and a spec defect: with §5.2's 2^13, the column cost 128 × (c + 2^13) exceeds the 2^20 refusal limit for every c ≥ 1, because n² × 2^13 = `REQUEST_BUDGET` at n = 128, so the draft was drawn and then the 128² slice was refused with "node too heavy for a 128² slice (cost 571, limit 0)". Fixed in Task 17: `CORNER_STEEP_COST` is re-pinned to its measured 5,120 = 5 × 2^10 (64.5 µs at the default's 12.6 ns unit, 1.0 × the new constant, 1.70 × at partWorst's unit). A steep tree then gets its draft and its 128² slice (k = 11, 12 parts on 4 workers), and the refusal limits with steep are 3,072 per sample for a 128² slice (5.4 × the default) and 11,264 for a draft. The spec's §5.2 and §16 say so.
   Tests: Task 17 "a steep-reading horizontal 128² slice of a default-weight tree fits REQUEST_BUDGET, and its 32² draft DRAFT_BUDGET", "acquisition costs, budgets and the rule field's n/a value"; Task 18 "a steep-reading tree of default weight: its horizontal 128² slice and draft are planned, never refused with limit 0"; Task 24 "a tree that reads col steep: the horizontal draft and then the 128² slice are requested with no notice; its limit is 3 072, never 0"
2. **The JSON editor's scroll while its text is hidden.** The input is a drawer narrower than 1,200 px, the default on 1,366-1,440 px laptops, where the Slice/JSON sub-tabs start on "Slice": a row whose text lies below the editor's first view (`root.b.x`, at 2,165 px of text) is selected there, then the "JSON" sub-tab is clicked; or a re-print happens while the Density tab is hidden (the toolbar's undo on another tab). Nothing tested it. Only the pure line arithmetic was tested (`scrollTopForLine` with a visible height, `densityLayout`, `shownPanes`). The DOM wrote `scrollTop` at once on a `display: none` textarea, which ignores the write. The sub-tab button never scrolled again, and `restoreScroll` put back the pixels saved before the hide, not the re-print's anchor. uiSmoke's 800 px step only took a screenshot. A reasonable person expects §3.2's "selecting a row highlights the node and scrolls the text to it" to hold whenever the text is shown, and a re-print to show the anchor it mapped. It was a bug, confirmed in headless Chrome: the new smoke step failed on the old code with the editor at 0 px and the highlighted node at 2,165 px. Fixed in Task 25: a pure `ScrollKeeper` (`editorModel.ts`) keeps a scroll asked for while the view is 0 tall (a line, a re-print's anchor, the latest winning) and writes it when the text shows again. Hiding a displayed view keeps its offsets the same way unless a request is owed. `jsonEditor.ts` routes every scroll through it, and the tab's layout (sub-tab click, layout change) calls save before it hides the JSON pane and restore after it shows it. With the fix the step scrolls to 2,049 px, with the node in view, and keeps that scroll across a Slice/JSON switch. §3.1 says so.
   Tests: Task 25 "a scroll request made while the view height is 0 is kept and applied on show", "a re-print while hidden restores the mapped anchor, not the saved pixels"; Task 29 uiSmoke step "density narrow: the tab 1,000 px wide (Slice/JSON sub-tabs), a row selected under Slice, then the JSON sub-tab" (and "the steps run in SMOKE_STEPS order: the Density steps after rule and before console (SP3d spec §6)")
3. **Literal text typed in the node form.** The input is '0,5' or '1,5' (a Spanish decimal comma), '' (a cleared field), '0x10', ' 7 ', '-0' or '1e999' committed in any literal number field of the form (`const.v`, clamp or rangeChoice `lo`/`hi`, `mute`, slide knots). Nothing tested it: the form's own `typedNumber` (`Number(text.trim())`, '' → NaN) was private, the form tests passed numbers straight to `setNumber`, and only the panel's `parseFieldText` had tests. A reasonable person expects §3.3's "as `valueField` does": text that is not a number refused with a message naming what was typed, and '-0' handled as the panel handles it. It was a bug: '0,5' and '' were refused as `NOT_FINITE — expected a finite number, got NaN`, which dropped the typed text, and '-0' was refused as `NEGATIVE_ZERO`, which the panel accepts as 0. Fixed in Task 25: `form.ts` `setTypedNumber` reads the text with the panel's `parseFieldText`. Text that spells no number is refused with `NOT_NUMBER — expected a number, got "0,5"`, a typed −0 is written 0, '0x10' is 16 in both places, ' 7 ' is 7, and '1e999' stays tier 1's `NOT_FINITE`. The form's text fields commit through it. §3.3 says so.
   Test: Task 25 "typed literal text commits like valueField: the panel's parse, NOT_NUMBER naming the text, a typed −0 as 0"
4. **Muting a tap from its tree row while another node is selected.** The input is `root` (or any node other than the tap) selected, with the slice field on `selected` or the form's value at the hover in view, then the mute checkbox of the `terrain` row (`root.a.a`) ticked. Nothing tested it: the row's checkbox committed through the form's commit, which selects the edit's returned node, and `toggleMute` returns the tap. The form tests checked only the candidate value, and uiSmoke's mute step muted from the row with the field on `density`, where the jump does not show. A reasonable person expects a mute toggled from a row to be a plain edit, with the selection staying where it was (§3.2 moves it only after undo, redo, reset, load or a renumbering edit), so the selected node's slice and hover value show the muted world. It was a bug: the selection jumped to the tap, and a selected muted tap shows its unmuted subtree (§3.4). Fixed in Task 25: the row's commit keeps the current selection (`form.ts` `selectionAfterCommit('row', current, …)`), while the form's own mute keeps the tap. In headless Chrome the root stays the current row after the row's mute, and its `selected` slice equals the `density` field's (p1 −1.448, < 0: 50.4 %). §3.2 says so.
   Tests: Task 25 "a row mute keeps the current selection; the form mute keeps the tap"; Task 29 uiSmoke step "density mute: the terrain tap muted from its row, the root selected and the field on selected"
5. **A `rule` slice part, or a rule probe, interrupted on a heavy valid tree.** The input is the field `selected` on a rule node, vertical plane, with a tier-2-valid density tree near the column-cost maximum: the default root plus mul(20, a balanced add of 32 `noise detail` leaves at 16 octaves, double), column cost about 0.4 G of the 0.95 G maximum. Configures arrive while rule parts run, as when the user drags a slider. Nothing tested it: the 50 ms abort tests covered only the density field on the default and partWorst trees. The rule branch built its probe column through `surfaceProbeColumn`, whose density fill ran with `NEVER`, and polled `stop()` only between samples. A reasonable person expects §4.5 and §10: a configure stops a running part within 50 ms for every field. It was a bug: the probe column takes 101-131 ms to build on that tree, and a part returned 103-110 ms after `stop()` turned true in process, 152-159 ms after `Atomics.store` in real threads. Fixed in Task 17: `surfaceProbeColumn` gains a `stop` overload whose density fill polls it every 8 corner rows (a stopped build returns null and leaves the one-column cache empty). The rule branch of `evaluateFieldSlice` and `probeField` pass the part's `stop`. The part now stops within 0.1 ms in process, and the probe within 0.8 ms. §5.1 and §5.3 say so.
   Tests: Task 17 "a rule part, and a rule probe, stop within 50 ms of stop() on a heavy valid tree: the probe column's build polls it" (and the poll counts in "%s: stop() is polled once per sample, and a stop returns null", "stop() is polled before the column and before evaluating"); Task 19 "a heavy valid tree (heavyDetailPatch), a vertical rule part of one sample column: ABORTED within 50 ms of Atomics.store while its probe column fills"

## Branch

Create `sp3d/editable-dag-inspector` from `main` before Task 1: `git switch main && git switch -c sp3d/editable-dag-inspector`.

## How to apply the code blocks

- **New files:** create them with exactly the content shown.
- **Modified files:** each diff is `git diff` output. Apply it from the repository root with `git apply` (or `git apply --3way`), in task order; every diff applies on top of all earlier tasks. Renamed files (Task 14's arch fixture) are a `git apply` diff too.
- **Generated files** come from the commands shown:
  - `test/thresholds.lock.json`, `test/schema-shape.lock.json` and the README params block are shown as the dry run's output, and yours must match;
  - `test/goldens.json` is never changed: the goldens checks rerun it and it must stay equal to `main`'s;
  - `test/baselines.json` and the five uiSmoke screenshots in `docs/superpowers/specs/assets/sp3d/` are produced on your machine.
- **Expected outputs** come from the dry-run replay on the reference machine (i7-12700H, 20 threads, Node 24.21, Chrome 155, Firefox 157, Bun 1.4.3). Timings vary; counts must match.
- **Order inside a task:** the failing tests and their fixtures come first (Step 1, including `test/fixtures/**`, `test/unit/fixtures/**` and `test/arch/fixtures/**`), watched failing (Step 2), then the implementation. Test-support code under `test/harness/`, `test/arch/rules/`, `test/bench/` and `test/tools/` is part of the implementation step, because the tests fail without it.
- **Dry-run notes** under each task record the rulings the dry run made, and the executor follows them.
  - **Task numbers.** The dry run used this plan's numbers, so "Task N" in a note means this plan's Task N. The dry run's commit SHAs have been rewritten to the task they were, and `main`'s to `main`.
  - **Combined notes.** Notes headed "From …" combine several rulings sections: the controller's pre-flight rulings (Tasks 11, 13, 14, 19, 20, 23, 27), the two joins (Tasks 13 and 23), the spec revision (Tasks 4 and 30) and the Review Focus items (Tasks 17, 25 and 29).
  - **Paths.** `P/…` in a note is the dry run's git-ignored work directory (`.superpowers/sp3d/`), which you do not have; the scratch worktrees named there were the dry run's. `P/baseline-out/` is your `$BASE_OUT` (Task 1), and `P/base` the detached worktree at `main` that recorded it.
  - **Totals.** A note's RED/GREEN totals are the dry run's at the time. The Review Focus tests were added later, so the replay's `Expected:` blocks are authoritative.

1. A detached worktree at `main`, sharing `node_modules`:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p "$BASE_OUT"
   git worktree add --detach ../wi10-sp3d-base main
   ln -s "$PWD/node_modules" ../wi10-sp3d-base/node_modules
   ```
2. In `../wi10-sp3d-base`: `npm run test:metrics`, then `cp -r test/metrics/.out "$BASE_OUT/quick"` (the dry run: 80 s, 9 files, 28 passed and 1 skipped, 30 `.out` files).
3. Still there, start `npm run test:metrics:full` in the background and, when it is done, `cp -r test/metrics/.out "$BASE_OUT/full"` (the dry run: 275 s, 9 files, 29 passed, 30 `.out` files). It must be finished before any timing task (Tasks 19 and 28). Then remove the worktree: delete its `node_modules` symlink, then `git worktree remove ../wi10-sp3d-base`.
4. Save the comparison script as `$BASE_OUT/compare.mjs`. It drops every key matching /seconds/i at any depth, so only wall times are ignored:
   ```js
   // node compare.mjs <outDir> <baseDir>: compare metric .out JSON files, ignoring keys that match /seconds/i.
   import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
   import { join } from 'node:path';

   const [outDir, baseDir] = process.argv.slice(2);
   const strip = (v) => Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(strip)
     : v !== null && typeof v === 'object'
       ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(v).filter(([k]) => !/seconds/i.test(k)).map(([k, x]) => [k, strip(x)]))
       : v;
   const read = (dir, f) => strip(JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, f), 'utf8')));
   const files = readdirSync(baseDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json')).sort();
   let differ = 0;
   for (const f of files) {
     let same = false;
     try { same = JSON.stringify(read(outDir, f)) === JSON.stringify(read(baseDir, f)); } catch { same = false; }
     if (!same) differ++;
     console.log(`${same ? 'equal  ' : 'DIFFERS'} ${f}`);
   }
   console.log(`${differ} of ${files.length} differ`);
   ```
   Inspect a differing file by hand, e.g. `diff <(python3 -m json.tool "$BASE_OUT/quick/DT2.json") <(python3 -m json.tool test/metrics/.out/DT2.json)`.

Task 7's mask hash is already pinned in its test (the dry run computed it at `main`); it needs no baseline of yours.

```ts
import { describe, expect, expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
import { TREE_LIMITS } from '../../src/core/constants';
import { CanonicalError, canonicalCacheHits, canonicalJSON } from '../../src/core/params/canonical';
import { checkJson, countTreeNodes, TREE_KEY_RE, type JsonFormat, type JsonIssueCode, type TreeIssueCode } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import type { Issue, IssueCode } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import type { ExprErrorCode } from '../../src/gen/density/expr';
import type { RuleErrorCode } from '../../src/gen/surface/rules';

/** Runs tier 1 and lists `path CODE` pairs. */
const run = (v: unknown, format: JsonFormat = 'density', path = format === 'density' ? 'density.defs' : 'surface.rules') => {
  const out: Issue[] = [];
  const value = checkJson(v, path, out, format);
  return { value, issues: out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`), raw: out };
};
const ok = (v: unknown, format: JsonFormat = 'density') => {
  const r = run(v, format);
  expect(r.issues).toEqual([]);
  return r.value;
};
/** A value nested `n` containers deep: `[[…[0]…]]` or `{a: {a: … 0}}`, built without recursion. */
const nested = (n: number, kind: 'array' | 'object'): unknown => {
  let v: unknown = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) v = kind === 'array' ? [v] : { a: v };
  return v;
};
const isDeepFrozen = (v: unknown): boolean => {
  const stack = [v];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const x = stack.pop();
    if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null) continue;
    if (!Object.isFrozen(x)) return false;
    for (const k of Object.keys(x)) stack.push((x as Record<string, unknown>)[k]);
  }
  return true;
};

describe('TREE_LIMITS', () => {
  test('the tier-1 bounds of SP3d spec §1.7, in core/constants.ts', () => {
    expect(TREE_LIMITS).toEqual({ depth: 48, values: 65_536, arrayItems: 1_024, stringUnits: 256, textUnits: 131_072, issues: 50, keyLength: 32 });
    expect(Object.isFrozen(TREE_LIMITS)).toBe(true);
  });
  test('the key pattern is ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$', () => {
    expect(TREE_KEY_RE.source).toBe('^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$');
    for (const k of ['a', 'Z9', 'terrain', 'constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty', 'a_b', 'x'.repeat(32)]) expect(TREE_KEY_RE.test(k)).toBe(true);
    for (const k of ['', '_a', '1a', 'a.b', 'a-b', '__proto__', 'a b', 'é', 'x'.repeat(33)]) expect(TREE_KEY_RE.test(k)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('checkJson: every tier-1 rule at its exact path (D1)', () => {
  test('a valid value passes and is cloned', () => {
    const v = { root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'const', v: 1.5 }, b: { op: 'y' } }, defs: { constructor: { op: 'const', v: -2 } }, flag: true, s: 'x' };
    const c = ok(v);
    expect(c).toEqual(v);
    expect(c).not.toBe(v);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(v)).toBe(false);
  });

  test('NOT_JSON: null, undefined, functions, symbols, bigints, non-plain objects, holes, accessors', () => {
    expect(run(undefined).issues).toEqual(['density.defs NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run(null).issues).toEqual(['density.defs NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run(undefined, 'surfaceRules').issues).toEqual(['surface.rules.root NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run({ root: { a: null } }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.root.a NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run({ root: { a: undefined } }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.root.a NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run({ f: () => 1, s: Symbol('s'), b: 1n }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.b NOT_JSON', 'density.defs.f NOT_JSON', 'density.defs.s NOT_JSON']);
    expect(run({ d: new Date(0), m: new Map(), r: /x/, k: new (class K {})() }).issues)
      .toEqual(['density.defs.d NOT_JSON', 'density.defs.k NOT_JSON', 'density.defs.m NOT_JSON', 'density.defs.r NOT_JSON']);
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-sparse-arrays
    expect(run({ root: { knots: [[0, 1], , [2, 3]] } }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.root.knots[1] NOT_JSON']);
    let reads = 0;
    const getter = Object.defineProperty({}, 'g', { enumerable: true, get: () => { reads++; return 1; } });
    expect(run({ x: getter }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.x.g NOT_JSON']);
    expect(reads).toBe(0);
    // A null-prototype object is plain.
    expect(ok(Object.assign(Object.create(null) as object, { a: 1 }))).toEqual({ a: 1 });
  });

  test('NOT_FINITE and NEGATIVE_ZERO (never normalised)', () => {
    expect(run({ a: NaN, b: Infinity, c: -Infinity, d: JSON.parse('1e999') as number }).issues)
      .toEqual(['density.defs.a NOT_FINITE', 'density.defs.b NOT_FINITE', 'density.defs.c NOT_FINITE', 'density.defs.d NOT_FINITE']);
    expect(run({ root: { op: 'const', v: -0 } }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.root.v NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
    expect(run(JSON.parse('{"root": {"knots": [[0, -0]]}}')).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.root.knots[0][1] NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
    expect(run(-0).issues).toEqual(['density.defs NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
    expect(run({ kind: 'block', t: -0 }, 'surfaceRules').issues).toEqual(['surface.rules.root.t NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
    expect(ok({ a: 0, b: -1e308, c: 5e-324 })).toEqual({ a: 0, b: -1e308, c: 5e-324 });
  });

  test('BAD_KEY: empty, dotted, __proto__, leading digit or underscore, too long; quoted and truncated to 40', () => {
    const v = JSON.parse('{"defs": {"": 1, "a.b": 2, "__proto__": {"polluted": 1}, "1a": 3, "_a": 4, "ok": 5}}') as unknown;
    expect(run(v).issues).toEqual([
      'density.defs.defs."" BAD_KEY', 'density.defs.defs."1a" BAD_KEY', 'density.defs.defs."__proto__" BAD_KEY',
      'density.defs.defs."_a" BAD_KEY', 'density.defs.defs."a.b" BAD_KEY',
    ]);
    const long = 'k'.repeat(100);
    const r = run({ [long]: 1, [`a\nb\u0000`]: 2 });
    expect(r.issues).toEqual([`density.defs.${JSON.stringify('a\nb\u0000')} BAD_KEY`, `density.defs."${'k'.repeat(39)} BAD_KEY`]);
    expect(r.raw[1]!.path.length).toBe('density.defs.'.length + 40);
    expect(run({ ['x'.repeat(33)]: 1 }).issues).toEqual([`density.defs."${'x'.repeat(33)}" BAD_KEY`]);
    expect(ok({ ['x'.repeat(32)]: 1 })).toEqual({ ['x'.repeat(32)]: 1 });
    // A key in an array item's object, and at the top of a rules value.
    expect(run({ rules: [{ 'b-c': 1 }] }, 'surfaceRules').issues).toEqual(['surface.rules.root.rules[0]."b-c" BAD_KEY']);
    // A surrogate pair is never split by the truncation.
    const pairs = run({ [`${'p'.repeat(38)}\u{1F600}x`]: 1 });
    expect(pairs.raw[0]!.path).toBe(`density.defs."${'p'.repeat(38)}`);
  });

  test('keys are checked before they are written: __proto__ never reaches a prototype', () => {
    const v = JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {"polluted": 1}, "a": {"__proto__": {"polluted": 2}}}') as unknown;
    const r = run(v);
    expect(r.issues).toEqual(['density.defs."__proto__" BAD_KEY', 'density.defs.a."__proto__" BAD_KEY']);
    expect(r.value).toBeUndefined();
    expect((({}) as Record<string, unknown>)['polluted']).toBeUndefined();
    // Object.prototype member names are valid keys and become own data properties of a plain clone.
    const c = ok({ constructor: 1, toString: { op: 'y' }, valueOf: [1] }) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(c)).toBe(Object.prototype);
    expect(Object.hasOwn(c, 'constructor') && Object.hasOwn(c, 'toString') && Object.hasOwn(c, 'valueOf')).toBe(true);
    expect(c['constructor']).toBe(1);
  });

  test('JSON_TOO_DEEP: container depth ≤ 48, the top container being 1; the deep container is not entered', () => {
    expect(ok(nested(48, 'array'))).toEqual(nested(48, 'array'));
    expect(ok(nested(48, 'object'))).toEqual(nested(48, 'object'));
    expect(run(nested(49, 'array')).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'[0]'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    expect(run(nested(49, 'object')).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'.a'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    expect(run(nested(49, 'object'), 'surfaceRules').issues).toEqual([`surface.rules.root${'.a'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
  });

  test('ARRAY_TOO_LONG and STRING_TOO_LONG at the offending value', () => {
    expect(ok({ a: new Array<number>(1024).fill(1) })).toBeDefined();
    expect(run({ a: new Array<number>(1025).fill(1) }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.a ARRAY_TOO_LONG']);
    expect(ok({ s: 'é'.repeat(256) })).toBeDefined();
    expect(run({ s: 'x'.repeat(257), t: ['y'.repeat(300)] }).issues).toEqual(['density.defs.s STRING_TOO_LONG', 'density.defs.t[0] STRING_TOO_LONG']);
  });

  test('JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES: 65,536 values pass, 65,537 stop the walk with that single issue', () => {
    // 1 top array + 64 arrays + 63 × 1,023 + x numbers.
    const build = (x: number) => [...Array.from({ length: 63 }, () => new Array<number>(1023).fill(1)), new Array<number>(x).fill(1)];
    const c = ok(build(1022));
    expect(canonicalJSON(c).length).toBe(131_071);
    expect(run(build(1023)).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
    // The single issue replaces the issues collected before the bound (here a NOT_FINITE, whose text counts 0).
    const r = run([NaN, ...build(1023)]);
    expect(r.issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
    expect(r.raw[0]!.message).toBe('more than 65536 values');
    expect(run(build(1023), 'surfaceRules').issues).toEqual(['surface.rules.root JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
  });

  test('JSON_TOO_LARGE: the canonical text ≤ 128 KiB, by a running estimate that stops the walk', () => {
    // 512 strings: 2 + 511 + Σ (L + 2) characters.
    const exact = [...new Array<string>(511).fill('s'.repeat(253)), 's'.repeat(252)];
    const c = ok(exact);
    expect(canonicalJSON(c).length).toBe(131_072);
    const r = run([...new Array<string>(512).fill('s'.repeat(253))]);
    expect(r.issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_LARGE']);
    expect(r.raw[0]!.message).toBe('canonical text longer than 131072 characters');
    // Keys count: {"k":…} adds the quoted key and the colon.
    const keyed = Object.fromEntries(Array.from({ length: 600 }, (_, i) => [`k${i}`, 'v'.repeat(250)]));
    expect(run(keyed).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_LARGE']);
  });

  test('the issue list stops at 50 and ends with one TOO_MANY_ISSUES at the leaf path ("N more")', () => {
    const v = Array.from({ length: 60 }, () => new Array<number>(1000).fill(Infinity));
    const r = run(v);
    expect(r.issues).toHaveLength(51);
    expect(r.issues.slice(0, 2)).toEqual(['density.defs[0][0] NOT_FINITE', 'density.defs[0][1] NOT_FINITE']);
    expect(r.issues[49]).toBe('density.defs[0][49] NOT_FINITE');
    expect(r.raw[50]).toEqual({ path: 'density.defs', code: 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES', message: '59950 more' });
    const rules = run({ rules: new Array<number>(51).fill(NaN) }, 'surfaceRules');
    expect(rules.issues.at(-1)).toBe('surface.rules TOO_MANY_ISSUES');
    expect(rules.raw.at(-1)!.message).toBe('1 more');
    expect(run({ rules: new Array<number>(50).fill(NaN) }, 'surfaceRules').issues).toHaveLength(50);
  });

  test('issues are appended to `out` after the issues already there', () => {
    const out: Issue[] = [{ path: 'x', code: 'NOT_NUMBER', message: 'm' }];
    expect(checkJson({ a: null }, 'p', out, 'density')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['x NOT_NUMBER', 'p.a NOT_JSON']);
  });

  test('an empty leaf path gives node paths alone', () => {
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    checkJson({ root: { a: null }, s: [NaN] }, '', out, 'density');
    checkJson(null, '', out, 'density');
    checkJson({ b: null }, '', out, 'surfaceRules');
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['root.a NOT_JSON', 's[0] NOT_FINITE', ' NOT_JSON', 'root.b NOT_JSON']);
  });
});

describe('checkJson: the budgeted walk (no recursion, no overflow, one issue)', () => {
  test('16,383 arrays of 1,024 numbers: the text estimate (commas included) stops it first', () => {
    const inner = () => new Array<number>(1024).fill(1);
    const v = Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, i) => Array.from({ length: i === 15 ? 1023 : 1024 }, inner));
    expect(v.flat()).toHaveLength(16_383);
    const t0 = performance.now();
    expect(run(v).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_LARGE']);
    expect(performance.now() - t0).toBeLessThan(2000);
  });

  test('shared sub-objects are counted at every visit', () => {
    const leaf = new Array<number>(1000).fill(NaN);
    expect(run(new Array<unknown>(100).fill(leaf)).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
    let d: unknown = 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) d = [d, d];
    expect(run(d).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_LARGE']);
    // A shared object that fits is cloned twice (the clone is a tree).
    const s = { op: 'y' };
    const c = ok({ a: s, b: s }) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(c['a']).toEqual(s);
    expect(c['a']).not.toBe(c['b']);
  });

  test('cyclic in-memory objects stop at the depth bound or the count bound', () => {
    const a: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    a['x'] = a;
    expect(run(a).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'.x'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    const b: unknown[] = [];
    b.push(b, b);
    expect(run(b).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
  });

  test('a 100,000-deep value gives one JSON_TOO_DEEP', () => {
    expect(run(nested(100_000, 'array')).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'[0]'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    expect(run(nested(100_000, 'object')).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'.a'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    expect(run(JSON.parse(`${'['.repeat(100_000)}${']'.repeat(100_000)}`)).issues).toEqual([`density.defs${'[0]'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
  });

  test('250,000 NOT_FINITE values: the count bound stops the walk first (one issue, never 250,000)', () => {
    const v = Array.from({ length: 250 }, () => new Array<number>(1000).fill(Infinity));
    expect(run(v).issues).toEqual(['density.defs JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES']);
  });
});

describe('checkJson: the identity-preserving frozen clone (§1.7, §1.12)', () => {
  test('object keys in sorted order at every depth, arrays in order', () => {
    const c = ok({ b: 1, a: { d: [{ z: 1, y: 2 }], c: 2 }, B: 0 }) as Record<string, any>;
    expect(Object.keys(c)).toEqual(['B', 'a', 'b']);
    expect(Object.keys(c['a'])).toEqual(['c', 'd']);
    expect(Object.keys(c['a'].d[0])).toEqual(['y', 'z']);
    expect(JSON.stringify(c)).toBe(canonicalJSON(c));
  });

  test('the clone is deep-frozen, and the input is left as it was', () => {
    const v = { root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'const', v: 1 }, b: { op: 'y' } }, k: [[1, 2], [3]] };
    const c = ok(v) as Record<string, any>;
    expect(isDeepFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
    expect(() => { c['root'].a.v = 2; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(v) || Object.isFrozen(v.root)).toBe(false);
  });

  test('a registered value is returned as itself, unchecked, for either format and path', () => {
    const c = ok({ root: { op: 'y' } });
    for (const [format, path] of [['density', 'density.defs'], ['surfaceRules', 'x.y'], ['density', '']] as const) {
      const out: Issue[] = [];
      expect(checkJson(c, path, out, format)).toBe(c);
      expect(out).toEqual([]);
    }
    // A frozen value tier 1 did not produce is still checked and cloned.
    const frozen = Object.freeze({ a: Object.freeze({ b: 1 }) });
    const c2 = ok(frozen);
    expect(c2).toEqual(frozen);
    expect(c2).not.toBe(frozen);
    // Primitives pass through (tier 2 rejects them).
    expect(ok(5)).toBe(5);
    expect(ok('s')).toBe('s');
  });
});

describe('canonicalJSON text cache (§1.12)', () => {
  test('a registered value prints from the cache, alone or nested, with the uncached text', () => {
    const v = { root: { op: 'mul', a: { op: 'const', v: 0.1 }, b: { op: 'noise', noise: 'density.noises.jag' } }, defs: {} };
    const c = ok(v);
    const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(c)) as unknown;
    const h0 = canonicalCacheHits();
    const text = canonicalJSON(c);
    expect(canonicalCacheHits()).toBe(h0 + 1);
    expect(text).toBe(canonicalJSON(copy));
    expect(canonicalCacheHits()).toBe(h0 + 1);
    expect(canonicalJSON({ patch: { density: { defs: c } } })).toBe(canonicalJSON({ patch: { density: { defs: copy } } }));
    expect(canonicalCacheHits()).toBe(h0 + 2);
  });

  test('the cache keeps the 64-level guard: a deep registered value nested too deep still throws the same error', () => {
    const c = ok(nested(48, 'array'));
    let wrapped: unknown = c;
    let wrappedCopy: unknown = nested(48, 'array');
    for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) { wrapped = [wrapped]; wrappedCopy = [wrappedCopy]; }
    expect(canonicalJSON(wrapped)).toBe(canonicalJSON(wrappedCopy));
    wrapped = [wrapped];
    wrappedCopy = [wrappedCopy];
    let err: unknown;
    try { canonicalJSON(wrappedCopy); } catch (e) { err = e; }
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(CanonicalError);
    expect(() => canonicalJSON(wrapped)).toThrow((err as Error).message);
  });

  test('unregistered values are not cached', () => {
    const v = { a: { b: 1 } };
    const h0 = canonicalCacheHits();
    canonicalJSON(v);
    canonicalJSON(v);
    expect(canonicalCacheHits()).toBe(h0);
  });
});

describe('countTreeNodes', () => {
  test('counts the objects that carry the format’s discriminator (op / kind)', () => {
    expect(countTreeNodes({ root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'const', v: 1 }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 't' } }, defs: { t: { op: 'y' } } }, 'density')).toBe(4);
    expect(countTreeNodes({ kind: 'sequence', rules: [{ kind: 'condition', if: { kind: 'not', if: { kind: 'skyOpen' } }, then: { kind: 'block', state: 'stone' } }] }, 'surfaceRules')).toBe(5);
    expect(countTreeNodes({ root: { op: 'slide', knots: [[0, 1]], x: { op: 'y' } } }, 'density')).toBe(2);
    expect(countTreeNodes(5, 'density')).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('issue codes', () => {
  test('tier-1 codes, and every gen tree code is a TreeIssueCode; both are IssueCodes', () => {
    expectTypeOf<JsonIssueCode>().toEqualTypeOf<
      'NOT_JSON' | 'NOT_FINITE' | 'NEGATIVE_ZERO' | 'BAD_KEY' | 'JSON_TOO_DEEP' | 'JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES' | 'ARRAY_TOO_LONG'
      | 'STRING_TOO_LONG' | 'JSON_TOO_LARGE' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES'>();
    expectTypeOf<ExprErrorCode>().toExtend<TreeIssueCode>();

      | 'EXPANDED_TOO_DEEP' | 'TOO_COSTLY' | 'VALUE_RANGE' | 'COLUMN_COST' | 'TOO_MANY_BIOMES' | 'NOT_SOLID' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES'>().toExtend<TreeIssueCode>();
    expectTypeOf<JsonIssueCode | TreeIssueCode>().toExtend<IssueCode>();
    const code: IssueCode = 'JSON_TOO_DEEP';
    expect(code).toBe('JSON_TOO_DEEP');
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkJson } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import {
  applyPatch, buildSchema, checkLeaf, checkParams, diffParams, group, int, jsonLeaf, num, renderReference, type Issue,
} from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { randomParams, randomPatch, randomValue } from '../harness/params';
import { currentShape } from '../harness/schemaShape';

const T = { scope: 'terrain', stage: 'terrain' } as const;
const TREE = { root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'const', v: 1 }, b: { op: 'y' } }, defs: {} };
const RULES = { kind: 'sequence', rules: [{ kind: 'block', state: 'stone' }] };
const children = (withJson: boolean) => ({
  a: group('A', 'group a', {
    n: num(0.5, { label: 'n', doc: 'a number', min: 0, max: 1, ...T }),
    ...(withJson ? { t: jsonLeaf(TREE, 'density', { label: 'tree', doc: 'a density tree', ...T }) } : {}),
    k: int(3, { label: 'k', doc: 'an int', min: 1, max: 8, ...T }),
  }),
  ...(withJson ? { r: jsonLeaf(RULES, 'surfaceRules', { label: 'rules', doc: 'a rule tree', ...T }) } : {}),
  m: num(2, { label: 'm', doc: 'another number', min: 0, max: 4, ...T }),
});
const S = buildSchema(group('J', 'json test schema', children(true)));
const PLAIN = buildSchema(group('J', 'json test schema', children(false)));
const leafOf = (path: string) => S.leaves.find((l) => l.path === path)!.leaf;
const brief = (issues: readonly Issue[]) => issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`);
/** A counting xorshift stream. */
const counted = (seed: number) => {
  let s = seed >>> 0 || 1;
  const next = () => {
    next.draws++;
    s ^= s << 13; s >>>= 0; s ^= s >>> 17; s ^= s << 5; s >>>= 0;
    return s;
  };
  next.draws = 0;
  return next;
};

describe('the json leaf kind (SP3d spec §1.1, D1)', () => {
  test('jsonLeaf builds an atomic leaf with its format; ParamMeta carries the format only on json leaves', () => {
    const l = jsonLeaf(TREE, 'density', { label: 'tree', doc: 'd', ...T });
    expect(l).toEqual({ tag: 'leaf', kind: 'json', merge: 'atomic', format: 'density', def: TREE, meta: { label: 'tree', doc: 'd', ...T } });
    expect(S.leaves.map((x) => x.path)).toEqual(['a.n', 'a.t', 'a.k', 'r', 'm']);
    expect(S.leaves[1]!.meta).toEqual({ path: 'a.t', label: 'tree', doc: 'a density tree', kind: 'json', format: 'density', scope: 'terrain', stage: 'terrain' });
    expect(S.leaves[3]!.meta.format).toBe('surfaceRules');
    expect(Object.hasOwn(S.leaves[0]!.meta, 'format')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('the schema default is tier 1’s registered frozen clone', () => {
    const d = S.defaults as unknown as { a: { t: unknown }; r: unknown };
    expect(d.a.t).toEqual(TREE);
    expect(d.a.t).not.toBe(TREE);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(d.a.t)).toBe(true);
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkJson(d.a.t, 'a.t', out, 'density')).toBe(d.a.t);
    expect(checkJson(d.r, 'r', out, 'surfaceRules')).toBe(d.r);
    expect(out).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('checkLeaf: tier 1 at the leaf path, undefined is NOT_JSON, never a throw', () => {
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkLeaf(leafOf('a.t'), undefined, 'a.t', out)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(checkLeaf(leafOf('r'), undefined, 'r', out)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(checkLeaf(leafOf('a.t'), { root: { op: 'const', v: -0 }, defs: { 'a.b': 1 } }, 'a.t', out)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(checkLeaf(leafOf('r'), { kind: 'block', state: null }, 'r', out)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(brief(out)).toEqual(['a.t NOT_JSON', 'r.root NOT_JSON', 'a.t.defs."a.b" BAD_KEY', 'a.t.root.v NEGATIVE_ZERO', 'r.root.state NOT_JSON']);
  });

  test('checkParams and applyPatch clone a new tree once and keep a registered one by identity', () => {
    const d = S.defaults as unknown as { a: { t: unknown } };
    const doc = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(S.defaults)) as { a: { t: unknown } };
    const r = checkParams(S, doc);
    expect(r.ok && (r.value as unknown as { a: { t: unknown } }).a.t).toEqual(TREE);
    const bad = checkParams(S, { ...doc, a: { ...doc.a, t: { root: [NaN] } } });
    expect(bad.ok ? [] : brief(bad.issues)).toEqual(['a.t.root[0] NOT_FINITE']);

    const edited = { root: { op: 'const', v: 2 }, defs: {} };
    const p1 = applyPatch(S, S.defaults, { a: { t: edited } });
    if (!p1.ok) throw new Error('patch refused');
    const t1 = (p1.value as unknown as { a: { t: unknown } }).a.t;
    expect(t1).toEqual(edited);
    expect(t1).not.toBe(edited);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(t1)).toBe(true);
    // Re-applying the patch that holds the clone (what commitPatch does on every edit) keeps the object.
    const p2 = applyPatch(S, S.defaults, { a: { t: t1, n: 0.25 } });
    expect(p2.ok && (p2.value as unknown as { a: { t: unknown } }).a.t).toBe(t1);
    const p3 = applyPatch(S, S.defaults, { a: { t: d.a.t } });
    expect(p3.ok && p3.value).toBe(S.defaults);
  });

  test('diffParams: a leaf that is the same object is unchanged without being printed; an edited tree is the patch by reference', () => {
    // canonicalJSON would throw on NaN: the identity short-circuit never prints it.
    const odd = { a: { ...S.defaults.a, t: { root: NaN } } };
    const base = { ...S.defaults, ...odd } as typeof S.defaults;
    expect(diffParams(S, base, base)).toEqual({});
    const edited = applyPatch(S, S.defaults, { r: { kind: 'block', state: 'dirt' } });
    if (!edited.ok) throw new Error('patch refused');
    const patch = diffParams(S, S.defaults, edited.value) as { r?: unknown };
    expect(Object.keys(patch)).toEqual(['r']);
    expect(patch.r).toBe((edited.value as unknown as { r: unknown }).r);
  });

  test('renderReference writes "<format> tree, <n> nodes" and an empty range', () => {
    const rows = renderReference(S).split('\n');
    expect(rows[3]).toBe('| `a.t` | json | density tree, 3 nodes |  |  | terrain | tree: a density tree |');
    expect(rows[5]).toBe('| `r` | json | surfaceRules tree, 2 nodes |  |  | terrain | rules: a rule tree |');
  });

  test('the shape lock records json:<format>', () => {
    expect(currentShape(S)).toEqual({ 'a.n': 'number', 'a.t': 'json:density', 'a.k': 'int', r: 'json:surfaceRules', m: 'number' });
  });
});

describe('the random-params harness skips json leaves with no draw (§1.1)', () => {
  test('randomValue returns the leaf default and draws nothing', () => {
    const next = counted(7);
    expect(randomValue(leafOf('a.t'), next)).toBe(leafOf('a.t').def);
    expect(randomValue(leafOf('r'), next)).toBe(leafOf('r').def);
    expect(next.draws).toBe(0);
  });

  test('randomPatch and randomParams draw the other leaves exactly as without the json leaves', () => {
    for (let seed = 1; seed <= 20; seed++) {
      const a = counted(seed);
      const b = counted(seed);
      const withJson = randomPatch(S, a);
      const without = randomPatch(PLAIN, b);
      expect(withJson).toEqual(without);
      expect(a.draws).toBe(b.draws);
      const pa = counted(seed);
      const pb = counted(seed);
      const full = randomParams(S, pa) as unknown as Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>;
      const plain = randomParams(PLAIN, pb) as unknown as Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>;
      expect(pa.draws).toBe(pb.draws);
      expect(full['a']!['t']).toEqual(TREE);
      expect([full['a']!['n'], full['a']!['k'], full['m']]).toEqual([plain['a']!['n'], plain['a']!['k'], plain['m']]);
    }
  });
});
```

Create `src/core/params/json.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The `json` leaf kind's tier-1 validator (SP3d spec §1.1, §1.7, D1) and the tree issue codes. `checkJson` guarantees a
 * canonical-safe, bounded JSON value whatever it is given (parsed text, a crafted URL, an in-memory candidate that
 * shares sub-objects or is cyclic): one budgeted iterative walk, never a throw, at most 50 issues. On success it returns
 * a fresh deep-frozen clone with sorted object keys, registered so that the same value is returned as itself
 * (identity-preserving, §1.12) and printed by `canonicalJSON` from a cache. Tier 2 (the formats' semantics) is gen's
 * (`validateParamTrees`, §1.8).
 */
import { TREE_LIMITS } from '../constants';
import { canonicalJSON, rememberCanonical } from './canonical';
import type { Issue } from './kit';

/** A JSON value as tier 1 accepts it: no null, finite numbers, plain objects (§1.7). */
export type JsonValue = string | number | boolean | readonly JsonValue[] | { readonly [key: string]: JsonValue };

/** The formats of the `json` kind: the density expression `{root, defs}` and the root surface rule (§1.2). */
export type JsonFormat = 'density' | 'surfaceRules';

/** Tier-1 codes (§1.7); no code names two different bounds. */
export type JsonIssueCode =
  | 'NOT_JSON' | 'NOT_FINITE' | 'NEGATIVE_ZERO' | 'BAD_KEY' | 'JSON_TOO_DEEP' | 'JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES' | 'ARRAY_TOO_LONG'
  | 'STRING_TOO_LONG' | 'JSON_TOO_LARGE' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES';

/**
 * Tier-2 codes, complete for SP3d (§1.7): every code of gen's `validateExpr` (`ExprErrorCode`) and `validateRules`
 * (`RuleErrorCode`), plus the source and bound codes of `validateDensitySource` and `validateRulesSource`. Declared here
 * because core cannot import gen; a type test keeps gen's unions inside it.
 */
export type TreeIssueCode =
  // validateExpr (gen/density/expr.ts)
  | 'NOT_OBJECT' | 'UNKNOWN_OP' | 'UNKNOWN_KEY' | 'NOT_FINITE' | 'BAD_FIELD' | 'UNKNOWN_NOISE' | 'NOISE_DIMS' | 'NOISE_REMAP'
  | 'BAD_NAME' | 'DUPLICATE_TAP' | 'UNKNOWN_REF' | 'REF_CYCLE' | 'NESTED_INTERPOLATED' | 'CLAMP_ORDER' | 'RANGE_ORDER'
  | 'KNOTS_SHAPE' | 'KNOTS_ORDER'
  // validateRules (gen/surface/rules.ts)
  | 'NOT_ARRAY' | 'UNKNOWN_KIND' | 'UNKNOWN_FIELD' | 'MISSING_FIELD' | 'UNKNOWN_BLOCK' | 'UNKNOWN_BIOME' | 'NOT_INTEGER'
  | 'OUT_OF_RANGE' | 'NEGATIVE_ZERO' | 'NOT_BOOLEAN' | 'BAD_SIDE' | 'GRADIENT_ORDER' | 'TOO_DEEP' | 'TOO_MANY_NODES'
  | 'NO_BAND_NOISE'
  // SP3d tier 2: parameter refs, recip, literal and value ranges, slide slopes, counts, depth and cost bounds, solidity
  | 'UNKNOWN_PARAM' | 'PARAM_KIND' | 'RECIP_OPERAND' | 'RECIP_ZERO' | 'LITERAL_RANGE' | 'SLIDE_SLOPE' | 'TOO_MANY_DEFS'
  | 'EXPANDED_TOO_DEEP' | 'TOO_COSTLY' | 'VALUE_RANGE' | 'COLUMN_COST' | 'TOO_MANY_BIOMES' | 'NOT_SOLID' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES';

/**
 * An object key of a tree value, also the pattern of def and tap names (§1.7): it closes empty, dotted and `__proto__`
 * names; `Object.prototype` member names (`constructor`, `toString`, …) match it, so lookups keyed by tree content use a
 * `Map`, a `Set` or `Object.hasOwn`.
 */
export const TREE_KEY_RE = new RegExp(`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,${TREE_LIMITS.keyLength - 1}}$`);

/** A rejected key appears in its issue path as JSON.stringify(key) cut to this many characters (§1.2). */
const KEY_PATH_CHARS = 40;

/** The deep-frozen clones checkJson produced; given one, checkJson returns it unchecked. */
const REGISTRY = new WeakSet<object>();

/** The node path of the value itself: '' for density (validateExpr's top level), `root` for rules (§1.2). */
const valuePath = (format: JsonFormat): string => (format === 'surfaceRules' ? 'root' : '');

/** `leaf` + node path: an empty node path gives the leaf path alone (D3). */
function fullPath(leaf: string, node: string): string {
  if (node === '') return leaf;
  if (leaf === '') return node;
  return node.startsWith('[') ? `${leaf}${node}` : `${leaf}.${node}`;
}

const childPath = (parent: string, key: string): string => (parent === '' ? key : `${parent}.${key}`);

/** JSON.stringify(key) cut to 40 characters, never between the two halves of a surrogate pair. */
function quotedKey(key: string): string {
  const q = JSON.stringify(key);
  if (q.length <= KEY_PATH_CHARS) return q;
  const last = q.charCodeAt(KEY_PATH_CHARS - 1);
  return q.slice(0, last >= 0xd800 && last <= 0xdbff ? KEY_PATH_CHARS - 1 : KEY_PATH_CHARS);
}

interface Visit {
  readonly v: unknown;
  /** Node path in the format's syntax. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** Containers above the value (the top value is 0). */
  readonly level: number;
  readonly parent: unknown[] | Record<string, unknown> | null;
  readonly key: string | number;
  /** An issue found when the parent was read (a rejected key, an array hole, an accessor); the value is not visited. */
  readonly bad?: { readonly code: JsonIssueCode; readonly message: string };
}

/**
 * Tier 1 for both formats (§1.7). Appends issues to `out` (paths: `path` + the format's node path) and returns
 * undefined, or returns the deep-frozen, key-sorted, registered clone (a registered value: itself). One iterative walk
 * that counts every value at every visit and keeps the canonical text's length as it goes: the first exceeded count or
 * text bound stops it with that single issue (replacing any collected); per-value bounds (depth, array length, string
 * length) are reported at the value, which is not entered. Collects at most 50 issues, then one TOO_MANY_ISSUES at
 * `path` ("N more"). Never throws.
 */
export function checkJson(v: unknown, path: string, out: Issue[], format: JsonFormat): JsonValue | undefined {
  if (typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && REGISTRY.has(v)) return v as JsonValue;
  const L = TREE_LIMITS;
  const top = valuePath(format);
  const issues: Issue[] = [];
  let more = 0;
  const report = (node: string, code: JsonIssueCode, message: string): void => {
    if (issues.length < L.issues) issues.push({ path: fullPath(path, node), code, message });
    else more++;
  };
  const containers: object[] = [];
  let values = 0;
  let text = 0;
  let height = 0;
  let result: unknown;
  let stop: Issue | null = null;
  const stack: Visit[] = [{ v, path: top, level: 0, parent: null, key: 0 }];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const t = stack.pop()!;
    if (t.bad !== undefined) { report(t.path, t.bad.code, t.bad.message); continue; }
    if (++values > L.values) { stop = { path: fullPath(path, top), code: 'JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES', message: `more than ${L.values} values` }; break; }
    if (t.level > height) height = t.level;
    const x = t.v;
    let clone: unknown;
    switch (typeof x) {
      case 'number':
        if (!Number.isFinite(x)) { report(t.path, 'NOT_FINITE', `expected a finite number, got ${String(x)}`); continue; }
        if (Object.is(x, -0)) { report(t.path, 'NEGATIVE_ZERO', 'negative zero is not allowed (write 0)'); continue; }
        text += String(x).length;
        clone = x;
        break;
      case 'string':
        if (x.length > L.stringUnits) { report(t.path, 'STRING_TOO_LONG', `${x.length} UTF-16 units, more than ${L.stringUnits}`); continue; }
        text += JSON.stringify(x).length;
        clone = x;
        break;
      case 'boolean':
        text += x ? 4 : 5;
        clone = x;
        break;
      case 'object': {
        if (x === null) { report(t.path, 'NOT_JSON', 'expected a JSON value, got null'); continue; }
        const depth = t.level + 1;
        if (Array.isArray(x)) {
          if (depth > L.depth) { report(t.path, 'JSON_TOO_DEEP', `container depth above ${L.depth}`); continue; }
          if (x.length > L.arrayItems) { report(t.path, 'ARRAY_TOO_LONG', `${x.length} items, more than ${L.arrayItems}`); continue; }
          text += 2 + (x.length > 0 ? x.length - 1 : 0);
          const c: unknown[] = [];
          containers.push(c);
          clone = c;
          for (let i = x.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const p = `${t.path}[${i}]`;
            const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(x, i);
            if (d === undefined) stack.push({ v: undefined, path: p, level: depth, parent: c, key: i, bad: { code: 'NOT_JSON', message: 'an array hole' } });
            else if (d.get !== undefined || d.set !== undefined) stack.push({ v: undefined, path: p, level: depth, parent: c, key: i, bad: { code: 'NOT_JSON', message: 'an accessor property' } });
            else stack.push({ v: d.value, path: p, level: depth, parent: c, key: i });
          }
        } else {
          const proto: unknown = Object.getPrototypeOf(x);
          if (proto !== Object.prototype && proto !== null) { report(t.path, 'NOT_JSON', 'expected a plain object'); continue; }
          if (depth > L.depth) { report(t.path, 'JSON_TOO_DEEP', `container depth above ${L.depth}`); continue; }
          const keys = Object.keys(x);
          let written = 0;
          // A key that matches the pattern prints as itself in quotes, then a colon.
          for (const k of keys) if (TREE_KEY_RE.test(k)) { written++; text += k.length + 3; }
          text += 2 + (written > 0 ? written - 1 : 0);
          // Leaves the switch before sorting a huge key list; the check after it stops the walk.
          if (text > L.textUnits) break;
          keys.sort();
          const c: Record<string, unknown> = {};
          containers.push(c);
          clone = c;
          for (let i = keys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            const k = keys[i]!;
            if (!TREE_KEY_RE.test(k)) {
              stack.push({ v: undefined, path: childPath(t.path, quotedKey(k)), level: depth, parent: c, key: k, bad: { code: 'BAD_KEY', message: `key ${quotedKey(k)} does not match ${TREE_KEY_RE.source}` } });
              continue;
            }
            const p = childPath(t.path, k);
            const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(x, k)!;
            if (d.get !== undefined || d.set !== undefined) stack.push({ v: undefined, path: p, level: depth, parent: c, key: k, bad: { code: 'NOT_JSON', message: 'an accessor property' } });
            else stack.push({ v: d.value, path: p, level: depth, parent: c, key: k });
          }
        }
        break;
      }
      default:
        report(t.path, 'NOT_JSON', `expected a JSON value, got ${typeof x}`);
        continue;
    }
    if (text > L.textUnits) break;
    // Keys are written in the order they are visited (sorted), and only once they matched the pattern.
    if (t.parent === null) result = clone;
    else if (Array.isArray(t.parent)) t.parent[t.key as number] = clone;
    else t.parent[t.key as string] = clone;
  }
  if (stop === null && text > L.textUnits) {
    stop = { path: fullPath(path, top), code: 'JSON_TOO_LARGE', message: `canonical text longer than ${L.textUnits} characters` };
  }
  if (stop !== null) { out.push(stop); return undefined; }
  if (issues.length > 0) {
    out.push(...issues);
    if (more > 0) out.push({ path, code: 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES', message: `${more} more` });
    return undefined;
  }
  for (const c of containers) Object.freeze(c);
  if (typeof result === 'object' && result !== null) {
    // The running count is exact; the canonical text of the clone confirms it, and is cached for canonicalJSON.
    const canonical = canonicalJSON(result);
    if (canonical.length > L.textUnits) {
      out.push({ path: fullPath(path, top), code: 'JSON_TOO_LARGE', message: `canonical text longer than ${L.textUnits} characters` });
      return undefined;
    }
    REGISTRY.add(result);
    rememberCanonical(result, canonical, height);
  }
  return result as JsonValue;
}

/**
 * The nodes of a tier-1-valid tree value (the README's `<format> tree, <n> nodes`): the plain objects that carry the
 * format's discriminator (`op` / `kind`) as a string.
 */
export function countTreeNodes(v: unknown, format: JsonFormat): number {
  const tag = format === 'density' ? 'op' : 'kind';
  let n = 0;
  const stack: unknown[] = [v];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const x = stack.pop();
    if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null) continue;
    if (Array.isArray(x)) { for (const item of x) stack.push(item); continue; }
    const rec = x as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (Object.hasOwn(rec, tag) && typeof rec[tag] === 'string') n++;
    for (const k of Object.keys(rec)) stack.push(rec[k]);
  }
  return n;
}
```

- Ruling: the two whole-value bounds (`JSON_TOO_MANY_VALUES`, `JSON_TOO_LARGE`) stop the walk and *replace* any issues collected so far by that single issue, at the value's node path (density: the leaf path; rules: `<leaf>.root`); the per-value bounds (`JSON_TOO_DEEP`, `ARRAY_TOO_LONG`, `STRING_TOO_LONG`) are reported at the offending value, which is not entered, and the walk goes on (so a 100,000-deep chain gives one `JSON_TOO_DEEP`) — §1.7's "stops at the first exceeded size bound with that single issue" read for the global bounds — cost if wrong: issue lists of oversized values change.
- Ruling: at each visit the value count is checked before the text; the text count is exact, not an estimate (brackets, commas, quoted keys and colons added at the container's visit; `String(v)` / `JSON.stringify(s)` for primitives); invalid primitives and rejected keys add 0; it is measured in UTF-16 code units (`canonicalJSON(...).length`), so "128 KiB" = 131,072 characters (core cannot use `TextEncoder`) — cost if wrong: a tree of non-ASCII strings may reach 3× the bytes (strings ≤ 256 units; tree strings are ASCII op names and paths).
- Ruling: rejected keys, array holes and accessor properties are queued as "bad" visits, so issues come out in DFS pre-order with sorted keys; they are not counted as values. Accessors (getters/setters, objects or arrays) are `NOT_JSON` and are never invoked (read by descriptor), so a getter cannot run or throw inside tier 1 — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: path syntax — object keys joined with `.`, array items `[i]` without a dot (`density.defs[0]`, `surface.rules.root.rules[0]`); `BAD_KEY` at `<parent>.` + `JSON.stringify(key)` cut to 40 characters, never between the halves of a surrogate pair (`density.defs.defs."__proto__"`); an empty leaf path (the editor) gives node paths alone; `TOO_MANY_ISSUES` at the leaf path itself (`surface.rules`, not `.root`) with the message `<N> more` — cost if wrong: test strings.
- Ruling: the text cache lives in `canonical.ts` (a `WeakMap` of text + nesting height, filled only by `checkJson` through `rememberCanonical` for the clones it registers in its `WeakSet`); `canonicalJSON` uses an entry only when `depth + height ≤ 64`, else it walks the value and throws exactly as uncached (same path and message); `canonicalCacheHits()` is the tests' counter. `checkJson` computes `canonicalJSON(clone)` once (the §1.7 confirmation) and caches that text — cost if wrong: one extra canonical print per new tree.
- Ruling: `diffParams` short-circuits `b === x` for every leaf (atomic and fields), not only json leaves: the same object is canonically equal — cost if wrong: none (results unchanged).
- Ruling: `renderReference`'s `<n> nodes` = `countTreeNodes`: plain objects carrying the format's discriminator as a string (`op` for density, `kind` for rules; rule and condition nodes both count) — cost if wrong: README wording (Task 14 runs `docs:params`).

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { canonicalJSON } from '../../src/core/params/canonical';
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import { checkJson, countTreeNodes, type JsonFormat, type JsonValue } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import type { Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import type { DensityParams, SurfaceParams } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { legacyDefaultDensityExpr, legacyDefaultSurfaceRules } from '../harness/legacyTrees';

const FIXTURE = new URL('../fixtures/sp3c-default-rules.json', import.meta.url);
const fixture = (): unknown => JSON.parse(readFileSync(FIXTURE, 'utf8')) as unknown;

type Rec = Record<string, unknown>;
const isRec = (v: unknown): v is Rec => typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v);

/** Every container (object or array) of a value, the value included. */
function containers(v: unknown): object[] {
  const out: object[] = [];
  const stack: unknown[] = [v];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const x = stack.pop();
    if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null) continue;
    out.push(x);
    for (const c of Array.isArray(x) ? x : Object.values(x)) stack.push(c);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The first path where two trees differ (numbers compared with Object.is, so −0 ≠ +0; key order ignored), or null. */
function treeDiff(a: unknown, b: unknown, path = ''): string | null {
  if (typeof a === 'number' || typeof b === 'number') return Object.is(a, b) ? null : `${path}: ${String(a)} vs ${String(b)}`;
  if (Array.isArray(a) || Array.isArray(b)) {
    if (!Array.isArray(a) || !Array.isArray(b) || a.length !== b.length) return `${path}: array shape`;
    for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) {
      const d = treeDiff(a[i], b[i], `${path}[${i}]`);
      if (d !== null) return d;
    }
    return null;
  }
  if (isRec(a) && isRec(b)) {
    const ka = Object.keys(a).sort();
    const kb = Object.keys(b).sort();
    if (ka.join() !== kb.join()) return `${path}: keys ${ka.join()} vs ${kb.join()}`;
    for (const k of ka) {
      const d = treeDiff(a[k], b[k], path === '' ? k : `${path}.${k}`);
      if (d !== null) return d;
    }
    return null;
  }
  return a === b ? null : `${path}: ${String(a)} vs ${String(b)}`;
}

/**
 * The default density tree with §2.1's three substitutions undone, as the legacy builder computes them:
 * `recip(param jag.clampSigma)` → const(1 / cs), `add(param hi, neg(param lo))` → const(hi − lo), `param lo` → const(lo).
 * Any other `param` or `recip` is an error. Returns the tree and the number of substitutions undone.
 */
function densityUndone(tree: unknown, p: DensityParams): { tree: unknown; undone: number } {
  let undone = 0;
  const isParam = (v: unknown, path: string): boolean => isRec(v) && v['op'] === 'param' && v['path'] === path;
  const walk = (v: unknown): unknown => {
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map(walk);
    if (!isRec(v)) return v;
    if (v['op'] === 'recip' && isParam(v['x'], 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma')) {
      undone++;
      return { op: 'const', v: 1 / p.noises.jag.clampSigma };
    }
    const b = v['b'];
    if (v['op'] === 'add' && isParam(v['a'], 'density.detailAmpHi') && isRec(b) && b['op'] === 'neg' && isParam(b['x'], 'density.detailAmpLo')) {
      undone++;
      return { op: 'const', v: p.detailAmpHi - p.detailAmpLo };
    }
    if (isParam(v, 'density.detailAmpLo')) {
      undone++;
      return { op: 'const', v: p.detailAmpLo };
    }
    if (v['op'] === 'param' || v['op'] === 'recip') throw new Error(`unexpected ${String(v['op'])} node`);
    const o: Rec = {};
    for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(v)) o[k] = walk(x);
    return o;
  };
  return { tree: walk(tree), undone };
}

/** The four surface parameters a default-rules ref may name (§2.2), read from `p`. */
const surfaceTargets = (p: SurfaceParams): ReadonlyMap<string, number> => new Map([
  ['surface.patchThreshold', p.patchThreshold],
  ['surface.cliffSteep', p.cliffSteep],
  ['surface.cliffMinY', p.cliffMinY],
  ['surface.snowline', p.snowline],
]);

/** The default rules with each `{param, neg?}` ref replaced by its value (`0 − v` when negated); the refs it met. */
function surfaceAt(tree: unknown, p: SurfaceParams): { tree: unknown; refs: string[] } {
  const targets = surfaceTargets(p);
  const refs: string[] = [];
  const walk = (v: unknown, path: string): unknown => {
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map((x, i) => walk(x, `${path}[${i}]`));
    if (!isRec(v)) return v;
    if (Object.hasOwn(v, 'param')) {
      const name = v['param'] as string;
      const t = targets.get(name);
      if (t === undefined) throw new Error(`unknown ref ${name} at ${path}`);
      const neg = v['neg'] === true;
      refs.push(`${path} ${neg ? '-' : ''}${name}`);
      return neg ? 0 - t : t;
    }
    const o: Rec = {};
    for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(v)) o[k] = walk(x, `${path}.${k}`);
    return o;
  };
  return { tree: walk(tree, 'root'), refs };
}

const withDensity = (patch: Partial<DensityParams>, clampSigma?: number): DensityParams => {
  const d = DEFAULTS.density;
  const noises = clampSigma === undefined ? d.noises : { ...d.noises, jag: { ...d.noises.jag, clampSigma } };
  return { ...d, ...patch, noises };
};
const withSurface = (patch: Partial<SurfaceParams>): SurfaceParams => ({ ...DEFAULTS.surface, ...patch });

const CASES: ReadonlyArray<[string, JsonValue, string, JsonFormat]> = [
  ['DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE', DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density.defs', 'density'],
  ['DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES', DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surface.rules', 'surfaceRules'],
];

describe('the default trees as data (SP3d spec §2)', () => {
  test.each(CASES)('%s is tier 1\'s registered clone: checkJson returns it as itself, with no issue', (_, tree, path, format) => {
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkJson(tree, path, out, format)).toBe(tree);
    expect(out).toEqual([]);
  });

  test.each(CASES)('%s passes tier 1 when checked afresh (a plain copy gives no issue and the same canonical text)', (_, tree, path, format) => {
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(tree)) as unknown;
    const again = checkJson(copy, path, out, format);
    expect(out).toEqual([]);
    expect(again).toBeDefined();
    expect(again).not.toBe(copy);
    expect(canonicalJSON(again)).toBe(canonicalJSON(tree));
  });

  test.each(CASES)('%s is frozen at every depth and stores its object keys sorted', (_, tree) => {
    const all = containers(tree);
    expect(all.length).toBeGreaterThan(50);
    for (const c of all) {
      expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
      if (!Array.isArray(c)) expect(Object.keys(c)).toEqual(Object.keys(c).sort());
    }
    expect(() => { (tree as Rec)['x'] = 1; }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE is the whole expression {root, defs} with no defs', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE)).toEqual(['defs', 'root']);
    expect((DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE as Rec)['defs']).toEqual({});
  });

  test('DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE with its three substitutions undone equals legacyDefaultDensityExpr at DEFAULTS (Object.is on every number)', () => {
    const { tree, undone } = densityUndone(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULTS.density);
    expect(undone).toBe(3);
    expect(treeDiff(tree, legacyDefaultDensityExpr(DEFAULTS.density))).toBeNull();
  });

  test.each([1, 3, 7.3, 8])('… and at density.noises.jag.clampSigma %s', (cs) => {
    const p = withDensity({}, cs);
    expect(treeDiff(densityUndone(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, p).tree, legacyDefaultDensityExpr(p))).toBeNull();
  });

  test.each([[0, 0], [0, 8], [8, 0], [0.35, 1.05]])('… and at detailAmpLo %s, detailAmpHi %s', (lo, hi) => {
    const p = withDensity({ detailAmpLo: lo, detailAmpHi: hi });
    expect(treeDiff(densityUndone(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, p).tree, legacyDefaultDensityExpr(p))).toBeNull();
  });

  test('DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE has 4 nodes more than the legacy tree (recip + param for one const; add, param, neg, param for one)', () => {
    // Nodes as the README counts them (every occurrence; the legacy builder's three `y` are one shared object).
    const legacy = legacyDefaultDensityExpr(DEFAULTS.density);
    expect(countTreeNodes(legacy as unknown as JsonValue, 'density')).toBe(56);
    expect(countTreeNodes(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density')).toBe(60);
  });

  test('DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES holds exactly §2.2\'s 15 refs', () => {
    const { refs } = surfaceAt(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, DEFAULTS.surface);
    const by = (name: string): number => refs.filter((r) => r.endsWith(` ${name}`)).length;
    expect(refs.length).toBe(15);
    expect(by('surface.patchThreshold')).toBe(10);
    expect(by('-surface.patchThreshold')).toBe(2);
    expect(by('surface.cliffSteep')).toBe(1);
    expect(by('surface.cliffMinY')).toBe(1);
    expect(by('surface.snowline')).toBe(1);
    // Every ref sits in the field the builder writes the parameter to (P.min, Pn.max, steep.min, yAbove.minY, temperatureBelow.t).
    for (const r of refs) expect(r).toMatch(/\.(?:if\.min |if\.max -|if\.minY |if\.t )surface\./);
  });

  test('DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES with its refs substituted at DEFAULTS canonicalises to test/fixtures/sp3c-default-rules.json', () => {
    expect(canonicalJSON(surfaceAt(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, DEFAULTS.surface).tree)).toBe(canonicalJSON(fixture()));
  });

  test.each([
    ['patchThreshold 0 (+0 in Pn.max)', { patchThreshold: 0 }],
    ['patchThreshold 3', { patchThreshold: 3 }],
    ['cliffSteep 0, cliffMinY −64, snowline −1', { cliffSteep: 0, cliffMinY: -64, snowline: -1 }],
    ['cliffSteep 8, cliffMinY 319, snowline 1', { cliffSteep: 8, cliffMinY: 319, snowline: 1 }],
  ] as const)('… and equals legacyDefaultSurfaceRules at %s', (_, patch) => {
    const p = withSurface(patch);
    expect(canonicalJSON(surfaceAt(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, p).tree)).toBe(canonicalJSON(legacyDefaultSurfaceRules(p)));
  });

  test('DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES has as many rule and condition nodes as the fixture (refs are not nodes)', () => {
    expect(countTreeNodes(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules')).toBe(countTreeNodes(fixture() as JsonValue, 'surfaceRules'));
    expect(countTreeNodes(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules')).toBe(163);
  });
});
```
