        }
      }
    }
    for (const bad of BAD) {
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivClamp(0, 1, bad, 1, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivClamp(0, 1, 0, bad, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivNoise(bad, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    }
    const out = new Float64Array(2);
    ivUnknown(out, 0);
    expect([...out]).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
  });

  test('UNKNOWN propagates: max and min do not keep a known side, clamp and rangeChoice never make it known', () => {
    // SP3b's max([−∞, ∞], [1, 1]) was [1, ∞]: the measured unsound early-out (map-density.md §2).
    expect(BINARY['max']!(-Infinity, Infinity, 1, 1)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(BINARY['min']!(-1, 1, -Infinity, Infinity)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(UNARY['clamp']!(-Infinity, Infinity)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(UNARY['abs']!(-Infinity, Infinity)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(UNARY['square']!(NaN, NaN)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    const rc = (x0: number, x1: number, i0: number, i1: number, o0: number, o1: number): [number, number] =>
      iv((o, k) => ivRangeChoice(x0, x1, 0, 10, i0, i1, o0, o1, o, k));
    expect(rc(-Infinity, Infinity, 1, 1, 2, 2)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(rc(NaN, NaN, 1, 1, 2, 2)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    // An UNKNOWN branch is UNKNOWN even when x decides the other one.
    expect(rc(1, 2, 1, 1, -Infinity, Infinity)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    expect(rc(20, 30, NaN, NaN, 2, 2)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
    // Known inputs: SP3b's choice.
    expect(rc(1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2)).toEqual([1, 1]);
    expect(rc(20, 30, 1, 1, 2, 2)).toEqual([2, 2]);
    expect(rc(5, 30, 1, 1, 2, 3)).toEqual([1, 3]);
    expect(rc(-0, 9, -0, 0, 5, 5)).toEqual([-0, 0]);
  });

  test('a NaN result endpoint is UNKNOWN: slide factors with an overflowing segment (0 · ∞ at a knot)', () => {
    const cases: Array<readonly SlideKnot[]> = [
      [[0, -1e308], [1, 1e308]],
      [[0, 0], [5e-324, 1], [10, 1]],
    ];
    for (const knots of cases) {
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivSlideFactor(knots, 0, 8, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivSlide(1, 2, knots, 0, 8, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
      // Away from the segment the factor is known.
      expect(iv((o, k) => ivSlideFactor(knots, 16, 24, o, k))).toEqual([knots[knots.length - 1]![1], knots[knots.length - 1]![1]]);
    }
    // A finite segment that only reaches its overflowing slope at an interior knot (the left formula is ±∞).
    expect(iv((o, k) => ivSlideFactor([[-100, 0], [4, -1e308], [5, 1e308]], 0, 8, o, k))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
  });

  test('finite inputs give SP3b\'s intervals exactly (±0 included); an overflow keeps its ±∞ end and poisons the parent', () => {
    const next = testRng(707);
    for (let n = 0; n < 3000; n++) {
      const A = randIv(next), B = randIv(next);
      for (const [name, f] of Object.entries(BINARY)) {
        const got = f(A[0], A[1], B[0], B[1]), want = OLD_BINARY[name]!(A[0], A[1], B[0], B[1]);
        if (!same(got, want)) throw new Error(`${name}([${A}], [${B}]) = [${got}], SP3b [${want}]`);
      }
      for (const [name, f] of Object.entries(UNARY)) {
        const got = f(A[0], A[1]), want = OLD_UNARY[name]!(A[0], A[1]);
        if (!same(got, want)) throw new Error(`${name}([${A}]) = [${got}], SP3b [${want}]`);
      }
      const lo = Math.min(B[0], -B[0]), hi = -lo;
      const rcGot = iv((o, k) => ivRangeChoice(A[0], A[1], lo, hi === lo ? hi + 1 : hi, 1, 2, -3, -1, o, k));
      const which = rangeChoiceCase(A[0], A[1], lo, hi === lo ? hi + 1 : hi);
      expect(rcGot).toEqual(which === 'inside' ? [1, 2] : which === 'outside' ? [-3, -1] : [-3, 2]);
    }
    expect(BINARY['mul']!(1e200, 1e200, 1e200, 1e200)).toEqual([Infinity, Infinity]);
    expect(BINARY['add']!(-1e308, 1, -1e308, 1)).toEqual([-Infinity, 2]);
    expect(UNARY['neg']!(...BINARY['mul']!(1e200, 1e200, 1e200, 1e200))).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
  });
});

// ---- bounds.ts: the hulls test every folded value for NaN and the finished hull for finiteness ----

const C = (v: number): Expr => ({ op: 'const', v });
const Y: Expr = { op: 'y' };
const col = (field: 'offset' | 'E'): Expr => ({ op: 'col', field });
const add = (a: Expr, b: Expr): Expr => ({ op: 'add', a, b });
const mul = (a: Expr, b: Expr): Expr => ({ op: 'mul', a, b });
const neg = (x: Expr): Expr => ({ op: 'neg', x });
const interp = (x: Expr): Expr => ({ op: 'interpolated', x });
const only = (root: Expr, defs: Record<string, Expr> = {}): DensityExpr => ({ root, defs });
const none: DensityNoiseSource = () => undefined;

/** A hand-built ColumnSample at column (2, −3): offset i·j + 0.5 and E i + 10·j on the lattice, every other field 0. */
function handSample(): ColumnSample {
  const s = newColumnSample();
  s.cx = 2;
  s.cz = -3;
  for (let j = -1; j <= 5; j++) {
    for (let i = -1; i <= 5; i++) {
      s.f.offset[latticeIndex(i, j)] = i * j + 0.5;
      s.f.E[latticeIndex(i, j)] = i + 10 * j;
    }
  }
  return s;
}

const vIdx = (lx: number, y: number, lz: number): number => (((y + 64) << 4) | lz) << 4 | lx;
const rootIv = (b: DensityBounds, ci: number, ck: number, cj: number): [number, number] => {
  const out = new Float64Array(2);
  b.cellInterval(ci, ck, cj, out, 0);
  return [out[0]!, out[1]!];
};
const slotOf = (c: CompiledDensity, key: 'colSlot' | 'posSlot' | 'interpSlot'): number => {
  const n = c.nodes.find((d) => d[key] >= 0);
  if (n === undefined) throw new Error(`no ${key}`);
  return n[key];
};

describe('bounds: NaN and ±∞ slot and corner values never decide a cell (SP3d spec §1.9 D)', () => {
  test('a position hull: a NaN or ±∞ at any of the 16 positions makes the root UNKNOWN; finite hulls are unchanged', () => {
    const c = compileDensity(only(add(mul(col('E'), C(0.5)), Y)), none);
    const b = createDensityBounds(c, none);
    const s = handSample();
    c.columnFn(s);
    c.positionFn(s);
    b.beginColumn();
    const clean = rootIv(b, 1, 20, 2), other = rootIv(b, 3, 20, 0);
    expect(clean.every(Number.isFinite)).toBe(true);
    const slot = slotOf(c, 'posSlot');
    for (const bad of BAD) {
      for (let q = 0; q < 16; q++) {
        const lx = 4 + (q & 3), lz = 8 + (q >> 2);
        c.positionFn(s);
        c.posValues[posValueIndex(slot, lx, lz)] = bad;
        b.beginColumn();
        if (!same(rootIv(b, 1, 20, 2), UNKNOWN)) throw new Error(`position (${lx}, ${lz}) = ${bad}: [${String(rootIv(b, 1, 20, 2))}]`);
        // Another cell's hull is untouched.
        expect(rootIv(b, 3, 20, 0)).toEqual(other);
      }
    }
    c.positionFn(s);
    b.beginColumn();
    expect(rootIv(b, 1, 20, 2)).toEqual(clean);
  });

  test('a column hull: a NaN or ±∞ at any of the cell\'s 4 corner columns makes the root UNKNOWN', () => {
    const c = compileDensity(only(interp(add(col('offset'), neg(Y)))), none);
    const b = createDensityBounds(c, none);
    const s = handSample();
    const slot = slotOf(c, 'colSlot');
    for (const bad of BAD) {
      for (const [i, j] of [[1, 2], [2, 2], [1, 3], [2, 3]] as const) {
        c.columnFn(s);
        c.positionFn(s);
        c.colValues[colValueIndex(slot, i, j)] = bad;
        b.beginColumn();
        expect(rootIv(b, 1, 10, 2)).toEqual(UNKNOWN);
        expect(rootIv(b, 3, 10, 0).every(Number.isFinite)).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  test('a corner hull: a NaN or ±∞ at any of the cell\'s 8 corners makes the refined root UNKNOWN', () => {
    const s = handSample();
    const slot = slotOf(compileDensity(only(interp(add(col('offset'), neg(Y)))), none), 'interpSlot');
    const out = new Float64Array(2);
    for (const bad of BAD) {
      for (let q = 0; q < 8; q++) {
        const i = 1 + (q & 1), j = 2 + ((q >> 1) & 1), k = 10 + (q >> 2);
        const fresh = compileDensity(only(interp(add(col('offset'), neg(Y)))), none);
        const fb = createDensityBounds(fresh, none);
        fresh.columnFn(s);
        fresh.positionFn(s);
        fb.beginColumn();
        fb.cellInterval(1, 10, 2, out, 0);
        fresh.cellCorners(1, 10, 2);
        fb.cellIntervalCorners(1, 10, 2, out, 0);
        expect([out[0], out[1]].every(Number.isFinite)).toBe(true);
        fresh.cornerValues[cornerValueIndex(slot, i, k, j)] = bad;
        fb.cellIntervalCorners(1, 10, 2, out, 0);
        if (!same([out[0]!, out[1]!], UNKNOWN)) throw new Error(`corner (${i}, ${k}, ${j}) = ${bad}: [${out[0]}, ${out[1]}]`);
      }
    }
  });

  /** The driver's solidity against a full evaluation of an independent compile; returns the evaluated voxel count. */
  function driverEqualsFull(e: DensityExpr, s: ColumnSample, noises: DensityNoiseSource): number {
    const b = createDensityBounds(compileDensity(e, noises), noises);
    const full = compileDensity(e, noises);
    full.columnFn(s);
    full.positionFn(s);
    const solid = new Uint8Array(98304), mask = new Uint8Array(98304);
    expect(fillDensityColumn(b, s, solid, null, mask, () => false)).toBe(true);
    let masked = 0;
    for (let y = -64; y < 320; y++) {
      for (let lz = 0; lz < 16; lz++) {
        for (let lx = 0; lx < 16; lx++) {
          const i = vIdx(lx, y, lz);
          const v = full.voxelFn(lx, y, lz);
          if (solid[i] !== (v > 0 ? 1 : 0)) throw new Error(`voxel (${lx}, ${y}, ${lz}) solid ${solid[i]} but full value ${v}`);
          masked += mask[i]!;
        }
      }
    }
    return masked;
  }

  test('a NaN or ±∞ ColumnSample value: the early-out driver equals full evaluation at every voxel', () => {
    for (const bad of BAD) {
      for (const at of [[2, 2], [0, 0], [4, 4]] as const) {
        const s = handSample();
        s.f.offset[latticeIndex(at[0], at[1])] = bad;
        // A voxel-level read (position hull) and a corner read inside interpolated (column hull), both ≫ 0 elsewhere.
        expect(driverEqualsFull(only(add(col('offset'), C(100))), s, none)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        expect(driverEqualsFull(only(interp(add(col('offset'), C(100)))), s, none)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    }
    // Finite values: every cell early-outs solid.
    expect(driverEqualsFull(only(add(col('offset'), C(100))), handSample(), none)).toBe(0);
    expect(driverEqualsFull(only(interp(add(col('offset'), C(100)))), handSample(), none)).toBe(0);
  });

  test('the measured unsound tree max(add(Z, neg(Z)), 1), Z = mul(mul(noise, 1e308), 1e308): voxels evaluated, equal to the probe', () => {
    const tree: DensityExpr = {
      root: { op: 'max', a: add({ op: 'ref', name: 'Z' }, neg({ op: 'ref', name: 'Z' })), b: C(1) },
      defs: { Z: mul(mul({ op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, C(1e308)), C(1e308)) },
    };
    const dc = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'), tree);
    const solid = new Uint8Array(98304), values = new Float64Array(98304), mask = new Uint8Array(98304);
    for (const [cx, cz] of [[0, 0], [-5, 7]] as const) {
      expect(fillDensityColumn(dc.bounds, dc.columns.get(cx, cz), solid, values, mask, () => false)).toBe(true);
      let masked = 0, mismatches = 0, nan = 0;
      for (let y = -64; y < 320; y++) {
        for (let lz = 0; lz < 16; lz++) {
          for (let lx = 0; lx < 16; lx++) {
            const i = vIdx(lx, y, lz);
            masked += mask[i]!;
            const p = probe(dc, 16 * cx + lx, y, 16 * cz + lz);
            if (Number.isNaN(p)) nan++;
            if (solid[i] !== (p > 0 ? 1 : 0)) mismatches++;
            if (mask[i] === 1 && !Object.is(values[i], p)) mismatches++;
          }
        }
      }
      expect(mismatches).toBe(0);
      // The root interval is UNKNOWN in every cell: SP3b's [1, ∞] marked every cell solid without evaluating it.
      expect(masked).toBe(98304);
      expect(nan).toBeGreaterThan(98000);
    }
  });

  test('a constant-valued noise: every voxel is NaN and air, with no early-out', () => {
    const flat: DensityNoise = { dims: 3, remap: 'none', clampSigma: 4, z2: () => 0, z3: () => 1 };
    const noises: DensityNoiseSource = (id) => (id === 'n' ? flat : undefined);
    const tree: DensityExpr = {
      root: { op: 'max', a: add({ op: 'ref', name: 'Z' }, neg({ op: 'ref', name: 'Z' })), b: C(1) },
      defs: { Z: mul(mul({ op: 'noise', id: 'n' }, C(1e308)), C(1e308)) },
    };
    expect(driverEqualsFull(tree, handSample(), noises)).toBe(98304);
  });
});

describe('the default world is unchanged (SP3d spec §1.9 D: proven, not only claimed)', () => {
  test('fillDensityColumn\'s mask and solid arrays over 32 seed-\'42\' columns hash as at main (9fababa)', () => {
    // Computed with main's code (2ffec6a = 9fababa's code) in a detached worktree, by this same loop.
    const dc = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'));
    const solid = new Uint8Array(98304), mask = new Uint8Array(98304);
    const h = createFnv64();
    let masked = 0, solids = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
      const cx = ((i * 7919) % 513) - 256, cz = ((i * 104729) % 513) - 256;
      expect(fillDensityColumn(dc.bounds, dc.columns.get(cx, cz), solid, null, mask, () => false)).toBe(true);
      h.update(mask).update(solid);
      for (let k = 0; k < 98304; k++) { masked += mask[k]!; solids += solid[k]!; }
    }
    expect(`${hex64(h.digest())} ${masked} ${solids}`).toBe('1e25082c8ed7a949 167808 1040924');
  });
});
```

- Ruling: the poison rule is strict as §1.9 words it: an op with **any** non-finite input endpoint (NaN, ±∞, so UNKNOWN too) is UNKNOWN — `ivMin`/`ivMax` do not keep the known side, `ivRangeChoice` is UNKNOWN when the branch x does not take is UNKNOWN, `ivSet` (const, y, tap pass-through) and `ivWiden` too; a finite input may give an infinite result endpoint (an overflow, never NaN for these ops), which is kept (it holds every value) and makes the parent UNKNOWN. `ivSlideFactor` is UNKNOWN when any probed value (s(y0), s(y1), an interior knot's v or left formula) is non-finite, not only NaN: an overflowing segment is NaN at its lower knot (0 · ∞), which the probes may not include — cost if wrong: none on finite worlds (mask hash and compared set equal).
- Ruling: hulls — `colHull` and the `interpolated` corner hull keep their first-value seed, `posHull` its ±Infinity seed; each folded value is tested with `Number.isNaN` and the finished [lo, hi] with `Number.isFinite`; any failure gives UNKNOWN (the position hull is then not widened). For finite values every hull is bit-identical to SP3b's (the first value wins ties, ±0 included) — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: `VALUE_RANGE` is **one** issue for the whole source, at the first node in **post-order** (children before parents, `a` before `b`, slot order) over `root`, then each def in `Object.keys` order (reachable or not; a def's nodes are reported at `defs.<name>…`); a `ref` whose def leaves ±1e100 is itself such a node (reported at the ref in the root, before the def's own node). Post-order is §1.7's "first node … in source DFS order" read so that the node named is the one whose own op leaves the range (pre-order would always name the root) — cost if wrong: test strings and the inspector's issue → node mapping.
- Ruling: static inputs — `y` [cornerY(0), cornerY(48)] = [−64, 320]; `noise`/`noise2` ±`NOISE_FIELD_RANGES.clampSigma.max` (8) whatever the configured clampSigma; `col` its `COL_FIELD_BOUNDS` entry (a Map from `Object.entries`); `const` [v, v]; `param` and ref fields their `ALLOWED_REF_TARGETS` range (negated: [0 − hi, 0 − lo]); `recip` [1/x1, 1/x0] of its operand's interval (UNKNOWN if it contains 0); `clamp` with range bounds = hull(ivClamp(x, l0, h0), ivClamp(x, l1, h1)) (exact: clamp is nondecreasing in x, lo, hi while CLAMP_ORDER holds over the ranges); `rangeChoice` inside when `rangeChoiceCase(x, max lo, min hi)` is inside, outside when `rangeChoiceCase(x, min lo, max hi)` is outside, else the hull (UNKNOWN x → UNKNOWN); `slide` = x × ivWiden(hull of every knot's v range) (s(y) lies between two consecutive knot values up to rounding; the widening covers the rounding; tighter `ivSlideFactor` is not used because knots may be refs); `interpolated` ivWiden(child); a muted tap ivHull(mute range, child), an unmuted one its child; `ref` its def's interval (defs in topological order of the def graph, each once). The limit 1e100 is module-private (`VALUE_LIMIT`) — cost if wrong: looser intervals refuse a few more extreme trees.
- Ruling: Task 6's `defHeights` now takes the topological order from a new private `defOrder` (the same iterative post-order DFS, extracted), shared with the analysis; heights unchanged (Task 6's tests pass) — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: the skeleton's "a `col` read of an unbounded field" case has no instance: Task 4 bounded all 19 fields. It is pinned instead as "every col field reads its `COL_FIELD_BOUNDS` entry": for each `SAMPLE_FIELDS` f with M = max(|lo|, |hi|) > 0, `col f × (9.9/M) × 1e9^11` passes and `× (10.1/M) × …` is refused; `islandMask` [0, 0] never leaves — cost if wrong: none (a field later given [−∞, ∞] would be refused wherever read, by the same code path).
- Ruling: the mask hash pins `fillDensityColumn` (default tree of `createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'))`, no `values`) over 32 columns cx = (i·7919 mod 513) − 256, cz = (i·104729 mod 513) − 256, i = 0 … 31, streaming `mask` then `solid` of each column into `createFnv64`: `1e25082c8ed7a949`, 167,808 masked voxels, 1,040,924 solid voxels — computed by the same loop in a temporary test file in `P/base` (detached at `main` = `main`'s code; the file was deleted, `P/base` clean). This one test passes on the parent by design (D changes nothing on finite worlds); its file fails there (10 other tests) — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: the measured unsound tree is pinned twice: through `createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'), tree)` with the real `detail` noise (Z a def, root `max(add(ref Z, neg(ref Z)), const 1)`): at columns (0, 0) and (−5, 7) every one of the 98,304 voxels is evaluated (mask), its solidity and value equal `probe` (`Object.is` on values), > 98,000 of them NaN; and with an injected constant 3D noise (z3 = 1) through the driver-vs-full comparison. ```ts
/**
 * Resolution and freezing of density source trees (SP3d spec §1.5, §1.6, §2.1, §3.4; D6, D10): `resolveDensity`
 * (substitution, `recip`, mutes, constant folding, paths preserved, −0 kept, a fresh frozen output, tier 2 first),
 * `resolveDensityNode` (the inspector's selected-node expression), `freezeTree` and the DensityContext's frozen tree,
 * and §2.1's bit-identity of the resolved default with the legacy builder.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import { checkJson, type JsonValue } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import type { Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { SCHEMA, type Params, type ParamsPatch } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { createDensityContext, type DensityContext } from '../../src/gen/density/context';
import { cornerValueIndex } from '../../src/gen/density/compile';
import { exprHash, ExprValidationError, type DensityExpr, type Expr } from '../../src/gen/density/expr';
import { createDensityReference, findTap } from '../../src/gen/density/reference';
import {
  densitySourceValidations, freezeTree, resolveDensity, resolveDensityNode, type DensitySource,
} from '../../src/gen/density/source';
import { ctxFor, paramsWith } from '../harness/gen';
import { legacyDefaultDensityExpr } from '../harness/legacyTrees';
import { randomValue } from '../harness/params';
import { testRng } from '../harness/stats';

const P = paramsWith();
const COLUMNS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [[0, 0], [5, -7], [-68, 100]];

/** −0-aware deep equality: the same keys (any order), arrays of the same length, numbers by `Object.is`. */
function sameTree(a: unknown, b: unknown, path = ''): string | null {
  if (typeof a === 'number' || typeof b === 'number') return Object.is(a, b) ? null : `${path}: ${String(a)} vs ${String(b)}`;
  if (typeof a !== 'object' || a === null || typeof b !== 'object' || b === null) return a === b ? null : `${path}: ${String(a)} vs ${String(b)}`;
  if (Array.isArray(a) !== Array.isArray(b)) return `${path}: array vs object`;
  const ka = Object.keys(a).sort(), kb = Object.keys(b).sort();
  if (ka.join(',') !== kb.join(',')) return `${path}: keys ${ka.join(',')} vs ${kb.join(',')}`;
  for (const k of ka) {
    const d = sameTree((a as Record<string, unknown>)[k], (b as Record<string, unknown>)[k], `${path}.${k}`);
    if (d !== null) return d;
  }
  return null;
}

/** Every container of `v` is frozen. */
function frozenEverywhere(v: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof v !== 'object' || v === null) return true;
  if (!Object.isFrozen(v)) return false;
  return Object.values(v).every(frozenEverywhere);
}

const C = (v: number) => ({ op: 'const', v });
const Y = { op: 'y' };
const src = (root: unknown, defs: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DensitySource => ({ root, defs }) as unknown as DensitySource;
const rootOf = (e: DensityExpr): Record<string, unknown> => e.root as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
const codes = (f: () => unknown): string[] => {
  try { f(); } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof ExprValidationError) return e.issues.map((i) => `${i.path}: ${i.code}`);
    throw e;
  }
  return [];
};

describe('resolveDensity (§1.6)', () => {
  test('param nodes and ref-valued fields become numbers (0 − v for neg, never −0)', () => {
    const p = paramsWith({ density: { detailAmpLo: 0, detailAmpHi: 2.5, noises: { jag: { clampSigma: 7.3 } } }, surface: { snowline: 0.5, cliffMinY: 140 } });
    const e = resolveDensity(src({
      op: 'add',
      a: { op: 'clamp', x: Y, lo: { param: 'density.detailAmpLo', neg: true }, hi: { param: 'density.detailAmpHi' } },
      b: { op: 'add',
        a: { op: 'slide', x: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, knots: [[{ param: 'density.detailAmpHi', neg: true }, { param: 'surface.snowline' }], [10, { param: 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma' }]] },
        b: { op: 'tap', name: 't', x: Y, mute: { param: 'surface.cliffMinY', neg: true } } },
    }), p);
    const r = rootOf(e);
    const clamp = r['a'] as { lo: number; hi: number };
    expect(Object.is(clamp.lo, 0)).toBe(true); // 0 − 0 = +0
    expect(clamp.hi).toBe(2.5);
    const slide = (r['b'] as Record<string, unknown>)['a'] as { knots: number[][] };
    expect(slide.knots).toEqual([[-2.5, 0.5], [10, 7.3]]);
    expect((r['b'] as Record<string, unknown>)['b']).toEqual({ op: 'tap', name: 't', x: { op: 'const', v: -140 } });

    const q = resolveDensity(src({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'param', path: 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma' }, b: Y }), p);
    expect(rootOf(q)).toEqual({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'const', v: 7.3 }, b: { op: 'y' } });
  });

  test('recip becomes const(1 / c), the same double the builder computes', () => {
    for (const cs of [1, 3, 7.3, 8, 2.9]) {
      const p = paramsWith({ density: { noises: { jag: { clampSigma: cs } } } });
      const v = p.density.noises.jag.clampSigma;
      const e = resolveDensity(src({ op: 'mul', a: { op: 'noise2', id: 'jag' }, b: { op: 'recip', x: { op: 'param', path: 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma' } } }), p);
      expect(Object.is((rootOf(e)['b'] as { v: number }).v, 1 / v)).toBe(true);
    }
    const k = resolveDensity(src({ op: 'mul', a: Y, b: { op: 'recip', x: C(-3) } }), P);
    expect(rootOf(k)['b']).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: 1 / -3 });
  });

  test('a muted tap keeps the tap and yields its mute; the subtree below leaves the resolved tree', () => {
    const e = resolveDensity(src({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'tap', name: 'm', mute: -1e6, x: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'inner', x: Y } } }, b: Y }), P);
    expect(rootOf(e)['a']).toEqual({ op: 'tap', name: 'm', x: { op: 'const', v: -1e6 } });
    expect(findTap(e, 'inner')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(findTap(e, 'm')).toBeDefined();
    // A mute of 0 under a muted tap stays +0; a tap of a const is never folded (`islands`).
    const z = resolveDensity(src({ op: 'max', a: { op: 'tap', name: 'z', mute: 0, x: Y }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'islands', x: C(-1e6) } }), P);
    expect(rootOf(z)).toEqual({ op: 'max', a: { op: 'tap', name: 'z', x: { op: 'const', v: 0 } }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'islands', x: { op: 'const', v: -1e6 } } });
  });

  test('constant folding with nodes.ts\'s value functions, bottom-up; −0 kept', () => {
    const fold = (root: unknown, p: Params = P): Record<string, unknown> => rootOf(resolveDensity(src(root), p));
    expect(fold({ op: 'add', a: C(0.1), b: C(0.2) })).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: 0.1 + 0.2 });
    expect(fold({ op: 'mul', a: C(3), b: { op: 'square', x: { op: 'abs', x: C(-2) } } })).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: 12 });
    expect(fold({ op: 'min', a: C(1), b: C(-1) })).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: -1 });
    expect(fold({ op: 'max', a: C(1), b: C(5) })).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: 5 });
    expect(fold({ op: 'clamp', x: C(7), lo: 0, hi: { param: 'density.detailAmpHi' } })).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: DEFAULTS.density.detailAmpHi });
    // min/max return a on ties (+0 against −0), as valMin / valMax.
    expect(Object.is((fold({ op: 'max', a: { op: 'neg', x: C(0) }, b: C(0) }) as { v: number }).v, -0)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.is((fold({ op: 'min', a: C(0), b: { op: 'neg', x: C(0) } }) as { v: number }).v, 0)).toBe(true);
    // neg(param p) with p = 0, and neg(const 0), fold to −0.
    const neg0 = fold({ op: 'neg', x: { op: 'param', path: 'density.detailAmpLo' } }, paramsWith({ density: { detailAmpLo: 0 } }));
    expect(Object.is(neg0['v'], -0)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.is((fold({ op: 'neg', x: C(0) }) as { v: number }).v, -0)).toBe(true);
    // ampHi − ampLo: add(param hi, neg(param lo)) → const(hi + (−lo)).
    const p = paramsWith({ density: { detailAmpLo: 0.35, detailAmpHi: 1.05 } });
    const lo = p.density.detailAmpLo, hi = p.density.detailAmpHi;
    expect(Object.is((fold({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'param', path: 'density.detailAmpHi' }, b: { op: 'neg', x: { op: 'param', path: 'density.detailAmpLo' } } }, p) as { v: number }).v, hi - lo)).toBe(true);
  });

  test('tap, interpolated, slide, rangeChoice and ref are never folded; a def is folded inside itself', () => {
    const e = resolveDensity(src({
      op: 'add',
      a: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'tap', name: 't', x: C(1) }, b: { op: 'interpolated', x: { op: 'add', a: C(1), b: C(2) } } },
      b: { op: 'add',
        a: { op: 'slide', x: C(2), knots: [[0, 1], [10, 0]] },
        b: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'rangeChoice', x: C(0.5), lo: 0, hi: 1, inside: C(1), outside: C(2) }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'd' } } },
    }, { d: { op: 'mul', a: C(2), b: { op: 'neg', x: C(4) } } }), P);
    expect(rootOf(e)).toEqual({
      op: 'add',
      a: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'tap', name: 't', x: C(1) }, b: { op: 'interpolated', x: C(3) } },
      b: { op: 'add',
        a: { op: 'slide', x: C(2), knots: [[0, 1], [10, 0]] },
        b: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'rangeChoice', x: C(0.5), lo: 0, hi: 1, inside: C(1), outside: C(2) }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'd' } } },
    });
    expect(e.defs).toEqual({ d: C(-8) });
  });

  test('paths are preserved: every surviving node keeps its source path', () => {
    const e = resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, P);
    const at = (v: unknown, path: string): Record<string, unknown> => path.split('.').reduce<Record<string, unknown>>((n, k) => n[k] as Record<string, unknown>, v as Record<string, unknown>);
    const recipPath = 'root.a.a.x.x.a.a.a.a.b.b.x.b.x.x.b';
    expect(at(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, recipPath)['op']).toBe('recip');
    expect(at(e, recipPath)).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: 1 / P.density.noises.jag.clampSigma });
    expect(at(e, 'root.a.b.b.a')).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: P.density.detailAmpLo });
    expect(at(e, 'root.a.b.b.b.a')).toEqual({ op: 'const', v: P.density.detailAmpHi - P.density.detailAmpLo });
    expect(at(e, 'root.a.a')['op']).toBe('tap');
    expect(at(e, 'root.b')).toEqual({ op: 'tap', name: 'islands', x: C(-1e6) });

  test('a fresh, deep-frozen output; the source is neither changed nor frozen', () => {
    const s = { root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'param', path: 'density.detailAmpLo' }, b: { op: 'clamp', x: Y, lo: 0, hi: { param: 'density.detailAmpHi' } } }, defs: { d: Y } };

  test('tier 2 runs first: an invalid source throws ExprValidationError with its source paths', () => {
    expect(codes(() => resolveDensity(src({ op: 'param', path: 'climate.T' }), P))).toEqual(['root.path: UNKNOWN_PARAM']);

    expect(codes(() => resolveDensity(src({ op: 'mul', a: Y, b: C(1e10) }), P))).toEqual(['root.b.v: LITERAL_RANGE']);
    // A tier-1-valid REF_CYCLE source (tier 1 knows nothing of refs) is refused instead of overflowing the stack.

    const cyclic = checkJson({ root: { op: 'ref', name: 'a' }, defs: { a: { op: 'ref', name: 'b' }, b: { op: 'neg', x: { op: 'ref', name: 'a' } } } }, 'density.defs', issues, 'density');
    expect(issues).toEqual([]);
    expect(codes(() => resolveDensity(cyclic, P)).map((c) => c.split(': ')[1])).toContain('REF_CYCLE');
    expect(() => resolveDensity(cyclic, P)).toThrow(ExprValidationError);
  });

  test('the validation memo: a frozen source is validated once (the default across contexts), an unfrozen one every call', () => {
    resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, P);
    const n0 = densitySourceValidations();
    resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, paramsWith({ density: { detailAmpHi: 3 } }));
    createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'));
    createDensityContext(ctxFor('7', { density: { detailAmpLo: 0.1 } }));
    expect(densitySourceValidations()).toBe(n0);
    const loose = { root: Y, defs: {} };
    resolveDensity(loose, P);
    resolveDensity(loose, P);
    expect(densitySourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 2);
  });
});

/** The resolved default and the legacy builder's tree for `p`: equal hash and −0-aware deep equality. */
function checkIdentity(p: Params, what: string): DensityExpr {
  const e = resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, p);
  const legacy = legacyDefaultDensityExpr(p.density);
  expect(exprHash(e.root), what).toBe(exprHash(legacy.root));
  expect(sameTree(e, legacy), what).toBeNull();
  return e;
}

/** Compiled corner and voxel values (Object.is) of the resolved default and the legacy tree at the three columns. */
function checkCompiled(seedText: string, patch: ParamsPatch, what: string, voxelStride: number): void {
  const c = ctxFor(seedText, patch);
  const a = createDensityContext(c);
  const b = createDensityContext(c, legacyDefaultDensityExpr(c.params.density));
  const shape = (dc: DensityContext): number[] => [dc.compiled.nodes.length, dc.compiled.positionSlotCount, dc.compiled.columnSlotCount, dc.compiled.interpolatedSlotCount];
  expect(shape(a), what).toEqual(shape(b));
  // §2.1: 51 nodes, 2 position slots, 2 column slots (at clampSigma 1 the constant 1 / 1 merges with the 1 of J: 50).
  if (seedText === '42' && Object.keys(patch).length === 0) expect(shape(a)).toEqual([51, 2, 2, 1]);
  const eq = (dc: DensityContext, cx: number, cz: number): void => { dc.column(cx, cz); };
  for (const [cx, cz] of COLUMNS) {
    eq(a, cx, cz);
    eq(b, cx, cz);
    for (let k = 0; k <= 48; k++) {
      for (let j = 0; j <= 4; j++) {
        for (let i = 0; i <= 4; i++) {
          a.compiled.cornerFn(i, k, j);
          b.compiled.cornerFn(i, k, j);
          const ix = cornerValueIndex(0, i, k, j);
          if (!Object.is(a.compiled.cornerValues[ix], b.compiled.cornerValues[ix])) throw new Error(`${what}: corner (${i}, ${k}, ${j}) of (${cx}, ${cz})`);
        }
      }
    }
    for (let v = 0; v < 98304; v += voxelStride) {
      const lx = v & 15, lz = (v >> 4) & 15, y = (v >> 8) - 64;
      const va = a.compiled.voxelFn(lx, y, lz), vb = b.compiled.voxelFn(lx, y, lz);
      if (!Object.is(va, vb)) throw new Error(`${what}: voxel (${lx}, ${y}, ${lz}) of (${cx}, ${cz}): ${va} vs ${vb}`);
    }
  }
}

describe('§2.1 bit-identity: the resolved default is the legacy builder\'s tree', () => {
  test('at DEFAULTS and at clampSigma ∈ {1, 3, 7.3, 8}: equal exprHash, −0-aware equality, equal compiled values at every corner and voxel', () => {
    checkIdentity(P, 'DEFAULTS');
    checkCompiled('42', {}, 'DEFAULTS', 1);
    for (const cs of [1, 3, 7.3, 8]) {
      const patch: ParamsPatch = { density: { noises: { jag: { clampSigma: cs } } } };
      checkIdentity(paramsWith(patch), `clampSigma ${cs}`);
      checkCompiled('42', patch, `clampSigma ${cs}`, 1);
    }
  });

  test('at 64 random schema-valid density groups (noise leaves included, q15 through the schema; every corner, every 61st voxel)', () => {
    const next = testRng(808);
    const leaves = SCHEMA.leaves.filter((l) => l.path.startsWith('density.'));
    for (let t = 0; t < 64; t++) {
      const noises: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      const density: Record<string, unknown> = { noises };
      for (const { path, leaf } of leaves) {
        const key = path.slice('density.'.length);
        if (key.startsWith('noises.')) noises[key.slice('noises.'.length)] = randomValue(leaf, next);
        else density[key] = randomValue(leaf, next);
      }
      const patch = { density } as ParamsPatch;
      const what = `group ${t}: ${JSON.stringify(density)}`;
      checkIdentity(paramsWith(patch), what);
      checkCompiled('42', patch, what, 61);
    }
  });

  test('the default DensityContext compiles the resolved default (one frozen tree)', () => {
    const dc = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'));
    expect(exprHash(dc.expr.root)).toBe(exprHash(legacyDefaultDensityExpr(DEFAULTS.density).root));
    expect(dc.compiled.expr).toBe(dc.expr);
    expect(frozenEverywhere(dc.expr)).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('resolveDensityNode (§3.4)', () => {
  /** The default tree with the terrain tap muted to 0 (U2's density perturbation). */
  const muted = (() => {
    const t = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE)) as { root: { a: { a: Record<string, unknown> } } };
    t.root.a.a['mute'] = 0;
    return t as unknown as DensitySource;
  })();
  const ctx = ctxFor('42');
  const dc = createDensityContext(ctx);

  test('a node under a muted tap is evaluated from the source: the muted terrain tap and its interpolated sum give the unmuted terrain', () => {
    const full = createDensityReference(resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, P), dc.noises);
    const tapNode = resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root.a.a', P);
    expect(rootOf(tapNode)['op']).toBe('tap');
    expect(rootOf(tapNode)['x']).toMatchObject({ op: 'interpolated' });
    const inner = resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root.a.a.x.x', P);
    expect(rootOf(inner)['op']).toBe('interpolated'); // wrapped: it has an interpolated ancestor
    expect(sameTree(rootOf(inner)['x'], (rootOf(resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, P))['a'] as { a: { x: { x: unknown } } }).a.x.x)).toBeNull();
    const rTap = createDensityReference(tapNode, dc.noises), rInner = createDensityReference(inner, dc.noises);
    const mutedRoot = createDensityReference(resolveDensity(muted, P), dc.noises);
    const next = testRng(809);
    for (let n = 0; n < 300; n++) {
      const [cx, cz] = COLUMNS[n % COLUMNS.length]!;
      const s = dc.columns.get(cx, cz);
      const x = 16 * cx + (next() % 16), z = 16 * cz + (next() % 16), y = -64 + (next() % 384);
      const want = full.tap(s, 'terrain', x, y, z);
      expect(Object.is(rTap.voxel(s, x, y, z), want)).toBe(true);
      expect(Object.is(rInner.voxel(s, x, y, z), want)).toBe(true);
      expect(mutedRoot.tap(s, 'terrain', x, y, z)).toBe(0);
    }
  });

  test('the root is the final density (its own mute applies there); a node with no interpolated ancestor is not wrapped', () => {
    expect(sameTree(resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root', P), resolveDensity(muted, P))).toBeNull();
    const detail = resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root.a.b', P);
    expect(sameTree(detail.root, (rootOf(resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, P))['a'] as { b: unknown }).b)).toBeNull();
    expect(detail.defs).toEqual({});
    // An interpolated node itself is not wrapped again.
    expect(rootOf(resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root.a.a.x', P))['op']).toBe('interpolated');
    expect((rootOf(resolveDensityNode(muted, 'root.a.a.x', P))['x'] as { op: string }).op).toBe('add');
    // A param operand of recip is a node too: its value.
    expect(resolveDensityNode(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'root.a.a.x.x.a.a.a.a.b.b.x.b.x.x.b.x', P).root)
      .toEqual({ op: 'interpolated', x: C(P.density.noises.jag.clampSigma) });
  });

  test('a def, and a node inside it, take the placement of the def\'s first reference; an unreachable def is at voxel placement', () => {
    const s = src(
      { op: 'add', a: { op: 'interpolated', x: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'ref', name: 'inner' }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 't', x: Y } } }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'amp' } },
      {
        amp: { op: 'mul', a: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'inner' } },
        inner: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'col', field: 'offset' }, b: { op: 'neg', x: Y } },
        lone: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'ref', name: 'amp' }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'u', mute: 0, x: Y } },
      },
    );
    // inner is first referenced inside interpolated (root.a.x.a), although amp also reads it at voxel placement.
    const inner = resolveDensityNode(s, 'defs.inner', P);
    expect(inner.root).toEqual({ op: 'interpolated', x: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'col', field: 'offset' }, b: { op: 'neg', x: Y } } });
    expect(inner.defs).toEqual({});
    expect(resolveDensityNode(s, 'defs.inner.b.x', P).root).toEqual({ op: 'interpolated', x: Y });
    // amp is first referenced at voxel placement; its own output carries the defs it reaches.
    const amp = resolveDensityNode(s, 'defs.amp', P);
    expect(amp.root).toEqual({ op: 'mul', a: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'inner' } });
    expect(Object.keys(amp.defs)).toEqual(['inner']);
    // lone is unreachable: voxel placement; its muted tap applies inside it, the selected tap's own mute does not.
    const lone = resolveDensityNode(s, 'defs.lone', P);
    expect(lone.root).toEqual({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'ref', name: 'amp' }, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'u', x: C(0) } });
    expect(Object.keys(lone.defs).sort()).toEqual(['amp', 'inner']);
    expect(resolveDensityNode(s, 'defs.lone.b', P).root).toEqual({ op: 'tap', name: 'u', x: Y });
    // Every output compiles and evaluates.
    const s0 = dc.columns.get(0, 0);
    for (const path of ['defs.inner', 'defs.inner.b.x', 'defs.amp', 'defs.lone', 'defs.lone.b', 'root', 'root.a', 'root.a.x.b']) {
      const r = createDensityReference(resolveDensityNode(s, path, P), dc.noises);
      expect(Number.isFinite(r.voxel(s0, 3, 70, 5)), path).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(frozenEverywhere(amp)).toBe(true);
  });

  test('a path that names no node throws a RangeError; an invalid source throws ExprValidationError', () => {
    expect(() => resolveDensityNode(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'root.q', P)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => resolveDensityNode(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'root.a.b.b.b.b.lo', P)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => resolveDensityNode(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'defs.nope', P)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => resolveDensityNode(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, '', P)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => resolveDensityNode(src({ op: 'bogus' }), 'root', P)).toThrow(ExprValidationError);
  });
});

describe('freezeTree and the DensityContext\'s frozen tree (D10)', () => {
  test('freezeTree deep-freezes in place, identity kept, also below an already-frozen node; shared and cyclic objects once', () => {
    const leaf = { op: 'y' };
    const mid = Object.freeze({ op: 'neg', x: { op: 'abs', x: leaf } }); // frozen, its child not
    const tree = { root: { op: 'add', a: mid, b: leaf }, defs: { d: { op: 'slide', x: leaf, knots: [[0, 1], [2, 3]] } } };
    expect(freezeTree(tree)).toBe(tree);
    expect(frozenEverywhere(tree)).toBe(true);
    const cyc: Record<string, unknown> = { op: 'neg' };
    cyc['x'] = cyc;
    expect(freezeTree(cyc)).toBe(cyc);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(cyc)).toBe(true);
    expect(freezeTree(5)).toBe(5);
    const typed = new Float64Array(2);
    expect(() => freezeTree({ a: typed })).not.toThrow();
    expect(Object.isFrozen(typed)).toBe(false);
  });

  test('an explicit tree is frozen in place (identity kept): mutating dc.expr at any depth throws', () => {
    const inner = Object.freeze({ op: 'add', a: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }, b: { op: 'y' } });
    const e = { root: { op: 'max', a: inner, b: { op: 'tap', name: 'islands', x: { op: 'const', v: -1e6 } } }, defs: {} } as unknown as DensityExpr;
    const dc2 = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'), e);
    expect(dc2.expr).toBe(e);
    expect(dc2.compiled.expr).toBe(e);
    expect(frozenEverywhere(e)).toBe(true);
    expect(() => { (rootOf(e)['b'] as Record<string, unknown>)['name'] = 'x'; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { ((inner as unknown as { a: Record<string, unknown> }).a)['id'] = 'jag'; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { (e.defs as Record<string, Expr>)['n'] = { op: 'y' }; }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('the default context\'s tree is frozen at every depth', () => {
    const dc3 = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42'));
    expect(() => { (rootOf(dc3.expr)['b'] as Record<string, unknown>)['name'] = 'x'; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    const tap = rootOf(dc3.expr)['a'] as { a: { x: { x: Record<string, unknown> } } };
    expect(() => { tap.a.x.x['op'] = 'mul'; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { (dc3.expr as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)['root'] = null; }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('the default tree is JSON data: resolution reads it, never mutates it', () => {
    const text = JSON.stringify(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE as JsonValue);
    resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, paramsWith({ density: { detailAmpLo: 2 } }));
    expect(JSON.stringify(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE)).toBe(text);
  });
});

"The default's resolution memo hits across contexts" is pinned as `densitySourceValidations()` not moving across `resolveDensity(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, …)` at other params and two `createDensityContext` on different seeds and params, while an unfrozen source is validated on every call — cost if wrong: ~60 allocations per context.
- Ruling: resolution is a recursive copy over validated trees only (tier 2 bounds every tree root's expanded depth at 128 and refs are not followed), every node rebuilt in place of its source node (paths preserved) with `op` first and the builder's field order (`{op, a, b}`, `{op, x, lo, hi}`, `{op, name, x}`, `{op, x, knots}`), each frozen as it is built; knots become fresh frozen `[y, v]` pairs; `defs` are written with `Object.defineProperty` (no def name reaches a setter); a ref whose target reads as a non-finite number in `params` throws `RangeError('resolveDensity: <path> is not a finite number in params')` (unreachable through `checkParams`). Folding checks the children after their own resolution (bottom-up), so `neg(param lo)` → `const(−lo)` → `add(const hi, const(−lo))` → `const(hi + (−lo))`; `clamp` folds with `valClamp(x, lo, hi)` when x is const — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: `resolveDensityNode` placement — a node is inside when an `interpolated` **strictly** above it in its own tree root holds it (an `interpolated` node itself is not wrapped again), or when its tree root is a def whose first reference is inside `interpolated`; "first reference in source DFS order" = an explicit-stack pre-order from `root` in evaluation order (`SOURCE_CHILD_KEYS`) that enters a def at its first `ref` (the `findTap` rule), then every def not reached yet in key order as a voxel-placed start (so a def referenced only from an unreachable def takes that reference's placement); **mutes are ignored** by this walk (a muted subtree is still source structure). The selected node's own mute is dropped at any depth of the selection (a selected muted tap yields `tap(name, resolved child)`), mutes strictly inside apply, the defs the output carries are resolved normally (their mutes apply). Restricting the output's `defs` to the reached closure avoids `DUPLICATE_TAP` when the node lies in a def (its taps would otherwise appear in the copy and in the def) — cost if wrong: Task 17's `node` field values for defs under mutes.
- Ruling: `'root'` in `resolveDensityNode` is §3.4's "the root is the final density, the resolved tree's voxel value", which takes precedence over "the node's own mute does not apply": a muted root tap shows its mute value there — cost if wrong: one branch.

import { describe, expect, expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
import { RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX } from '../../src/core/constants';
import { DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import { checkJson, type TreeIssueCode } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import type { Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { rulesColumnCost } from '../../src/gen/inspect/cost';
import {
  rulesSourceValidations, validateRulesSource, type RuleParamRef, type RulesSourceCode, type RulesSourceIssue,
} from '../../src/gen/surface/source';
import { validateRules, type RuleErrorCode, type RuleRefCode, type RuleSourceMode } from '../../src/gen/surface/rules';
import { surfaceOpsRules } from '../../src/metrics/sp3cGoldens';
import { COLLIDE, REGISTRY } from '../../src/world/blocks/index';
import { COLLIDE_NONE } from '../../src/world/blocks/kinds';

type Node = Record<string, unknown>;
const block = (state: string): Node => ({ kind: 'block', state });
const seq = (...rules: unknown[]): Node => ({ kind: 'sequence', rules });
const when = (c: Node, then: unknown): Node => ({ kind: 'condition', if: c, then });
const ref = (param: string, neg = false): Node => (neg ? { param, neg: true } : { param });
const lines = (issues: readonly RulesSourceIssue[]): string[] => issues.map((i) => `${i.path}: ${i.code}`);
const check = (tree: unknown): string[] => lines(validateRulesSource(tree));
/** A tree of one condition rule over `c` (a block under it), so the condition's path is `root.if`. */
const under = (c: Node): Node => when(c, block('stone'));

/** The nine numeric fields (§1.3), each in a minimal valid condition, `int` for the int fields. */
const FIELDS: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly kind: string; readonly field: string; readonly int: boolean; readonly node: (v: unknown) => Node }> = [
  { kind: 'stoneDepth', field: 'offset', int: true, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'stoneDepth', side: 'floor', offset: v, addSurfaceDepth: true }) },
  { kind: 'water', field: 'offset', int: true, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'water', offset: v, runTop: false }) },
  { kind: 'yAbove', field: 'minY', int: true, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'yAbove', minY: v, runTop: true }) },
  { kind: 'verticalGradient', field: 'trueAtAndBelow', int: true, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: v, falseAtAndAbove: 384 }) },
  { kind: 'verticalGradient', field: 'falseAtAndAbove', int: true, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: -384, falseAtAndAbove: v }) },
  { kind: 'steep', field: 'min', int: false, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'steep', min: v }) },
  { kind: 'noiseThreshold', field: 'min', int: false, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: v, max: 1e9 }) },
  { kind: 'noiseThreshold', field: 'max', int: false, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: -1e9, max: v }) },
  { kind: 'temperatureBelow', field: 't', int: false, node: (v) => ({ kind: 'temperatureBelow', t: v }) },
];

describe('validateRulesSource: the default tree and the ref form (SP3d spec §1.3, §1.7)', () => {
  test('the default source passes tier 2, and its 15 refs are where §2.2 puts them', () => {
    expect(validateRulesSource(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('every numeric field takes a ref and a negated ref; int fields take int targets only', () => {
    for (const f of FIELDS) {
      const at = `root.if.${f.field}`;
      // An int target in any field; its negation [−319, 64] is inside [−384, 384].
      expect(check(under(f.node(ref('surface.cliffMinY')))), `${f.kind}.${f.field}`).toEqual([]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(ref('surface.lapseBase', true)))), `${f.kind}.${f.field}`).toEqual([]);
      // A number target, and a noise's clampSigma: number fields only.
      for (const target of ['surface.snowline', 'density.detailAmpHi', 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma', 'surface.noises.depth.clampSigma']) {
        expect(check(under(f.node(ref(target)))), `${f.kind}.${f.field} ← ${target}`).toEqual(f.int ? [`${at}: PARAM_KIND`] : []);
        expect(check(under(f.node(ref(target, true)))), `${f.kind}.${f.field} ← −${target}`).toEqual(f.int ? [`${at}: PARAM_KIND`] : []);
      }
      expect(validateRulesSource(under(f.node(ref('surface.snowline'))))[0]?.message ?? '').toMatch(f.int ? /integer field/ : /^$/);
    }
  });

  test('a malformed ref is BAD_FIELD, a path that is not a target UNKNOWN_PARAM, both at the field (never .param)', () => {
    const bad: unknown[] = [
      {}, { neg: true }, { param: 3 }, { param: 'surface.snowline', neg: false }, { param: 'surface.snowline', neg: 1 },
      { param: 'surface.snowline', scale: -1 }, { param: ['surface.snowline'] },
    ];
    const unknown = [
      'climate.scaleMul', 'surface.noises.patch', 'surface.noises.patch.octaves', 'surface.depthMul.x', 'surface', '',
      'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__', 'hasOwnProperty', 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma.x', 'SURFACE.snowline',
    ];
    for (const f of FIELDS) {
      const at = `root.if.${f.field}`;
      for (const v of bad) expect(check(under(f.node(v))), `${f.kind}.${f.field} = ${JSON.stringify(v)}`).toEqual([`${at}: BAD_FIELD`]);
      for (const p of unknown) expect(check(under(f.node(ref(p)))), `${f.kind}.${f.field} → ${p}`).toEqual([`${at}: UNKNOWN_PARAM`]);
    }
    // Arrays, strings and booleans in a numeric field keep validateRules' codes.
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'steep', min: [1] }))).toEqual(['root.if.min: NOT_FINITE']);
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'yAbove', minY: '80', runTop: true }))).toEqual(['root.if.minY: NOT_INTEGER']);
  });

  test('refs only in the nine numeric fields: other fields keep their codes', () => {
    const r = ref('surface.cliffMinY');
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'stoneDepth', side: r, offset: 0, addSurfaceDepth: true }))).toEqual(['root.if.side: BAD_SIDE']);
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'stoneDepth', side: 'floor', offset: 0, addSurfaceDepth: r }))).toEqual(['root.if.addSurfaceDepth: NOT_BOOLEAN']);
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'biome', biomes: r }))).toEqual(['root.if.biomes: NOT_ARRAY']);
    expect(check(under({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: r, min: 0, max: 1 }))).toEqual(['root.if.noise: UNKNOWN_NOISE']);
    expect(check({ kind: 'block', state: r })).toEqual(['root.state: UNKNOWN_BLOCK']);
  });

  test('order checks over static ranges: largest min vs smallest max, two refs to one leaf independent', () => {
    const nt = (min: unknown, max: unknown): Node => under({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min, max });
    const pt = ref('surface.patchThreshold'); // [0, 3]
    const ptn = ref('surface.patchThreshold', true); // [−3, 0]
    expect(check(nt(pt, 8))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(nt(pt, 3))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(nt(pt, 2.99))).toEqual(['root.if: RANGE_ORDER']);
    expect(check(nt(-8, ptn))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(nt(-3, ptn))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(nt(-2.99, ptn))).toEqual(['root.if: RANGE_ORDER']);
    expect(check(nt(ptn, pt))).toEqual([]);
    // min = max = t is true for every t, but two refs are judged independently (conservative; the message says so).
    expect(check(nt(pt, pt))).toEqual(['root.if: RANGE_ORDER']);
    expect(validateRulesSource(nt(pt, pt))[0]!.message).toMatch(/independently, even two to the same parameter/);
    expect(validateRulesSource(nt(2, 1))[0]!.message).toBe('noiseThreshold needs min ≤ max');
    const vg = (lo: unknown, hi: unknown): Node => under({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: lo, falseAtAndAbove: hi });
    const cm = ref('surface.cliffMinY'); // [−64, 319]
    expect(check(vg(cm, 320))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(vg(cm, 319))).toEqual(['root.if: GRADIENT_ORDER']);
    expect(check(vg(-65, cm))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(vg(-64, cm))).toEqual(['root.if: GRADIENT_ORDER']);
    expect(check(vg(ref('surface.cliffMinY', true), 65))).toEqual([]); // [−319, 64]
    expect(check(vg(ref('surface.cliffMinY', true), 64))).toEqual(['root.if: GRADIENT_ORDER']);
    expect(check(vg(cm, cm))).toEqual(['root.if: GRADIENT_ORDER']);
    expect(check(vg(cm, ref('surface.lapseBase')))).toEqual(['root.if: GRADIENT_ORDER']);
    // An invalid side is not order-checked.
    expect(check(vg(ref('surface.snowline'), 0))).toEqual(['root.if.trueAtAndBelow: PARAM_KIND']);
  });

  test('an int field\'s ref range must lie in [−384, 384] (OUT_OF_RANGE at the field), checked on a wide int target', () => {
    const mode: RuleSourceMode = { target: (p) => (p === 'wide' ? { lo: -500, hi: 0, int: true } : p === 'ok' ? { lo: -384, hi: 384, int: true } : undefined) };
    const issues = (tree: unknown): string[] => validateRules(tree, () => undefined, mode).map((i) => `${i.path}: ${i.code}`);
    expect(issues(under({ kind: 'water', offset: ref('wide'), runTop: true }))).toEqual(['root.if.offset: OUT_OF_RANGE']);
    expect(issues(under({ kind: 'water', offset: ref('wide', true), runTop: true }))).toEqual(['root.if.offset: OUT_OF_RANGE']);
    expect(issues(under({ kind: 'water', offset: ref('ok'), runTop: true }))).toEqual([]);
    expect(issues(under({ kind: 'water', offset: ref('ok', true), runTop: true }))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('literals: number fields within ±1e9 (LITERAL_RANGE), int fields keep [−384, 384]; source mode only', () => {
    for (const f of FIELDS) {
      const at = `root.if.${f.field}`;
      if (f.int) {
        expect(check(under(f.node(385))), at).toEqual([`${at}: OUT_OF_RANGE`]);
        expect(check(under(f.node(2e9))), at).toEqual([`${at}: OUT_OF_RANGE`]);
        continue;
      }
      expect(check(under(f.node(1e9))), at).toEqual([]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(-1e9))), at).toEqual([]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(1e9 + 1))), at).toEqual([`${at}: LITERAL_RANGE`]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(-1.5e300))), at).toEqual([`${at}: LITERAL_RANGE`]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(-0))), at).toEqual([`${at}: NEGATIVE_ZERO`]);
      expect(check(under(f.node(Infinity))), at).toEqual([`${at}: NOT_FINITE`]);
      // validateRules without the source mode (code-built trees) accepts large literals, and keeps refusing refs as numbers.
      expect(validateRules(under(f.node(f.field === 'min' ? -2e9 : 2e9)), () => ({ dims: 2, remap: 'none', clampSigma: 3 }))).toEqual([]);
      expect(validateRules(under(f.node(ref('surface.snowline'))), () => ({ dims: 2, remap: 'none', clampSigma: 3 })).map((i) => i.code)).toEqual(['NOT_FINITE']);
    }
    expect(validateRules(under({ kind: 'water', offset: ref('surface.cliffMinY'), runTop: true }), () => undefined).map((i) => i.code)).toEqual(['NOT_INTEGER']);
  });

  test('a biome list holds at most 64 entries (TOO_MANY_BIOMES at .biomes, entries not checked); source mode only', () => {
    const biomes = (n: number, name = 'plains'): Node => under({ kind: 'biome', biomes: Array.from({ length: n }, () => name) });
    expect(check(biomes(64))).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(biomes(65))).toEqual(['root.if.biomes: TOO_MANY_BIOMES']);
    expect(check(biomes(1024, 'nowhere'))).toEqual(['root.if.biomes: TOO_MANY_BIOMES']);
    expect(check(biomes(2, 'nowhere'))).toEqual(['root.if.biomes[0]: UNKNOWN_BIOME', 'root.if.biomes[1]: UNKNOWN_BIOME']);
    expect(check(seq(block('stone'), when({ kind: 'not', if: { kind: 'biome', biomes: Array(65).fill('desert') } }, block('sand')))))
      .toEqual(['root.rules[1].if.if.biomes: TOO_MANY_BIOMES']);
    expect(validateRules(biomes(200), () => undefined)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('a block state that does not collide is NOT_SOLID (validateRulesSource only); every other registered state passes', () => {
    expect(check(block('air'))).toEqual(['root.state: NOT_SOLID']);
    expect(validateRulesSource(block('air'))[0]!.message).toMatch(/air does not collide/);
    expect(check(seq(block('stone'), when({ kind: 'skyOpen' }, block('air'))))).toEqual(['root.rules[1].then.state: NOT_SOLID']);
    expect(validateRules(block('air'), () => undefined)).toEqual([]);
    let solid = 0;
    for (let id = 0; id < REGISTRY.stateCount; id++) {
      const key = REGISTRY.stateKey(id);
      const want = COLLIDE[id] === COLLIDE_NONE ? ['root.state: NOT_SOLID'] : [];
      expect(check(block(key)), key).toEqual(want);
      if (want.length === 0) solid++;
    }
    expect(solid).toBe(REGISTRY.stateCount - 1);
  });

  test('the sp3c.surface.ops fixture\'s block states all collide (its tree passes tier 2)', () => {
    const states: string[] = [];
    const stack: unknown[] = [surfaceOpsRules()];
    while (stack.length > 0) {
      const x = stack.pop();
      if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null) continue;
      if (Array.isArray(x)) { stack.push(...x); continue; }
      const n = x as Node;
      if (n['kind'] === 'block') states.push(n['state'] as string);
      stack.push(...Object.values(n));
    }
    expect(states.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);
    for (const s of states) expect(COLLIDE[REGISTRY.parseStateKey(s)], s).not.toBe(COLLIDE_NONE);
    expect(validateRulesSource(surfaceOpsRules())).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('validateRulesSource: column cost, the issue cap and the memo (SP3d spec §1.7, §1.8)', () => {
  /** A tree without a fast path (its first leaf is under a biome condition, no floor stoneDepth) of exactly n nodes. */
  function noFastPath(n: number): Node {
    const rest = n - 4; // root sequence, the condition, its biome, its block
    const parts: Node[] = [when({ kind: 'biome', biomes: ['plains'] }, block('grass_block'))];
    for (let left = rest; left > 0;) {
      const k = Math.min(left - 1, 900);
      parts.push(seq(...Array.from({ length: k }, () => block('stone'))));
      left -= k + 1;
    }
    return seq(...parts);
  }

  test('COLUMN_COST at the leaf path above RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX (98,304 per node without a fast path), not at it', () => {
    const most = Math.floor(RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX / 98304);
    expect(most).toBe(1412);
    const ok = noFastPath(most), over = noFastPath(most + 1);
    expect(rulesColumnCost(ok)).toBe(most * 98304);
    expect(rulesColumnCost(over)).toBe((most + 1) * 98304);
    expect(rulesColumnCost(over)).toBeGreaterThan(RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX);
    expect(validateRules(over, () => undefined)).toEqual([]);
    expect(check(ok)).toEqual([]);
    expect(validateRulesSource(over)).toEqual([{
      path: '', code: 'COLUMN_COST', message: `column cost ${(most + 1) * 98304} is above ${RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX} (64 × the default tree's)`,
    }]);
    // The cost is judged only on an otherwise valid tree.
    const broken = noFastPath(most + 1);
    const parts = broken['rules'] as Node[];
    parts.push(block('air'));
    expect(check(broken)).toEqual([`root.rules[${parts.length - 1}].state: NOT_SOLID`]);
    // The same node count with a fast path costs 256 × (1 + depth bound) per node and passes.
    const fast = seq(...Array.from({ length: 1500 }, () => block('stone')));
    expect(check(fast)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('at most 50 issues, then TOO_MANY_ISSUES "<n> more" at the leaf path', () => {
    const tree = seq(...Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, k) => block(`nowhere${k}`)));
    const issues = validateRulesSource(tree);
    expect(issues.length).toBe(51);
    expect(issues[0]).toMatchObject({ path: 'root.rules[0].state', code: 'UNKNOWN_BLOCK' });
    expect(issues[49]).toMatchObject({ path: 'root.rules[49].state', code: 'UNKNOWN_BLOCK' });
    expect(issues[50]).toEqual({ path: '', code: 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES', message: '10 more' });
    expect(validateRulesSource(seq(...Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => block('x')))).length).toBe(50);
  });

  test('never throws on hostile input; issue lists are frozen', () => {
    const cyclic: Node = { kind: 'sequence', rules: [] };
    (cyclic['rules'] as unknown[]).push(cyclic);
    for (const v of [undefined, null, 3, 'root', [], {}, { kind: 'sequence', rules: [null] }, cyclic, { kind: 'condition' }]) {
      const issues = validateRulesSource(v);
      expect(issues.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      expect(issues.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(51);
      expect(Object.isFrozen(issues)).toBe(true);
      for (const i of issues) expect(Object.isFrozen(i)).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('memoised by identity for deep-frozen trees (a tier-1 clone is validated once); other trees on every call', () => {
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    const tree = { kind: 'sequence', rules: [when({ kind: 'steep', min: ref('surface.cliffSteep') }, block('stone')), block('dirt')] };
    const frozen = checkJson(tree, 'surface.rules', out, 'surfaceRules')!;
    expect(out).toEqual([]);
    const n0 = rulesSourceValidations();
    const a = validateRulesSource(frozen);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 1);
    const b = validateRulesSource(frozen);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 1);
    expect(b).toBe(a);
    expect(a).toEqual([]);
    // An invalid frozen tree: its issues are memoised too.
    const bad = checkJson(block('air'), 'surface.rules', out, 'surfaceRules')!;
    const i1 = validateRulesSource(bad);
    expect(validateRulesSource(bad)).toBe(i1);
    expect(lines(i1)).toEqual(['root.state: NOT_SOLID']);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 2);
    // Unfrozen, and frozen only at the top: validated every call (a child could change between calls).
    validateRulesSource(tree);
    validateRulesSource(tree);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 4);
    const top = Object.freeze({ ...tree });
    validateRulesSource(top);
    validateRulesSource(top);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n0 + 6);
    (top.rules[1] as Node)['state'] = 'air';
    expect(lines(validateRulesSource(top))).toEqual(['root.rules[1].state: NOT_SOLID']);
    // The default tree (tier 1's registered clone) is memoised.
    validateRulesSource(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES);
    const n1 = rulesSourceValidations();
    validateRulesSource(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n1);
  });
});

describe('issue codes (SP3d spec §1.1)', () => {
  test('RuleErrorCode, the source codes and validateRulesSource\'s codes are TreeIssueCodes', () => {
    expectTypeOf<RuleErrorCode>().toExtend<TreeIssueCode>();
    expectTypeOf<RuleRefCode>().toEqualTypeOf<'BAD_FIELD' | 'UNKNOWN_PARAM' | 'PARAM_KIND' | 'LITERAL_RANGE' | 'TOO_MANY_BIOMES' | 'NOT_SOLID'>();
    expectTypeOf<RulesSourceCode>().toEqualTypeOf<RuleErrorCode | RuleRefCode | 'COLUMN_COST' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES'>();
    expectTypeOf<RulesSourceCode>().toExtend<TreeIssueCode>();
    expectTypeOf<{ param: 'surface.snowline'; neg: true }>().toExtend<RuleParamRef>();
    const code: TreeIssueCode = validateRulesSource(block('air'))[0]!.code;
    expect(code).toBe('NOT_SOLID');
  });
});

Create `src/gen/surface/source.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The source model of the `surface.rules` leaf (SP3d spec §1.3, §1.7, §1.8): a rule tree as SP3c §3.1 encodes it, whose
 * nine numeric fields (`stoneDepth.offset`, `water.offset`, `yAbove.minY`, `verticalGradient.trueAtAndBelow` and
 * `.falseAtAndAbove`, `steep.min`, `noiseThreshold.min` and `.max`, `temperatureBelow.t`) may hold a parameter ref
 * `{param: <path>}` or `{param: <path>, neg: true}` instead of a number.
 *
 * `validateRulesSource` is tier 2 for the leaf: `validateRules` in its source mode over the schema's surface noises and
 * the ref targets below (every check over the targets' static ranges, so a slider move never invalidates a stored tree),
 * then, on a tree with no other issue, the column cost (`COLUMN_COST` at the leaf path when `rulesColumnCost` exceeds
 * `RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX`). It collects at most 50 issues (then one TOO_MANY_ISSUES, "N more", at the leaf path) and
 * never throws. Validity is a pure function of the tree, so the result is memoised by the tree object when the tree is
 * deep-frozen (tier 1's clones and the contexts' frozen trees are); any other tree is validated on every call.
 * Follows the gen determinism rules.
 */
import { RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX } from '../../core/constants';
import { NOISE_FIELD_RANGES, SCHEMA } from '../../core/params/schema';
import { rulesColumnCost } from '../inspect/cost';
import {
  validateRules, type RuleErrorCode, type RuleRefCode, type RuleRefTarget, type RuleSourceMode, type SurfaceNoiseInfo,
  type SurfaceNoiseLookup,
} from './rules';

const SCHEMA_ = SCHEMA;
const NOISE_RANGES = NOISE_FIELD_RANGES;
const VALIDATE = validateRules;
const COLUMN_COST = rulesColumnCost;
const COLUMN_COST_MAX = RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX;

/** A parameter ref in a numeric field: the target's value v, or 0 − v with `neg` (never −0). */
export interface RuleParamRef {
  readonly param: string;
  readonly neg?: true;
}

/** Tier 2's codes for the leaf: `validateRules`' codes, the source mode's, the column cost and the issue cap. */
export type RulesSourceCode = RuleErrorCode | RuleRefCode | 'COLUMN_COST' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES';

/** A tier-2 issue: the node path in `validateRules`' syntax (`root.rules[1].then.if.min`); '' is the leaf itself. */
export interface RulesSourceIssue {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly code: RulesSourceCode;
  readonly message: string;
}

/** Issues collected before the cap (§1.7: "at most 50, as tier 1"). */
const MAX_ISSUES = 50;

/**
 * The ref targets (§1.3): every `number` or `int` leaf under `density.` or `surface.`, and the `clampSigma` field of
 * their noise leaves, each with its static range ([min, max], or `NOISE_FIELD_RANGES.clampSigma`); only `int` leaves
 * may stand in an int field.
 */
const TARGETS: ReadonlyMap<string, RuleRefTarget> = (() => {
  const out = new Map<string, RuleRefTarget>();
  for (const { path, meta } of SCHEMA_.leaves) {
    if (!path.startsWith('density.') && !path.startsWith('surface.')) continue;
    if ((meta.kind === 'number' || meta.kind === 'int') && meta.min !== undefined && meta.max !== undefined) {
      out.set(path, Object.freeze({ lo: meta.min, hi: meta.max, int: meta.kind === 'int' }));
    } else if (meta.kind === 'noise') {
      out.set(`${path}.clampSigma`, Object.freeze({ lo: NOISE_RANGES.clampSigma.min, hi: NOISE_RANGES.clampSigma.max, int: false }));
    }
  }
  return out;
})();

const MODE: RuleSourceMode = Object.freeze({ target: (path: string) => TARGETS.get(path) });

/**
 * The schema's surface noises as validation sees them, from the leaves' metadata (no value is read): dims, and remap
 * 'none' for the leaves that must keep it (every surface noise; any other is taken as possibly 'uniform').
 */
const NOISES: SurfaceNoiseLookup = (() => {
  const m = new Map<string, SurfaceNoiseInfo>();
  for (const { path, meta } of SCHEMA_.leaves) {
    if (meta.kind !== 'noise' || !path.startsWith('surface.noises.')) continue;
    m.set(path, Object.freeze({ dims: meta.dims ?? 2, remap: meta.remapNone === true ? 'none' : 'uniform', clampSigma: NOISE_RANGES.clampSigma.max }));
  }
  return (name: string) => m.get(name);
})();

const MEMO = new WeakMap<object, readonly RulesSourceIssue[]>();
let validations = 0;

/** True when `v` and every object and array inside it are frozen (an iterative walk; shared objects visited once). */
function deepFrozen(v: object): boolean {
  const seen = new Set<object>();
  const stack: object[] = [v];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const x = stack.pop()!;
    if (seen.has(x)) continue;
    seen.add(x);
    if (!Object.isFrozen(x)) return false;
    for (const k of Object.keys(x)) {
      const c: unknown = (x as Record<string, unknown>)[k];
      if (typeof c === 'object' && c !== null) stack.push(c);
    }
  }
  return true;
}

/**
 * Tier 2 for `surface.rules` (§1.7): the issues of the source tree `source` (frozen, never empty when invalid; [] when
 * valid). Never throws. Memoised by identity for deep-frozen trees.
 */
export function validateRulesSource(source: unknown): readonly RulesSourceIssue[] {
  const key = typeof source === 'object' && source !== null ? source : null;
  if (key !== null) {
    const hit = MEMO.get(key);
    if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
  }
  validations++;
  const found: RulesSourceIssue[] = VALIDATE(source, NOISES, MODE);
  if (found.length === 0) {
    const cost = COLUMN_COST(source);
    if (cost > COLUMN_COST_MAX) {
      found.push({ path: '', code: 'COLUMN_COST', message: `column cost ${cost} is above ${COLUMN_COST_MAX} (64 × the default tree's)` });
    }
  }
  const issues = found.length <= MAX_ISSUES
    ? found
    : [...found.slice(0, MAX_ISSUES), { path: '', code: 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES' as const, message: `${found.length - MAX_ISSUES} more` }];
  for (const i of issues) Object.freeze(i);
  const result = Object.freeze(issues);
  if (key !== null && deepFrozen(key)) MEMO.set(key, result);
  return result;
}

/** How many times `validateRulesSource` validated a tree (memo misses); for the tests of the memo (§1.8). */
export function rulesSourceValidations(): number {
  return validations;
}
```

- Ruling: the source mode is an overload of `validateRules` itself — `validateRules(value, noises): RuleIssue[]` (unchanged) and `validateRules(value, noises, source: RuleSourceMode): RuleSourceIssue[]` — §1.7's "validateRules extended by the ref form", like Task 5's `validateExpr` source mode; without `source` nothing changes (a ref in a code-built tree is still `NOT_FINITE` / `NOT_INTEGER`; no `LITERAL_RANGE`, `TOO_MANY_BIOMES`, `NOT_SOLID`), so `surfaceRules`, `surfaceReference`, `surfaceCompile` tests and the goldens are untouched — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: exported names and shapes for later tasks — `src/gen/surface/rules.ts`: `type RuleRefCode = 'BAD_FIELD' | 'UNKNOWN_PARAM' | 'PARAM_KIND' | 'LITERAL_RANGE' | 'TOO_MANY_BIOMES' | 'NOT_SOLID'`; `interface RuleSourceIssue { path: string; code: RuleErrorCode | RuleRefCode; message: string }`; `interface RuleRefTarget { lo: number; hi: number; int: boolean }`; `interface RuleSourceMode { target(path: string): RuleRefTarget | undefined }`. `src/gen/surface/source.ts`: `validateRulesSource(source: unknown): readonly RulesSourceIssue[]` (a frozen array of frozen issues; `[]` when valid; never throws; no noise argument), `rulesSourceValidations(): number` (validations run = memo misses; Task 15's "slider-only commit misses neither memo" reads it), `type RulesSourceCode = RuleErrorCode | RuleRefCode | 'COLUMN_COST' | 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES'`, `interface RulesSourceIssue { path; code: RulesSourceCode; message }`, `interface RuleParamRef { param: string; neg?: true }`. `FIELDS` stays private (Task 20 exports it) — cost if wrong: renames in Tasks 10, 14, 15, 22.
- Ruling: issue paths are node paths in `validateRules`' syntax (`root.rules[1].then.if.min`); `COLUMN_COST` and `TOO_MANY_ISSUES` are at the empty node path `''`, so Task 14's `validateParamTrees` gives the leaf path alone (`surface.rules`, "at the leaf path", D3); `validateRules`' own `TOO_MANY_NODES` stays at `root` (→ `surface.rules.root`). `RANGE_ORDER` / `GRADIENT_ORDER` stay at the condition's path, as `validateRules` reports them today (`rules.ts:264`, `277`); every ref issue (`BAD_FIELD`, `UNKNOWN_PARAM`, `PARAM_KIND`, a ref's `OUT_OF_RANGE`) and `LITERAL_RANGE` is at the field's path, never `.param`; `TOO_MANY_BIOMES` at `<cond>.biomes`; `NOT_SOLID` at `<id>.state` — cost if wrong: test strings.
- Ruling: `COLUMN_COST` (`rulesColumnCost(source) > RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX`) is judged only on a tree with no other issue (density step 5's "only then"), so a broken oversized tree reports its structural issues alone — cost if wrong: one extra issue line on broken trees.
- Ruling: the 50-issue cap applies after the walk (validateRules collects everything; tier 1 bounds the input to 65,536 values): the first 50 issues in DFS pre-order, then `{path: '', code: 'TOO_MANY_ISSUES', message: '<n> more'}` — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: the memo (a `WeakMap` by tree object) is used only when the tree is **deep**-frozen, checked by an iterative walk once per miss: a tree frozen only at the top could change below and would make a memoised verdict stale (tested: a top-frozen tree is validated on every call and sees a child's change). Tier-1 clones (`checkJson`) and Tasks 8/10's `freezeTree` outputs are deep-frozen, so the defaults and every edited tree hit; §1.6's "frozen source" read as deep-frozen — cost if wrong: one O(n) walk per miss.
- Ruling: the ref targets are a private `TARGETS` Map in `gen/surface/source.ts`, built from `SCHEMA.leaves` (`number`/`int` leaves under `density.`/`surface.` with their [min, max] and an `int` flag; every noise leaf's `<path>.clampSigma` at `NOISE_FIELD_RANGES.clampSigma` [1, 8], not int), looked up with `Map.get` (so `constructor`, `toString`, `__proto__` are `UNKNOWN_PARAM`). It cannot import Task 5's `ALLOWED_REF_TARGETS` (other chain) and `cost.ts` (read-only) keeps its own private `TARGET_RANGES`: three equivalent tables at the join; Task 14 (or 17, the next writer of cost.ts) may switch both to Task 5's — cost if wrong: ~20 duplicated lines.
- Ruling: tier 2's noise lookup is built from the schema's metadata, not from a GenContext: every `surface.noises.*` noise leaf with its `dims` (default 2) and remap `'none'` when the leaf is `remapNone` (any other would be taken as possibly `'uniform'` and refused; every surface noise is `remapNone`), so the verdict is value-independent and equal to the context's `surfaceNoiseSource` for schema noises — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: the ref form — a plain object in one of the nine numeric fields is a ref when its own keys ⊆ {`param`, `neg`}, `param` is a string and `neg` is absent or exactly `true`; any other object there is `BAD_FIELD` (`{}`, `{neg: true}`, `{param: 3}`, `neg: false`, `neg: 1`, an extra key such as `scale`, `param` an array). Non-object non-numbers keep `NOT_FINITE` / `NOT_INTEGER`; a ref object in a non-numeric field keeps that field's code (`BAD_SIDE`, `NOT_BOOLEAN`, `NOT_ARRAY`, `UNKNOWN_NOISE`, `UNKNOWN_BLOCK`). Static range of a ref: the target's [lo, hi], negated [0 − hi, 0 − lo]; checks: int fields `PARAM_KIND` for a non-int target and `OUT_OF_RANGE` when the range leaves [−384, 384] (unreachable with today's int targets, [−64, 319]; pinned through `validateRules` with an injected wide target); `RANGE_ORDER` when max(min) > min(max); `GRADIENT_ORDER` when max(trueAtAndBelow) ≥ min(falseAtAndAbove); the order message gains "for every value of its parameters (refs are judged independently, even two to the same parameter)" only when a side is a ref (literal messages unchanged) — cost if wrong: test strings.
- Ruling: `LITERAL_RANGE` (|v| > 1e9) applies to the four number fields (`steep.min`, `noiseThreshold.min`/`.max`, `temperatureBelow.t`); int-field literals keep `OUT_OF_RANGE` [−384, 384]. 1e9 and the 64-biome limit are module-private constants of `rules.ts` (`core/constants.ts` is Task 11's alone in phase 1; no other layer needs them); Task 5's density literal limit is its own — cost if wrong: a later move into `TREE_LIMITS`.
- Ruling: `TOO_MANY_BIOMES` (> 64 entries) is reported at `.biomes` and the entries are not checked (tier 1's per-value-bound convention), so a 1,024-entry list of unknown names gives one issue; `NOT_SOLID` = `COLLIDE[parseStateKey(state)] === COLLIDE_NONE` read from `world/blocks` (today only `air` of the 25 states, pinned over every registered state) — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: the scan clamp is written `ns < -c ? -c : ns > c ? c : ns` with c = the depth noise's `clampSigma` (NormalNoise.z2's own form, `core/noise/normal.ts:35-36`, so schema noises are bit-identical and a NaN passes as before); `surfaceScanSettings` throws `RangeError('surface scan: depthMul <v> must be finite and ≥ 0')` before the noise checks, −0 accepted (sdMax 3) — cost if wrong: none.
- Ruling: no test mutates a rule tree after building a context (Task 9 changes no context; Task 10's list stays to be made).
- MEASUREMENT: a rule tree without a fast path is refused (`COLUMN_COST`) above ⌊RULES_COLUMN_COST_MAX / 98,304⌋ = 1,412 rule and condition nodes (138,805,248 passes, 1,413 × 98,304 = 138,903,552 refused), below `validateRules`' 4,096-node limit; a fast-path tree of 1,500 unconditioned blocks (256 per node) passes (`surfaceSource.test.ts`).
- MEASUREMENT: fast vs full `fillColumn` over a hand column (ground to y 60 … 66) with a constant depth noise 9 at clampSigma 3 (tree: floor 0+sd → dirt; stone): 4,096 differing voxels on the parent, 0 with the clamp; the sampled-columns check saw surfaceDepth 12 > SD_MAX 11 on the parent with a 3× schema-fuzz depth noise (`surfaceScan.test.ts`).
- No spec defects found for Task 9. No Green-on-parent file. No file of another chain touched (rules.ts, scan.ts and the master's `gen/surface` entry only; the master edit sits within 3 lines of Task 5/8's `gen/density` entry, the expected join conflict).
