Create `test/unit/surfaceResolve.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, expectTypeOf, test } from 'vitest';
import { canonicalJSON } from '../../src/core/params/canonical';
import { DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import { createSurfaceContext, surfaceContextOf } from '../../src/gen/surface/context';
import { RuleValidationError, type RuleValidationIssue } from '../../src/gen/surface/rules';
import { freezeRules, resolveRules, rulesSourceValidations, type RulesSourceIssue } from '../../src/gen/surface/source';
import { surfaceOpsRules } from '../../src/metrics/sp3cGoldens';
import { ctxFor, paramsWith } from '../harness/gen';
import { legacyDefaultSurfaceRules } from '../harness/legacyTrees';

type Node = Record<string, unknown>;
const block = (state: string): Node => ({ kind: 'block', state });
const seq = (...rules: unknown[]): Node => ({ kind: 'sequence', rules });
const when = (c: Node, then: unknown): Node => ({ kind: 'condition', if: c, then });

/** Params whose ref targets have values distinct from their defaults (all on the q15 grid). */
const P = paramsWith({
  density: { detailAmpLo: 0.25, noises: { jag: { clampSigma: 4 } } },
  surface: { patchThreshold: 0.75, snowline: -0.25, cliffSteep: 2.5, cliffMinY: 120, lapseBase: 100, noises: { patch: { clampSigma: 5 } } },
});

/** Each of the nine numeric fields as a ref (literal elsewhere), in one tree; every order check holds over the ranges. */
const SOURCE = (): Node => seq(
  when({ kind: 'stoneDepth', side: 'floor', offset: { param: 'surface.cliffMinY', neg: true }, addSurfaceDepth: true }, block('stone')),
  when({ kind: 'water', offset: { param: 'surface.lapseBase' }, runTop: false }, block('dirt')),
  when({ kind: 'yAbove', minY: { param: 'surface.cliffMinY' }, runTop: true }, block('stone')),
  when({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: { param: 'surface.cliffMinY', neg: true }, falseAtAndAbove: 384 }, block('deepslate')),
  when({ kind: 'steep', min: { param: 'surface.cliffSteep' } }, block('gravel')),
  when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: { param: 'surface.noises.patch.clampSigma', neg: true }, max: { param: 'surface.patchThreshold' } }, block('clay')),
  when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: { param: 'density.noises.jag.clampSigma', neg: true }, max: 8 }, block('mud')),
  when({ kind: 'temperatureBelow', t: { param: 'surface.snowline' } }, block('snow_block')),
  when({ kind: 'biome', biomes: ['desert', 'beach'] }, block('sand')),
  when({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: -384, falseAtAndAbove: { param: 'surface.lapseBase' } }, block('deepslate')),
  when({ kind: 'temperatureBelow', t: { param: 'density.detailAmpLo', neg: true } }, block('snow_block')),
  block('stone'),
);

/** SOURCE with every ref replaced by its value in P, as written by hand. */
const EXPECTED = (): Node => seq(
  when({ kind: 'stoneDepth', side: 'floor', offset: -120, addSurfaceDepth: true }, block('stone')),
  when({ kind: 'water', offset: 100, runTop: false }, block('dirt')),
  when({ kind: 'yAbove', minY: 120, runTop: true }, block('stone')),
  when({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: -120, falseAtAndAbove: 384 }, block('deepslate')),
  when({ kind: 'steep', min: 2.5 }, block('gravel')),
  when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: -5, max: 0.75 }, block('clay')),
  when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: -4, max: 8 }, block('mud')),
  when({ kind: 'temperatureBelow', t: -0.25 }, block('snow_block')),
  when({ kind: 'biome', biomes: ['desert', 'beach'] }, block('sand')),
  when({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: -384, falseAtAndAbove: 100 }, block('deepslate')),
  when({ kind: 'temperatureBelow', t: -0.25 }, block('snow_block')),
  block('stone'),
);

/** Every object and array of `v` (shared ones once). */
function containers(v: unknown): object[] {
  const out: object[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<object>();
  const walk = (x: unknown): void => {
    if (typeof x !== 'object' || x === null || seen.has(x)) return;
    seen.add(x);
    out.push(x);
    for (const c of Object.values(x)) walk(c);
  };
  walk(v);
  return out;
}

/** Every number of `v`, in DFS order. */
function numbers(v: unknown): number[] {
  if (typeof v === 'number') return [v];
  if (typeof v !== 'object' || v === null) return [];
  return Object.values(v).flatMap(numbers);
}

describe('resolveRules (SP3d spec §1.6): refs → numbers, nothing else changes', () => {
  test('every ref in the nine numeric fields becomes its target\'s value in params (0 − v for neg); literals and the rest are kept', () => {
    expect(P.surface.cliffMinY).toBe(120);
    expect(P.density.noises.jag.clampSigma).toBe(4);
    expect(P.surface.noises.patch.clampSigma).toBe(5);
    const tree = resolveRules(SOURCE(), P);
    expect(canonicalJSON(tree)).toBe(canonicalJSON(EXPECTED()));
  });

  test('the values follow params (the same source at the defaults)', () => {
    const d = paramsWith();
    const t = resolveRules(SOURCE(), d) as unknown as { rules: Array<{ if: Node }> };
    expect(t.rules[2]!.if['minY']).toBe(d.surface.cliffMinY);
    expect(t.rules[4]!.if['min']).toBe(d.surface.cliffSteep);
    expect(t.rules[5]!.if['min']).toBe(0 - d.surface.noises.patch.clampSigma);
    expect(t.rules[5]!.if['max']).toBe(d.surface.patchThreshold);
    expect(t.rules[6]!.if['min']).toBe(0 - d.density.noises.jag.clampSigma);
    expect(t.rules[7]!.if['t']).toBe(d.surface.snowline);
  });

  test('a negated ref of a target at 0 resolves to +0, never −0 (so the tree canonicalises)', () => {
    const p = paramsWith({ surface: { patchThreshold: 0 }, density: { detailAmpLo: 0 } });
    const src = seq(when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: -8, max: { param: 'surface.patchThreshold', neg: true } }, block('mud')),
      when({ kind: 'steep', min: { param: 'density.detailAmpLo', neg: true } }, block('stone')));
    const t = resolveRules(src, p);
    const zeros = numbers(t).filter((v) => v === 0);
    expect(zeros.length).toBe(2);
    for (const z of zeros) expect(Object.is(z, 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(() => canonicalJSON(t)).not.toThrow();
  });

  test('a fresh tree, deep-frozen at every depth; the source is neither changed nor frozen', () => {
    const src = SOURCE();
    const before = canonicalJSON(src);
    const t = resolveRules(src, P);
    expect(t).not.toBe(src);
    for (const c of containers(t)) expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
    expect(canonicalJSON(src)).toBe(before);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(src)).toBe(false);
    expect(() => { (t as unknown as { rules: unknown[] }).rules.push(block('stone')); }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { ((t as unknown as { rules: Array<{ if: Node }> }).rules[4]!.if)['min'] = 9; }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('the default source: the legacy tree at the defaults, from tier 2\'s memo (validated at most once, never again)', () => {
    const d = paramsWith();
    resolveRules(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, d);
    const n = rulesSourceValidations();
    const a = resolveRules(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, d), b = resolveRules(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, P);
    surfaceContextOf(ctxFor('42'));
    surfaceContextOf(ctxFor('42', { surface: { snowline: 0.5 } }));
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(n);
    expect(a).not.toBe(b);
    expect(canonicalJSON(a)).toBe(canonicalJSON(legacyDefaultSurfaceRules(d.surface)));
    expect(canonicalJSON(b)).toBe(canonicalJSON(legacyDefaultSurfaceRules(P.surface)));
    // An unfrozen source is validated on every call.
    const src = SOURCE();
    resolveRules(src, P);
    const m = rulesSourceValidations();
    resolveRules(src, P);
    expect(rulesSourceValidations()).toBe(m + 1);
  });

  test('an invalid source throws a RuleValidationError carrying tier 2\'s issues at their source paths', () => {
    const cases: ReadonlyArray<readonly [unknown, readonly string[]]> = [
      [block('air'), ['root.state NOT_SOLID']],
      [when({ kind: 'steep', min: { param: 'surface.nope' } }, block('stone')), ['root.if.min UNKNOWN_PARAM']],
      [when({ kind: 'yAbove', minY: { param: 'surface.cliffSteep' }, runTop: true }, block('stone')), ['root.if.minY PARAM_KIND']],
      [when({ kind: 'noiseThreshold', noise: 'surface.noises.patch', min: { param: 'surface.patchThreshold' }, max: { param: 'surface.patchThreshold' } }, block('mud')), ['root.if RANGE_ORDER']],
      [when({ kind: 'steep', min: { param: 'surface.cliffSteep', neg: false } }, block('stone')), ['root.if.min BAD_FIELD']],
    ];
    for (const [src, want] of cases) {
      let err: unknown;
      try { resolveRules(src, P); } catch (e) { err = e; }
      expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(RuleValidationError);
      expect((err as RuleValidationError).issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(want);
    }
  });

  test('a RuleValidationError carries tier 2\'s issue type', () => {
    expectTypeOf<RulesSourceIssue>().toExtend<RuleValidationIssue>();
    expectTypeOf<RuleValidationError['issues'][number]>().toEqualTypeOf<RuleValidationIssue>();
  });
});

describe('freezing (SP3d spec §1.6, D10): one frozen tree per SurfaceContext', () => {
  test('the default context: sc.rules, compiled.rules and reference.rules are one tree, frozen at every depth; mutating it throws', () => {
    const sc = createSurfaceContext(ctxFor('42'));
    expect(sc.compiled.rules).toBe(sc.rules);
    expect(sc.reference.rules).toBe(sc.rules);
    for (const c of containers(sc.rules)) expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
    const r = sc.rules as unknown as { rules: Array<{ then: { rules: Array<{ if: Node }> } }> };
    expect(() => { r.rules[1]!.then.rules[1]!.if['min'] = 0; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { r.rules.pop(); }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('an explicit tree is frozen in place (identity kept, values untouched), also when part of it was frozen already', () => {
    const tree = legacyDefaultSurfaceRules(paramsWith().surface) as unknown as { rules: Array<Node & { if: Node; then: Node }> };
    // A partly frozen tree: rule [2] frozen at its top only, its condition and block not.
    Object.freeze(tree.rules[2]!);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(tree.rules[2]!.if)).toBe(false);
    const before = canonicalJSON(tree);
    const sc = createSurfaceContext(ctxFor('42'), tree);
    expect(sc.rules).toBe(tree);
    expect(sc.compiled.rules).toBe(tree);
    expect(sc.reference.rules).toBe(tree);
    expect(canonicalJSON(tree)).toBe(before);
    for (const c of containers(tree)) expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
    expect(() => { tree.rules[2]!.if['falseAtAndAbove'] = 12; }).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => { tree.rules[0]!.then['state'] = 'stone'; }).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  test('the sp3c.surface.ops golden source is frozen in place and compiles as before', () => {
    const tree = surfaceOpsRules();
    const before = canonicalJSON(tree);
    const sc = createSurfaceContext(ctxFor('42'), tree);
    expect(sc.rules).toBe(tree);
    expect(canonicalJSON(sc.rules)).toBe(before);
    for (const c of containers(tree)) expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
  });

  test('freezeRules: shared and cyclic objects visited once; other values left alone; returns its argument', () => {
    const shared: Node = { kind: 'lake' };
    const t: Node = seq(when(shared, block('clay')), when(shared, block('mud')));
    expect(freezeRules(t)).toBe(t);
    for (const c of containers(t)) expect(Object.isFrozen(c)).toBe(true);
    const cyc: Node = { a: [] as unknown[] };
    (cyc['a'] as unknown[]).push(cyc);
    expect(freezeRules(cyc)).toBe(cyc);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(cyc) && Object.isFrozen(cyc['a'])).toBe(true);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(4);
    const holder: Node = { bytes };
    freezeRules(holder);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(holder)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(bytes)).toBe(false);
    expect(freezeRules(3)).toBe(3);
    expect(freezeRules(null)).toBe(null);
  });
});
```

```diff
+export function freezeRules<T>(tree: T): T {

+export function resolveRules(source: unknown, params: Params): Rule {
+  const issues = validateRulesSource(source);
+  if (issues.length > 0) throw new INVALID(issues);
+  return resolveNode(source, params) as Rule;
+}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import { columnPoint } from '../../src/gen/column/columnPoint';
import {
  buildColumnSample, buildCornerSample, gorgeAt, latticeIndex, LEVEL_FIELDS, newColumnSample, riverWetAt, SAMPLE_FIELDS,
  type ColumnSample, type SampleField,
} from '../../src/gen/column/columnStage';
import type { DensityExpr, Expr } from '../../src/gen/density/expr';
import { createDensityReference, type DensityReference } from '../../src/gen/density/reference';
import {
  colFieldsRead, CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS, createCornerSampler, horizontalCoord, horizontalSampling, readsSteep,
} from '../../src/gen/inspect/fieldSlice';
import { surfaceContextOf } from '../../src/gen/surface/context';
import { ctxFor } from '../harness/gen';
import { legacyDefaultDensityExpr } from '../harness/legacyTrees';
import { testRng } from '../harness/stats';

const ALL_FIELDS = [...SAMPLE_FIELDS, ...LEVEL_FIELDS] as const;
const col = (field: SampleField): Expr => ({ op: 'col', field });
const NO_NOISES = () => undefined;

/** Per field: the reference over `col f` (voxel placement, readField) and over `interpolated(col f)` (corner placement). */
const REFS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [SampleField, DensityReference, DensityReference]> = SAMPLE_FIELDS.map((f) => [
  f,
  createDensityReference({ root: col(f), defs: {} }, NO_NOISES),
  createDensityReference({ root: { op: 'interpolated', x: col(f) }, defs: {} }, NO_NOISES),
] as const);

/** 4,096 random voxels over the window: 256 random columns × 16 random voxels each (the full sample built once per column). */
function voxels(seed: number): Array<{ cx: number; cz: number; vs: Array<readonly [number, number, number]> }> {
  const next = testRng(seed);
  return Array.from({ length: 256 }, () => {
    const cx = (next() % 65536) - 32768;
    const cz = (next() % 65536) - 32768;
    const vs = Array.from({ length: 16 }, () => [16 * cx + (next() % 16), (next() % 384) - 64, 16 * cz + (next() % 16)] as const);
    return { cx, cz, vs };
  });
}

/** The quart corners (lattice i, j ∈ 0 … 4) the voxel at (x, z) reads: its cell's four. */
const cornersOf = (x: number, z: number): number[] => {
  const ci = (x & 15) >> 2;
  const cj = (z & 15) >> 2;
  return [latticeIndex(ci, cj), latticeIndex(ci + 1, cj), latticeIndex(ci, cj + 1), latticeIndex(ci + 1, cj + 1)];
};

describe('buildCornerSample (SP3d spec §4.4)', () => {
  const ctx = ctxFor('42');
  const cases = voxels(4411);

  test.each([[true], [false]])('withSteep %s: at 4,096 random voxels the reference reads equal the full sample\'s, except CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS', (withSteep) => {
    const full = newColumnSample();
    const corner = newColumnSample();
    const mismatched = new Set<string>();
    let compared = 0;
    for (const { cx, cz, vs } of cases) {
      buildColumnSample(ctx, cx, cz, full);
      for (const [x, y, z] of vs) {
        buildCornerSample(ctx, x, z, withSteep, corner);
        expect([corner.cx, corner.cz]).toEqual([cx, cz]);
        for (const [f, outside, inside] of REFS) {
          compared++;
          const a = outside.voxel(corner, x, y, z);
          const b = inside.voxel(corner, x, y, z);
          if (!withSteep && f === 'steep') {
            // Sampled without steep, the corners hold NaN: an expression that reads steep must take withSteep.
            expect(Number.isNaN(a) && Number.isNaN(b)).toBe(true);
            continue;
          }
          if (!Object.is(a, outside.voxel(full, x, y, z)) || !Object.is(b, inside.voxel(full, x, y, z))) mismatched.add(f);
        }
      }
    }
    expect(compared).toBe(4096 * SAMPLE_FIELDS.length);
    // The corner-vs-full rule: a field whose corner reads differ is read from a full ColumnSample instead.
    expect([...mismatched].sort()).toEqual([...CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS].sort());
  }, 60_000);

  test('the four corners hold the point values bit for bit (every field, flags, biome); every other entry is NaN or 0', () => {
    const s = newColumnSample();
    for (const { vs } of cases.slice(0, 16)) {
      for (const [x, , z] of vs) {
        buildCornerSample(ctx, x, z, true, s);
        const own = cornersOf(x, z);
        for (let j = -1; j <= 5; j++) for (let i = -1; i <= 5; i++) {
          const k = latticeIndex(i, j);
          if (own.includes(k)) {
            const p = columnPoint(ctx, 16 * s.cx + 4 * i, 16 * s.cz + 4 * j);
            for (const f of ALL_FIELDS) expect(Object.is(s.f[f][k], p[f])).toBe(true);
            expect([riverWetAt(s, k), gorgeAt(s, k), s.biome[k]]).toEqual([p.riverWet, p.gorge, p.biome]);
          } else {
            for (const f of ALL_FIELDS) expect(s.f[f][k]).toBeNaN();
            expect([s.flags[k], s.biome[k]]).toEqual([0, 0]);
          }
        }
      }
    }
  });

  test('a reused output is fully overwritten; a fresh one is made when none is passed', () => {
    const reused = buildCornerSample(ctx, 3, 5, true, buildColumnSample(ctx, 0, 0, newColumnSample()));
    const fresh = buildCornerSample(ctx, 3, 5, true);
    for (const f of ALL_FIELDS) for (let k = 0; k < 49; k++) expect(Object.is(reused.f[f][k], fresh.f[f][k])).toBe(true);
    expect([...reused.flags]).toEqual([...fresh.flags]);
    expect([...reused.biome]).toEqual([...fresh.biome]);
  });

  test('non-integer positions throw', () => {
    expect(() => buildCornerSample(ctx, 0.5, 0, false)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => buildCornerSample(ctx, 0, Number.NaN, false)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe('the per-part corner memo (createCornerSampler)', () => {
  const ctx = ctxFor('42');
  const same = (a: ColumnSample, b: ColumnSample): boolean => {
    if (a.cx !== b.cx || a.cz !== b.cz) return false;
    for (const f of ALL_FIELDS) for (let k = 0; k < 49; k++) if (!Object.is(a.f[f][k], b.f[f][k])) return false;
    for (let k = 0; k < 49; k++) if (a.flags[k] !== b.flags[k] || a.biome[k] !== b.biome[k]) return false;
    return true;
  };

  test.each([[false], [true]])('withSteep %s: memoised samples equal fresh ones bit for bit (extent 256, n = 32, two passes)', (withSteep) => {
    const sampler = createCornerSampler(ctx, withSteep);
    const fresh = newColumnSample();
    let differing = 0;
    for (let pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
      for (let j = 0; j < 32; j++) for (let i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
        const x = horizontalCoord(-3000, 256, i, 32);
        const z = horizontalCoord(1201, 256, j, 32);
        if (!same(sampler.sample(x, z), buildCornerSample(ctx, x, z, withSteep, fresh))) differing++;
      }
    }
    expect(differing).toBe(0);
  }, 30_000);

  test('a 128² slice at extent 256 makes 65,536 corner reads of 65² = 4,225 distinct points', () => {

describe('which samples an expression needs', () => {
  const steepDef: DensityExpr = { root: { op: 'add', a: { op: 'ref', name: 'a' }, b: col('E') }, defs: { a: { op: 'ref', name: 'b' }, b: { op: 'interpolated', x: col('steep') } } };
  test('colFieldsRead follows refs from the root only, through every child slot', () => {
    expect([...colFieldsRead(steepDef)].sort()).toEqual(['E', 'steep']);
    expect([...colFieldsRead({ root: col('jag'), defs: { unused: col('steep') } })]).toEqual(['jag']);
    const choice: Expr = { op: 'rangeChoice', x: col('C'), lo: 0, hi: 1, inside: col('W'), outside: { op: 'tap', name: 't', x: col('PV') } };
    expect([...colFieldsRead({ root: choice, defs: {} })].sort()).toEqual(['C', 'PV', 'W']);
    // Own-property lookups: a def named like an Object.prototype member.
    expect([...colFieldsRead({ root: { op: 'ref', name: 'constructor' }, defs: { constructor: col('T') } })]).toEqual(['T']);
  });
  test('readsSteep: through refs and interpolated; not from an unreachable def', () => {
    expect(readsSteep(steepDef)).toBe(true);
    expect(readsSteep({ root: col('offset'), defs: { unused: col('steep') } })).toBe(false);
    expect(readsSteep(legacyDefaultDensityExpr(DEFAULTS.density))).toBe(false);

  test('horizontalSampling: corner samples, with steep only when read, the full sample for a fallback field', () => {
    expect(horizontalSampling(legacyDefaultDensityExpr(DEFAULTS.density))).toBe('corner');
    expect(horizontalSampling(steepDef)).toBe('cornerSteep');
    for (const f of CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS) expect(horizontalSampling({ root: col(f), defs: {} })).toBe('full');
    expect(Object.isFrozen(CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS)).toBe(true);
  });

    let e: Expr = col('sigma');
    for (let i = 0; i < 100_000; i++) e = { op: 'neg', x: e };
    expect([...colFieldsRead({ root: e, defs: {} })]).toEqual(['sigma']);
```

```ts
    for (const s of [MOUNTAIN, DIAGONAL]) {
      expect(segmentPointAt(s, 0, n)).toEqual([s.ax, s.az]);
      expect(segmentPointAt(s, n - 1, n)).toEqual([s.bx, s.bz]);
      const i = n >> 1;
      expect(segmentPointAt(s, i, n)).toEqual([s.ax + (s.bx - s.ax) * (i / (n - 1)), s.az + (s.bz - s.az) * (i / (n - 1))]);
    }
  });
  test('the bounding-box clamp holds at every n (B the largest double below 2^19)', () => {
    const edge: Segment = { ax: -0.1, az: 0, bx: 524287.99999999994, bz: 0 };
    expect(segmentProblem(edge)).toBeNull();
    for (const n of SLICE_NS) expect(segmentPointAt(edge, n - 1, n)).toEqual([524287.99999999994, 0]);
  });
});

describe('vertical rows: y_r = 319 − ⌊(2r + 1)·384 / (2n)⌋', () => {
  test('row centres 318 … −63 at n = 128 and 313 … −59 at n = 32', () => {
    expect([sliceRowY(0, 128), sliceRowY(127, 128)]).toEqual([318, -63]);
    expect([sliceRowY(0, 32), sliceRowY(31, 32)]).toEqual([313, -59]);
  });
  test.each(SLICE_NS.map((n) => [n]))('n = %i: integers, strictly decreasing by 384/n, inside the world', (n) => {
    const ys = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, r) => sliceRowY(r, n));
    for (let r = 0; r < n; r++) {
      expect(Number.isInteger(ys[r])).toBe(true);
      expect(ys[r]).toBe(MAX_Y - Math.floor(((2 * r + 1) * HEIGHT) / (2 * n)));
      expect(ys[r]!).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MIN_Y);
      expect(ys[r]!).toBeLessThanOrEqual(MAX_Y);
      if (r > 0) expect(ys[r - 1]! - ys[r]!).toBe(HEIGHT / n);
    }
  });
  test('bad rows and sizes throw', () => {
    expect(() => sliceRowY(-1, 128)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceRowY(128, 128)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceRowY(1.5, 128)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceRowY(0, 64)).toThrow('n 64 is not a slice size (32, 128)');
  });
});

describe('horizontal coordinates: x_i = cx − E/2 + ⌊(2i + 1)·E / (2n)⌋', () => {
  test('ends and spacing', () => {
    expect([horizontalCoord(0, 256, 0, 128), horizontalCoord(0, 256, 127, 128)]).toEqual([-127, 127]);
    expect([horizontalCoord(0, 8192, 0, 128), horizontalCoord(0, 8192, 127, 128)]).toEqual([-4064, 4064]);
    expect([horizontalCoord(10, 2048, 0, 32), horizontalCoord(10, 2048, 31, 32)]).toEqual([10 - 1024 + 32, 10 + 1024 - 32]);
    expect([horizontalCoord(-7, 256, 0, 32), horizontalCoord(-7, 256, 1, 32)]).toEqual([-7 - 128 + 4, -7 - 128 + 12]);
  });
  test('integers for every allowed extent and size, evenly spaced E/n, strictly inside [c − E/2, c + E/2)', () => {
    for (const E of SLICE_EXTENTS) for (const n of SLICE_NS) for (const c of [0, -3, 524288 - E / 2, -524288 + E / 2]) {
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const x = horizontalCoord(c, E, i, n);
        expect(Number.isInteger(x)).toBe(true);
        expect(x).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(c - E / 2);
        expect(x).toBeLessThan(c + E / 2);
        if (i > 0) expect(x - horizontalCoord(c, E, i - 1, n)).toBe(E / n);
      }
    }
  });
  test('bad arguments throw', () => {
    expect(() => horizontalCoord(0, 300, 0, 128)).toThrow('extent 300 is not a slice extent (256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192)');
    expect(() => horizontalCoord(0, 256, 0, 16)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => horizontalCoord(0, 256, 128, 128)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => horizontalCoord(0.5, 256, 0, 128)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});

describe('the square must lie inside the world window', () => {
  test('the four edges at the limit pass, one block beyond refuses', () => {
    for (const E of SLICE_EXTENTS) {
      const h = E / 2;
      expect(squareProblem(-WINDOW_HALF + h, 0, E)).toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(WINDOW_HALF - h, 0, E)).toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(0, -WINDOW_HALF + h, E)).toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(0, WINDOW_HALF - h, E)).toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(-WINDOW_HALF + h - 1, 0, E)).not.toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(WINDOW_HALF - h + 1, 0, E)).not.toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(0, -WINDOW_HALF + h - 1, E)).not.toBeNull();
      expect(squareProblem(0, WINDOW_HALF - h + 1, E)).not.toBeNull();
    }
  });
  test('the messages', () => {
    expect(squareProblem(524161, 5, 256)).toBe('the square x [524033, 524289] × z [-123, 133] leaves the world window [-524288, 524288]');
    expect(squareProblem(0, -524200, 256)).toBe('the square x [-128, 128] × z [-524328, -524072] leaves the world window [-524288, 524288]');
    expect(squareProblem(0.5, 0, 256)).toBe('the centre (0.5, 0) is not a pair of integers');
    expect(squareProblem(0, Number.NaN, 256)).toBe('the centre (0, NaN) is not a pair of integers');
    expect(squareProblem(0, 0, 100)).toBe('extent 100 is not a slice extent (256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192)');
  });
  test('every sample of a square at the limit lies in the half-open window', () => {
    for (const E of SLICE_EXTENTS) for (const c of [-WINDOW_HALF + E / 2, WINDOW_HALF - E / 2]) {
      for (const i of [0, 127]) {
        const x = horizontalCoord(c, E, i, 128);
        expect(x >= -WINDOW_HALF && x < WINDOW_HALF).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });
});

describe('sample voxels of both planes', () => {
  const vertical = (s: Segment, n: number): SliceGeometry => ({ plane: 'vertical', n, pointAt: (i) => segmentPointAt(s, i, n) });
  test('vertical sample (i, r) = (⌊xᵢ⌋, y_r, ⌊zᵢ⌋), points injected', () => {
    for (const n of SLICE_NS) {
      const g = vertical(DIAGONAL, n);
      expect(sliceGeometryProblem(g)).toBeNull();
      for (const [i, r] of [[0, 0], [n - 1, n - 1], [n >> 1, 3], [5, n - 2]] as const) {
        const [px, pz] = segmentPointAt(DIAGONAL, i, n);
        expect(sliceSampleVoxel(g, i, r)).toEqual([Math.floor(px), sliceRowY(r, n), Math.floor(pz)]);
      }
    }
    // A non-integer point floors toward −∞, also below 0.
    const g: SliceGeometry = { plane: 'vertical', n: 32, pointAt: () => [-0.25, 7.75] };
    expect(sliceSampleVoxel(g, 3, 0)).toEqual([-1, 313, 7]);
  });
  test('horizontal sample (i, j) of sample column j = (x_i, y, z_j)', () => {
    const g: SliceGeometry = { plane: 'horizontal', n: 128, cx: 1000, cz: -2000, y: 63, extent: 2048 };
    expect(sliceGeometryProblem(g)).toBeNull();
    expect(sliceSampleVoxel(g, 0, 0)).toEqual([1000 - 1024 + 8, 63, -2000 - 1024 + 8]);
    expect(sliceSampleVoxel(g, 5, 127)).toEqual([horizontalCoord(1000, 2048, 127, 128), 63, horizontalCoord(-2000, 2048, 5, 128)]);
  });
  test('geometry problems', () => {
    expect(sliceGeometryProblem({ plane: 'vertical', n: 64, pointAt: () => [0, 0] })).toBe('n 64 is not a slice size (32, 128)');
    expect(sliceGeometryProblem({ plane: 'horizontal', n: 32, cx: 0, cz: 0, y: 320, extent: 256 })).toBe('y 320 is not an integer in [-64, 319]');
    expect(sliceGeometryProblem({ plane: 'horizontal', n: 32, cx: 0, cz: 0, y: 2.5, extent: 256 })).toBe('y 2.5 is not an integer in [-64, 319]');
    expect(sliceGeometryProblem({ plane: 'horizontal', n: 32, cx: 524288, cz: 0, y: 0, extent: 256 })).toBe(squareProblem(524288, 0, 256));
  });
  test('sample indices outside [0, n) and points outside the window throw', () => {
    const g = vertical(MOUNTAIN, 32);
    expect(() => sliceSampleVoxel(g, 32, 0)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceSampleVoxel(g, 0, -1)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceSampleVoxel({ plane: 'vertical', n: 32, pointAt: () => [524288, 0] }, 0, 0)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => sliceSampleVoxel({ plane: 'vertical', n: 32, pointAt: () => [Number.NaN, 0] }, 0, 0)).toThrow(RangeError);
  });
});
```

```diff
+/** A point at world (x, z) as `samplePoint` computes it; `buildCornerSample`'s injected source (a memo, for instance). */
+export type CornerPointSource = (x: number, z: number) => ColumnPoint;
+
+const POINT = NEW_POINT();
+const ALL_FIELDS: readonly (SampleField | LevelField)[] = [...SAMPLE_FIELDS, ...LEVEL_FIELDS];
+
+/**
+ * The corner sample of the voxel column at integer world (x, z) (SP3d spec §4.4): a ColumnSample of column
+ * (x >> 4, z >> 4) whose four quart corners around (x, z) — lattice (ci, cj), (ci + 1, cj), (ci, cj + 1),
+ * (ci + 1, cj + 1) with ci = (x & 15) >> 2, cj = (z & 15) >> 2, the corners `interpolated` and `readField` read at
+ * that voxel — hold the point values (`samplePoint`, equal to the lattice's bit for bit, DT2); every other entry
+ * is NaN (fields) or 0 (flags, biome). Steep is computed only `withSteep` (else NaN, whatever `pointAt` returns).
+ * `pointAt` replaces the direct `samplePoint` call (it must sample with steep when `withSteep`). Never touches a
+ * ColumnCache. Throws a RangeError for non-integer coordinates.
+ */
+export function buildCornerSample(
+  ctx: GenContext, x: number, z: number, withSteep: boolean, out: ColumnSample = newColumnSample(), pointAt?: CornerPointSource,
+): ColumnSample {
+  if (!Number.isInteger(x) || !Number.isInteger(z)) throw new RangeError(`corner sample: (${x}, ${z}) is not a pair of integers`);
+  const f = out.f;
+  for (const k of ALL_FIELDS) f[k].fill(Number.NaN);
+  out.flags.fill(0);
+  out.biome.fill(0);
+  const cx = x >> 4;
+  const cz = z >> 4;
+  const ci = (x & 15) >> 2;
+  const cj = (z & 15) >> 2;
+  out.cx = cx;
+  out.cz = cz;
+  for (let b = 0; b <= 1; b++) {
+    for (let a = 0; a <= 1; a++) {
+      const i = ci + a;
+      const j = cj + b;
+      const wx = 16 * cx + 4 * i;
+      const wz = 16 * cz + 4 * j;
+      const p = pointAt === undefined ? SAMPLE_POINT(ctx, wx, wz, withSteep, POINT) : pointAt(wx, wz);
+      const k = latticeIndex(i, j);
+      for (const name of ALL_FIELDS) f[name][k] = p[name];
+      if (!withSteep) f.steep[k] = Number.NaN;
+      out.flags[k] = (p.riverWet ? 1 : 0) | (p.gorge ? 2 : 0);
+      out.biome[k] = p.biome;
+    }
+  }
+  return out;
+}
```

Create `src/gen/inspect/fieldSlice.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The slice viewer's sample geometry and horizontal-plane samples (SP3d spec §4.2, §4.4, D16). The field evaluation
 * that uses them arrives with the slice job (§5.1).
 *
 * Geometry: a plane has n × n samples (n ∈ SLICE_NS), indexed (sample column, sample) — the pool splits by sample
 * columns. Vertical: sample column i is the line's point i, (xᵢ, zᵢ) = `segmentPointAt(segment, i, n)` of
 * `metrics/crossSection.ts`, which gen cannot import: the caller (the worker, the UI) injects it as `pointAt(i)` and
 * checks the segment with `segmentProblem`; sample r is the voxel (⌊xᵢ⌋, y_r, ⌊zᵢ⌋) with the row centre
 * y_r = 319 − ⌊(2r + 1) · 384 / (2n)⌋. Horizontal: sample column j is the row z_j, sample i the voxel (x_i, y, z_j),
 * x_i = cx − E/2 + ⌊(2i + 1) · E / (2n)⌋ (z_j alike), the square [cx − E/2, cx + E/2] × [cz − E/2, cz + E/2] inside
 * the world window [−2^19, 2^19] (every sample then lies in the half-open window).
 *
 * Horizontal samples read corner samples (`buildCornerSample`, `gen/column/columnStage.ts`): only the four quart corners
 * a voxel reads, never a ColumnCache entry; with steep only when the evaluated expression reads `col steep` (through
 * refs); memoised per part by lattice coordinate (`createCornerSampler`). A field whose corner reads are not
 * bit-identical to a full ColumnSample's is listed in CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS (none: pinned by a test at 4,096 random
 * voxels), and an expression that reads one takes full samples instead.
 *
 * Follows the gen determinism rules; every lookup keyed by tree content is own-property only.
 */
import { HEIGHT, MIN_Y, SLICE_EXTENTS, SLICE_NS } from '../../core/constants';
import { MAX_Y, WINDOW_HALF } from '../../core/coords';
import { newPointRecord, samplePoint, type ColumnPoint, type PointRecord } from '../column/columnPoint';
import { buildCornerSample, newColumnSample, type ColumnSample, type SampleField } from '../column/columnStage';
import type { GenContext } from '../context';
import { EXPR_CHILD_KEYS, type DensityExpr, type Expr } from '../density/expr';

const HEIGHT_ = HEIGHT;
const MIN_Y_ = MIN_Y;
const MAX_Y_ = MAX_Y;
const W = WINDOW_HALF;
const NS = SLICE_NS;
const EXTENTS = SLICE_EXTENTS;
const SAMPLE_POINT = samplePoint;
const NEW_POINT = newPointRecord;
const CORNER_SAMPLE = buildCornerSample;
const NEW_SAMPLE = newColumnSample;
const CHILD_KEYS = EXPR_CHILD_KEYS;

/** A line point (xᵢ, zᵢ) in blocks. */
export type SlicePoint = readonly [x: number, z: number];

/** A vertical plane along A → B: `pointAt(i)` = `segmentPointAt(segment, i, n)` for a segment without a problem. */
export interface VerticalSliceGeometry {
  readonly plane: 'vertical';
  readonly n: number;
  readonly pointAt: (i: number) => SlicePoint;
}
/** A horizontal XZ plane at y, centred on (cx, cz), of side `extent` blocks. */
export interface HorizontalSliceGeometry {
  readonly plane: 'horizontal';
  readonly n: number;
  readonly cx: number;
  readonly cz: number;
  readonly y: number;
  readonly extent: number;
}
export type SliceGeometry = VerticalSliceGeometry | HorizontalSliceGeometry;

const nProblem = (n: number): string | null => ((NS as readonly number[]).includes(n) ? null : `n ${n} is not a slice size (${NS.join(', ')})`);
const extentProblem = (e: number): string | null => ((EXTENTS as readonly number[]).includes(e) ? null : `extent ${e} is not a slice extent (${EXTENTS.join(', ')})`);

function checkN(n: number): void {
  const p = nProblem(n);
  if (p !== null) throw new RangeError(p);
}
function checkIndex(v: number, n: number, what: string): void {
  if (!Number.isInteger(v) || v < 0 || v >= n) throw new RangeError(`${what} ${v} is outside [0, ${n})`);
}

/** Row r's y on a vertical plane of n rows: 319 − ⌊(2r + 1) · 384 / (2n)⌋ (318 … −63 at n = 128, 313 … −59 at 32). */
export function sliceRowY(r: number, n: number): number {
  checkN(n);
  checkIndex(r, n, 'row');
  return MAX_Y_ - Math.floor(((2 * r + 1) * HEIGHT_) / (2 * n));
}

/** Coordinate i of a horizontal plane's axis centred on c of side `extent`: c − E/2 + ⌊(2i + 1) · E / (2n)⌋, an integer. */
export function horizontalCoord(c: number, extent: number, i: number, n: number): number {
  const e = extentProblem(extent);
  if (e !== null) throw new RangeError(e);
  checkN(n);
  checkIndex(i, n, 'sample');
  if (!Number.isInteger(c)) throw new RangeError(`centre ${c} is not an integer`);
  return c - extent / 2 + Math.floor(((2 * i + 1) * extent) / (2 * n));
}

/**
 * Why a horizontal square has no slice, or null: an integer centre, an extent of SLICE_EXTENTS, and the square inside
 * the world window: cx − E/2 ≥ −2^19 and cx + E/2 ≤ 2^19, and the same for z. The worker refuses with this text; the UI
 * clamps the centre first.
 */
export function squareProblem(cx: number, cz: number, extent: number): string | null {
  if (!Number.isInteger(cx) || !Number.isInteger(cz)) return `the centre (${cx}, ${cz}) is not a pair of integers`;
  const e = extentProblem(extent);
  if (e !== null) return e;
  const h = extent / 2;
  if (cx - h < -W || cx + h > W || cz - h < -W || cz + h > W) {
    return `the square x [${cx - h}, ${cx + h}] × z [${cz - h}, ${cz + h}] leaves the world window [${-W}, ${W}]`;
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Why a plane has no slice, or null: n ∈ SLICE_NS; horizontal: y an integer in [−64, 319] and `squareProblem`.
 * A vertical plane's segment is the caller's to check (`segmentProblem`), since its points are injected.
 */
export function sliceGeometryProblem(g: SliceGeometry): string | null {
  const n = nProblem(g.n);
  if (n !== null) return n;
  if (g.plane === 'vertical') return null;
  if (!Number.isInteger(g.y) || g.y < MIN_Y_ || g.y > MAX_Y_) return `y ${g.y} is not an integer in [${MIN_Y_}, ${MAX_Y_}]`;
  return squareProblem(g.cx, g.cz, g.extent);
}

/**
 * The voxel [x, y, z] of sample `k` of sample column `c` (both in [0, n)): vertical (⌊x_c⌋, y_k, ⌊z_c⌋), horizontal
 * (x_k, y, z_c). Throws a RangeError for indices outside [0, n), a bad n or extent, or a vertical point whose voxel
 * lies outside the half-open world window.
 */
export function sliceSampleVoxel(g: SliceGeometry, c: number, k: number): [number, number, number] {
  checkN(g.n);
  checkIndex(c, g.n, 'sample column');
  checkIndex(k, g.n, 'sample');
  if (g.plane === 'horizontal') return [horizontalCoord(g.cx, g.extent, k, g.n), g.y, horizontalCoord(g.cz, g.extent, c, g.n)];
  const [px, pz] = g.pointAt(c);
  const x = Math.floor(px);
  const z = Math.floor(pz);
  if (!(x >= -W && x < W && z >= -W && z < W)) throw new RangeError(`point (${px}, ${pz}) is outside the world window [${-W}, ${W})`);
  return [x, sliceRowY(k, g.n), z];
}

/**
 * The ColumnSample fields whose corner-sample reads are not bit-identical to a full ColumnSample's (§4.4): none. A
 * test compares every field at 4,096 random voxels and pins this list; an expression reading one of them is sampled
 * with full ColumnSamples on horizontal planes.
 */
export const CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS: readonly SampleField[] = Object.freeze([]);
const FALLBACK: ReadonlySet<SampleField> = new Set(CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS);

/**
 * The `col` fields an expression reads: the nodes reachable from the root through every child slot and through refs
 * (each def entered once; a def unreachable from the root is not read). Iterative; refs resolved by own property; a
 * ref to a missing def reads nothing.
 */
export function colFieldsRead(expr: DensityExpr): ReadonlySet<SampleField> {
  const out = new Set<SampleField>();
  const entered = new Set<string>();
  const seen = new Set<Expr>();
  const stack: Expr[] = [expr.root];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const e = stack.pop()!;
    if (seen.has(e)) continue;
    seen.add(e);
    if (e.op === 'col') out.add(e.field);
    else if (e.op === 'ref') {
      if (!entered.has(e.name) && Object.hasOwn(expr.defs, e.name)) {
        entered.add(e.name);
        stack.push(expr.defs[e.name]!);
      }
    } else {
      const rec = e as unknown as Readonly<Record<string, Expr>>;
      const keys = CHILD_KEYS[e.op];
      for (let i = keys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push(rec[keys[i]!]!);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Whether the expression reads `col steep` (through refs): its corner samples need steep (§4.4). */
export function readsSteep(expr: DensityExpr): boolean {
  return colFieldsRead(expr).has('steep');
}

/** How a horizontal plane samples an expression's columns: corner samples (with steep or not) or full ColumnSamples. */
export type HorizontalSampling = 'corner' | 'cornerSteep' | 'full';

/** The corner-vs-full rule (§4.4): full samples when the expression reads a CORNER_FALLBACK_FIELDS field. */
export function horizontalSampling(expr: DensityExpr): HorizontalSampling {
  const fields = colFieldsRead(expr);
  for (const f of fields) if (FALLBACK.has(f)) return 'full';
  return fields.has('steep') ? 'cornerSteep' : 'corner';
}

/** A per-part source of corner samples with its point memo. */
export interface CornerSampler {
  /** The corner sample of the voxel column at integer (x, z); the returned object is reused by the next call. */
  sample(x: number, z: number): ColumnSample;
  /** Distinct quart points computed so far. */
  readonly points: number;
}

/** Quart coordinates lie in [−2^17, 2^17]: offset and packed into one numeric key below 2^38. */
const Q_OFFSET = 131072;
const Q_SPAN = 524288;

/**
 * Corner samples for one part (§4.4): each quart point (world x, z multiples of 4) is computed once, by `samplePoint`
 * with or without steep, and kept in a Map by lattice coordinate, so neighbouring samples share it. The values are
 * those `buildCornerSample` computes without the memo, bit for bit.
 */
export function createCornerSampler(ctx: GenContext, withSteep: boolean): CornerSampler {
  const memo = new Map<number, PointRecord>();
  const out = NEW_SAMPLE();
  const pointAt = (x: number, z: number): ColumnPoint => {
    const key = (x / 4 + Q_OFFSET) * Q_SPAN + (z / 4 + Q_OFFSET);
    let p = memo.get(key);
    if (p === undefined) {
      p = SAMPLE_POINT(ctx, x, z, withSteep, NEW_POINT());
      memo.set(key, p);
    }
    return p;
  };
  return {
    sample: (x, z) => CORNER_SAMPLE(ctx, x, z, withSteep, out, pointAt),
    get points() { return memo.size; },
  };
}
```

```diff
- * overshoot never leaves the window.
+ * Point i (0 … n − 1) of n points of the segment, A and B included: A + (B − A) · i/(n − 1), kept within the segment's

   const z = s.az + (s.bz - s.az) * t;
   return [Math.min(Math.max(x, Math.min(s.ax, s.bx)), Math.max(s.ax, s.bx)), Math.min(Math.max(z, Math.min(s.az, s.bz)), Math.max(s.az, s.bz))];
```

```ts
/**
 * The session's tier-2 validation hook and its hashed history keys (SP3d spec §1.8 session part, §1.12),
 * with fake validators: the real `validateParamTrees` is wired by the pages (SP3d Task 15).
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { fnv1a64, hex64, type Seed64 } from '../../src/core/hash';
import { canonicalJSON } from '../../src/core/params/canonical';
import type { Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { resolveProfile } from '../../src/core/params/profiles';
import type { Params } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { draftKeyOf, WorldSession, type ParamsValidator } from '../../src/engine/session';

const random = (): Seed64 => [7, 1];
const TREE_ISSUE: Issue = { path: 'density.defs.root.b.x', code: 'UNKNOWN_OP', message: 'unknown op bogus' };
const issuesOf = (r: { ok: boolean; issues?: readonly Issue[] }) => (r.ok ? [] : r.issues!.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`));

/** A fake tier 2: refuses params whose `climate.scaleMul` is in `bad`, and logs every document it sees. */
function fake(bad: readonly number[], issue: Issue = TREE_ISSUE): { validate: ParamsValidator; seen: Params[] } {
  const seen: Params[] = [];
  const validate: ParamsValidator = (p) => {
    seen.push(p);
    return bad.includes(p.climate.scaleMul) ? [issue] : [];
  };
  return { validate, seen };
}

const notifications = (w: WorldSession) => {
  const log: string[] = [];
  w.subscribe((_s, c) => log.push(c.kind));
  return log;
};

describe('validateParams: the constructor', () => {
  test('issues take the invalid-patch branch: the default profile, no changes, the notice names the first issue', () => {
    const { validate, seen } = fake([2]);
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { seedText: 'x', profile: 'large_biomes', patch: { climate: { scaleMul: 2 } }, validateParams: validate });
    expect([w.state.profile, w.state.patch, w.state.seedText, w.state.epoch]).toEqual(['default', {}, 'x', 0]);
    expect(w.state.params).toBe(resolveProfile('default'));
    expect(w.initNotice).toBe('invalid patch (density.defs.root.b.x UNKNOWN_OP); opened the default profile with no changes');
    expect(seen.map((p) => p.climate.scaleMul)).toEqual([2]);
    expect([w.canUndo, w.canRedo]).toEqual([false, false]);
  });
  test('an issue at the empty path is named <root>', () => {
    const { validate } = fake([1], { path: '', code: 'NOT_OBJECT', message: 'x' });
    expect(new WorldSession(random, { validateParams: validate }).initNotice).toBe('invalid patch (<root> NOT_OBJECT); opened the default profile with no changes');
  });
  test('accepted params open as given; the validator sees exactly the patched document', () => {
    const { validate, seen } = fake([2]);
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { seedText: '1', profile: 'large_biomes', patch: { climate: { scaleMul: 3 } }, validateParams: validate });
    expect([w.state.profile, w.state.patch, w.initNotice]).toEqual(['large_biomes', { climate: { scaleMul: 3 } }, null]);
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(seen[0]).toBe(w.state.params);
  });
  test('a patch that applyPatch refuses keeps its own notice and never reaches the validator', () => {
    const { validate, seen } = fake([]);
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { patch: { nope: 1 }, validateParams: validate });
    expect(w.initNotice).toBe('invalid patch (nope UNKNOWN_KEY); opened the default profile with no changes');
    expect(seen).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('validateParams: setProfile, commits and load refuse; nothing changes', () => {
  test('setProfile refuses a profile whose params fail (large_biomes: scaleMul 4), with the issues; no step, no notification', () => {
    const issue: Issue = { path: 'surface.rules.root.rules[2].then', code: 'NOT_SOLID', message: 'air' };

    const { validate, seen } = fake([]);
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { seedText: '1', validateParams: validate });
    seen.length = 0;
    w.setSeedText('2');
    w.newSeed();
    expect([w.state.seedText, seen.length]).toEqual(['4294967303', 0]);
  });
});

describe('validateParams: restore', () => {
  test('undo and redo validate the snapshot; a refusal is a bug and throws', () => {
    let bad: number[] = [];
    const validate: ParamsValidator = (p) => (bad.includes(p.climate.scaleMul) ? [TREE_ISSUE] : []);
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { seedText: '1', validateParams: validate });
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 2);
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 3);
    expect(w.undo() && w.state.params.climate.scaleMul).toBe(2);
    expect(w.redo() && w.state.params.climate.scaleMul).toBe(3);
    bad = [2];
    expect(() => w.undo()).toThrow('history snapshot no longer loads: density.defs.root.b.x UNKNOWN_OP');
  });
});

describe('hashed history keys (SP3d spec §1.12)', () => {
  test('draftKeyOf is fnv1a64 of the snapshot canonical text, 16 hex digits', () => {
    const snap = { seedText: '42', profile: 'default' as const, patch: { climate: { scaleMul: 2 } } };
    const text = canonicalJSON({ seedText: '42', profile: 'default', patch: { climate: { scaleMul: 2 } } });
    expect(draftKeyOf(snap)).toBe(hex64(fnv1a64(text)));
    expect(draftKeyOf(snap)).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/);
    expect(draftKeyOf({ ...snap, patch: { climate: { scaleMul: 3 } } })).not.toBe(draftKeyOf(snap));
    expect(draftKeyOf({ ...snap, seedText: '042' })).not.toBe(draftKeyOf(snap));
    expect(draftKeyOf({ ...snap, profile: 'large_biomes' })).not.toBe(draftKeyOf(snap));
  });
  test('undo, redo and the redo tail work on the hashed keys', () => {
    const w = new WorldSession(random, { seedText: '1' });
    for (const v of [2, 3, 4]) w.set('climate.scaleMul', v);
    expect(w.undo() && w.undo() && w.state.params.climate.scaleMul).toBe(2);
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 2);
    expect([w.canUndo, w.canRedo]).toEqual([true, true]);
    w.beginGesture();
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 3.5);
    expect([w.canUndo, w.canRedo]).toEqual([true, false]);
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 2);
    w.endGesture();
    expect(w.redo() && w.state.params.climate.scaleMul).toBe(3);
    w.set('climate.scaleMul', 5);
    expect([w.canRedo, w.undo() && w.state.params.climate.scaleMul]).toEqual([false, 3]);
    expect(w.undo() && w.undo() && [w.state.params.climate.scaleMul, w.canUndo]).toEqual([1, false]);
  });
});
```

  - `src/ui/map/mapState.ts`: `MAP_HASH_READ_MAX = 1048576`; `decodeMapState` returns `{state: DEFAULT_MAP_STATE, error: 'map URL ignored: too long (<n> characters, limit 1048576)'}` for a text (after `#`) longer than it, before `base64urlDecode`.
  — cost if wrong: renames in Tasks 14, 15, 28.
- Ruling: the session keeps one key, the hash: `draftKey` (the draft's change test in `write`) and `HistoryEntry.key` (the cursor comparison) are both `draftKeyOf`, so the full canonical text is never stored; a 64-bit collision would drop one edit as "unchanged" (2^-64 per pair) — cost if wrong: keep the text for `write`'s exact test (one 256 KiB string, not 101).
- Ruling: the URL cap is measured at flush time (when the debounced write happens), on the hash text in characters (base64url is ASCII); an oversize URL is dropped (no retry), `onOversize` fires on transitions only (true on the first dropped URL, false on the next one that fits), and a value superseded inside the debounce is never measured. `noiseLab.ts` passes no callback: a lab URL above 64 KiB is silently not written (the lab accepts tier-1 trees in its B patch after Task 14; no notice there) — cost if wrong: a lab notice later.
- Ruling: constants placement — `URL_HASH_MAX`/`URL_OVERSIZE_NOTICE` in `ui/common/urlWriter.ts` and `MAP_HASH_READ_MAX` in `ui/map/mapState.ts` (UI-only numbers; no other layer reads them), not `core/constants.ts` — cost if wrong: a move.
- Ruling: tests in a new file `test/unit/sessionValidation.test.ts` (hook and hashed keys, fake validators keyed on `climate.scaleMul`; no json leaf exists before Task 14) plus cases appended to `urlWriter.test.ts` and `mapState.test.ts`; `session.test.ts` and every engine test keep constructing sessions without the option (unchanged) — cost if wrong: none.
- MEASUREMENT: `hex64(fnv1a64(text))` on a 262,144-character ASCII string (two trees at the 128 KiB cap) = 4.7 ms median of 30; of it `utf8Bytes` = 3.5 ms, `fnv1a64Bytes` = 1.2 ms (`fnv1a32` over the same string 3.5 ms; a string `===` 0.07 ms) (`node --experimental-strip-types` probe over `src/core/hash.ts`, not committed; load average 5.4-5.8 at the time: another chain was running). RISK for Task 28: `session.commitMaxTree`'s gate is p50 ≤ 4 ms and `draftKeyOf` alone costs about that on a capped draft; if the bench fails, the cheapest fix is an ASCII fast path in `fnv1a64` (hash char codes < 0x80 directly, no byte array; same hash value) or per-tree cached hashes in the canonical cache — not done here (the gate belongs to Task 28).
- No spec defects found for Task 12. No Green-on-parent file (single tests inside the files pass on the parent — the applyPatch-first, seed-change, hashed-undo and superseded-oversize cases — but each file fails). No file of another chain touched (`mapPage.ts` not edited).

Create `test/unit/clickAction.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { mapClickAction, type MapClick, type MapClickAction, type SlicePlane } from '../../src/ui/map/clickAction';
import type { DrawerTabId } from '../../src/ui/map/layout';

const PIN: MapClickAction = { kind: 'pin' };
const SECTION: MapClickAction = { kind: 'openSection' };
const CENTRE: MapClickAction = { kind: 'centre' };
const CUT_OPENS: MapClickAction = { kind: 'cut', openSection: true };
const CUT_KEEPS: MapClickAction = { kind: 'cut', openSection: false };

describe('mapClickAction (SP3d spec §3.7): the routing of a map click', () => {
  // Every (drawerTab, plane, nearLine, cutArmed); drawerTab null = the drawer is closed. Density is "shown" only
  // while the drawer is open on its tab.
  const cases: ReadonlyArray<readonly [DrawerTabId | null, SlicePlane, boolean, boolean, MapClickAction]> = [
    // The drawer closed, or open on Spline or Cross-section: today's routing, whatever the Density plane.
    [null, 'vertical', false, false, PIN], [null, 'vertical', true, false, SECTION],
    [null, 'vertical', false, true, CUT_OPENS], [null, 'vertical', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    [null, 'horizontal', false, false, PIN], [null, 'horizontal', true, false, SECTION],
    [null, 'horizontal', false, true, CUT_OPENS], [null, 'horizontal', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    ['spline', 'vertical', false, false, PIN], ['spline', 'vertical', true, false, SECTION],
    ['spline', 'vertical', false, true, CUT_OPENS], ['spline', 'vertical', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    ['spline', 'horizontal', false, false, PIN], ['spline', 'horizontal', true, false, SECTION],
    ['spline', 'horizontal', false, true, CUT_OPENS], ['spline', 'horizontal', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    ['section', 'vertical', false, false, PIN], ['section', 'vertical', true, false, SECTION],
    ['section', 'vertical', false, true, CUT_OPENS], ['section', 'vertical', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    ['section', 'horizontal', false, false, PIN], ['section', 'horizontal', true, false, SECTION],
    ['section', 'horizontal', false, true, CUT_OPENS], ['section', 'horizontal', true, true, CUT_OPENS],
    // Density shown: a finished cut line keeps Density shown; a click near the line does not open Cross-section;
    // on the horizontal plane a plain click sets the plane's centre instead of the pin.
    ['density', 'vertical', false, false, PIN], ['density', 'vertical', true, false, PIN],
    ['density', 'vertical', false, true, CUT_KEEPS], ['density', 'vertical', true, true, CUT_KEEPS],
    ['density', 'horizontal', false, false, CENTRE], ['density', 'horizontal', true, false, CENTRE],
    ['density', 'horizontal', false, true, CUT_KEEPS], ['density', 'horizontal', true, true, CUT_KEEPS],
  ];

  test('the table covers every combination once', () => {
    const keys = new Set(cases.map(([d, p, n, c]) => `${String(d)} ${p} ${n} ${c}`));
    expect(keys.size).toBe(cases.length);
    expect(cases).toHaveLength(4 * 2 * 2 * 2);
  });

  test.each(cases)('drawer %s, plane %s, near the line %s, cut armed %s', (drawerTab, plane, nearLine, cutArmed, want) => {
    const click: MapClick = { drawerTab, plane, nearLine, cutArmed };
    expect(mapClickAction(click)).toEqual(want);
  });
});
```

Create `src/ui/map/clickAction.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The routing of a map click (SP3d spec §3.7), pure and unit-tested. Today's rules (SP2b spec §4.5) hold while
 * the Density tab is not shown: an armed cut tool takes the click, and a finished line opens the Cross-section
 * tab; a click near the line opens Cross-section; any other click sets the pin. While Density is shown (the drawer
 * open on its tab) a finished cut line keeps Density shown (it only sets the line its vertical plane follows), a
 * click near the line does not open Cross-section, and on the horizontal plane a click that is not the cut tool's
 * sets the plane's centre instead of the pin.
 */
import type { DrawerTabId } from './layout';

/** The Density tab's slice plane (SP3d spec §4.2): along the cut line, or XZ at a y. */
export type SlicePlane = 'vertical' | 'horizontal';

export interface MapClick {
  /** The drawer tab on screen; null while the drawer is closed. */
  readonly drawerTab: DrawerTabId | null;
  /** The Density tab's plane (it matters only while Density is shown). */
  readonly plane: SlicePlane;
  /** The click is within the hit distance of the cut line (false when there is no line). */
  readonly nearLine: boolean;
  /** The cut-line tool waits for A or B. */
  readonly cutArmed: boolean;
}

export type MapClickAction =
  /** The cut tool takes the click; a line it finishes opens the Cross-section tab when `openSection`. */
  | { readonly kind: 'cut'; readonly openSection: boolean }
  /** Open the drawer on the Cross-section tab. */
  | { readonly kind: 'openSection' }
  /** Set the horizontal plane's centre. */
  | { readonly kind: 'centre' }
  /** Set the pin. */
  | { readonly kind: 'pin' };

export function mapClickAction(c: MapClick): MapClickAction {
  const density = c.drawerTab === 'density';
  if (c.cutArmed) return { kind: 'cut', openSection: !density };
  if (density) return c.plane === 'horizontal' ? { kind: 'centre' } : { kind: 'pin' };
  return c.nearLine ? { kind: 'openSection' } : { kind: 'pin' };
}
```

Create `test/unit/fixtures/editedTrees.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Edited trees of the two `json` leaves for the SP3d tests (spec §1.8 invariant, §1.11 round trips, §6 uiSmoke, §7 U2):
 * plain mutable copies of the defaults with the edits named below. Each call returns a fresh copy.
 */
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import type { ParamsPatch } from '../../../src/core/params/schema';

// Test-only JSON plumbing: the trees are walked by key, so `any` keeps the edits short.
type Tree = Record<string, any>;

const copy = (v: unknown): Tree => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v)) as Tree;

/** The default density tree (a mutable copy). Its terrain tap is `root.a.a`, its islands tap `root.b`. */
export const densityTree = (): Tree => copy(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
/** The default rule tree (a mutable copy). Its deepslate gradient is the condition `rules[2].if`. */
export const rulesTree = (): Tree => copy(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES);

/** uiSmoke step 2 (spec §6): the islands const edited from −1e6 to −10. */
export function islandsAt(v: number): Tree {
  const t = densityTree();
  t['root'].b.x.v = v;
  return t;
}

/** uiSmoke step 3 and U2's density variant (spec §6, §7): the terrain tap muted to `mute`. */
export function terrainMuted(mute = 0): Tree {
  const t = densityTree();
  t['root'].a.a.mute = mute;
  return t;
}

/** U2's rules variant (spec §7): the deepslate gradient's `falseAtAndAbove` 8 → `top`. */
export function gradientTop(top = 12): Tree {
  const t = rulesTree();
  t['rules'][2].if.falseAtAndAbove = top;
  return t;
}

/**
 * Spec §1.11's edited density tree: a def `lift` (2 · detailAmpLo through a `param` node) referenced by the islands tap,
 * the terrain tap muted to 0.5, and the detail amplitude's clamp with a negated ref as its lower bound.
 */
export function editedDensity(): Tree {
  const t = densityTree();
  t['defs'] = { lift: { op: 'mul', a: { op: 'const', v: 2 }, b: { op: 'param', path: 'density.detailAmpLo' } } };
  t['root'].b.x = { op: 'add', a: { op: 'ref', name: 'lift' }, b: { op: 'const', v: -1000000 } };
  t['root'].a.a.mute = 0.5;
  const clamp = t['root'].a.b.b.b.b;
  if (clamp.op !== 'clamp') throw new Error('the default density tree moved: no clamp at root.a.b.b.b.b');
  clamp.lo = { param: 'density.detailAmpLo', neg: true };
  return t;
}

/** Spec §1.11's edited rule tree: the gradient top 8 → 12 and the cliff steepness read negated (−cliffSteep ≤ steep). */
export function editedRules(): Tree {
  const t = gradientTop(12);
  const steep = findKind(t, 'steep');
  steep.min = { param: 'surface.cliffSteep', neg: true };
  return t;
}

/** The first node of `kind` in DFS order (rules, then, if, …). */
export function findKind(t: unknown, kind: string): Tree {
  const stack: unknown[] = [t];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const v = stack.pop();
    if (typeof v !== 'object' || v === null) continue;
    if (!Array.isArray(v) && (v as Tree)['kind'] === kind) return v as Tree;
    const children = Array.isArray(v) ? v : Object.values(v);
    for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push(children[i]);
  }
  throw new Error(`no ${kind} node`);
}

/** Both trees edited (spec §1.11), as a patch over the default profile. */
export const editedPatch = (): ParamsPatch => ({ density: { defs: editedDensity() }, surface: { rules: editedRules() } }) as ParamsPatch;

/**
 * A density tree at tier 1's depth bound (spec §1.7): its top object is container depth 1, `root` 2, and a chain of
 * `neg` nodes ends in the `y` node at container depth `depth`.
 */
export function deepDensity(depth = 48): Tree {
  let node: Tree = { op: 'y' };
  for (let d = depth - 1; d >= 2; d--) node = { op: 'neg', x: node };
  return { root: node, defs: {} };
}

/**
 * A rule tree of container depth `depth` (48: tier 1's bound): nested one-child sequences (2 levels each) around an
 * empty sequence (depth 2) or, for an odd depth, a sequence holding one block (depth 3).
 */
export function deepRules(depth = 48): Tree {
  let node: Tree = depth % 2 === 0 ? { kind: 'sequence', rules: [] } : { kind: 'sequence', rules: [{ kind: 'block', state: 'stone' }] };
  for (let d = depth % 2 === 0 ? 2 : 3; d < depth; d += 2) node = { kind: 'sequence', rules: [node] };
  return node;
}

/** Container depth of a JSON value (its top container 1; a primitive 0). */
export function jsonDepth(v: unknown): number {
  if (typeof v !== 'object' || v === null) return 0;
  let max = 0;
  for (const c of Array.isArray(v) ? v : Object.values(v)) max = Math.max(max, jsonDepth(c));
  return max + 1;
}
```

Create `test/unit/paramTrees.test.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The two `json` leaves of SP3d (spec §1.2, §1.7, §1.8, D3): `validateParamTrees` and its leaf-prefixed paths, the
 * defaults invariant (every profile, the U2 variants and the uiSmoke trees pass both tiers), the contexts reading the
 * leaves, and a depth-48 tree through every canonical wrapper.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { canonicalJSON } from '../../src/core/params/canonical';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import { applyPatch, renderReference, type Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { exportPreset, importPreset } from '../../src/core/params/presets';
import { PROFILE_IDS, resolveProfile } from '../../src/core/params/profiles';
import { SCHEMA, type Params, type ParamsPatch } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { paramsHash, stageHashes } from '../../src/core/stage/hash';
import { STAGES } from '../../src/core/stage/registry';
import { draftKeyOf } from '../../src/engine/session';
import { createDensityContext } from '../../src/gen/density/context';
import { ExprValidationError } from '../../src/gen/density/expr';
import { densitySourceValidations } from '../../src/gen/density/source';
import { createSurfaceContext, surfaceContextOf } from '../../src/gen/surface/context';
import { RuleValidationError } from '../../src/gen/surface/rules';
import { rulesSourceValidations } from '../../src/gen/surface/source';
import { validateParamTrees } from '../../src/gen/trees';
import { perturbations } from '../../src/metrics/liveness';
import { decodeLabState, DEFAULT_LAB_STATE, encodeLabState } from '../../src/ui/lab/labState';
import { decodeMapState, DEFAULT_MAP_STATE, encodeMapState } from '../../src/ui/map/mapState';
import { ctxFor, paramsWith } from '../harness/gen';
import {
  deepDensity, deepRules, densityTree, editedDensity, editedRules, findKind, gradientTop, islandsAt, jsonDepth, rulesTree, terrainMuted,
} from './fixtures/editedTrees';

const brief = (issues: readonly Issue[]) => issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`);
const trees = (density: unknown = DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, rules: unknown = DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES): Params =>
  paramsWith({ density: { defs: density }, surface: { rules } } as ParamsPatch);
const leafInfo = (path: string) => SCHEMA.leaves.find((l) => l.path === path)!;

describe('the two leaves (SP3d spec §1.2)', () => {
  test('defaults are the registered default trees, kept by identity through applyPatch, checkParams and resolveProfile', () => {
    expect(DEFAULTS.density.defs).toBe(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
    expect(DEFAULTS.surface.rules).toBe(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES);
    expect(paramsWith({ climate: { scaleMul: 2 } }).density.defs).toBe(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
    for (const id of PROFILE_IDS) expect(resolveProfile(id).surface.rules, id).toBe(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES);
  });

  test('the README rows: `<format> tree, <n> nodes`, no range; scope terrain', () => {
    const rows = renderReference(SCHEMA).split('\n');
    expect(rows.find((r) => r.startsWith('| `density.defs` |'))).toMatch(/^\| `density\.defs` \| json \| density tree, 60 nodes \|  \|  \| terrain \| Density expression: /);
    expect(rows.find((r) => r.startsWith('| `surface.rules` |'))).toMatch(/^\| `surface\.rules` \| json \| surfaceRules tree, 163 nodes \|  \|  \| terrain \| Surface rules: /);
  });

  test('an edited tree is tier 1\'s frozen clone: a patch with the same registered value keeps it', () => {
    const p = trees(islandsAt(-10));
    const tree = p.density.defs;
    expect(Object.isFrozen(tree)).toBe(true);
    expect(tree).not.toBe(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
    const again = applyPatch(SCHEMA, p, { climate: { scaleMul: 2 } });
    expect(again.ok && again.value.density.defs).toBe(tree);
  });
});

describe('validateParamTrees (spec §1.8, D3)', () => {
  test('the defaults have no issue, and a document whose trees are unchanged validates from the memos', () => {
    expect(validateParamTrees(DEFAULTS)).toEqual([]);
    const p = trees(islandsAt(-10), gradientTop(12));
    expect(validateParamTrees(p)).toEqual([]);
    const counts = [densitySourceValidations(), rulesSourceValidations()];
    expect(validateParamTrees(p)).toEqual([]);
    expect(validateParamTrees(paramsWith({ climate: { scaleMul: 3 } }))).toEqual([]);
    expect([densitySourceValidations(), rulesSourceValidations()]).toEqual(counts);
  });

  test('density issues carry `density.defs.` and the node path', () => {
    const t = densityTree();
    t['root'].b.x = { op: 'bogus' };
    t['defs'] = { lift: { op: 'ref', name: 'nowhere' } };
    expect(brief(validateParamTrees(trees(t)))).toEqual(['density.defs.root.b.x UNKNOWN_OP', 'density.defs.defs.lift.name UNKNOWN_REF']);
  });

  test('rule issues carry `surface.rules.` and the rule id with its field, never `.param`', () => {
    const t = rulesTree();
    findKind(t, 'steep').min = { param: 'surface.nope' };
    findKind(t, 'block').state = 'air';
    expect(brief(validateParamTrees(trees(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, t)))).toEqual([
      'surface.rules.root.rules[0].then.state NOT_SOLID',
      'surface.rules.root.rules[1].then.rules[1].if.min UNKNOWN_PARAM',
    ]);
  });

  test('both leaves at once: density first, then the rules', () => {
    const d = densityTree();
    d['root'].b.x = { op: 'bogus' };
    const r = rulesTree();
    findKind(r, 'block').state = 'air';
    expect(validateParamTrees(trees(d, r)).map((i) => i.path.split('.')[0])).toEqual(['density', 'surface']);
  });

  test('an issue at the value itself carries the leaf path alone (an empty node path)', () => {
    // 76 references to one detail noise: the column cost (76 × 128 + 75) × 98,304 is above the maximum (Task 6).
    const refs = (n: number): unknown => (n === 1 ? { op: 'ref', name: 'n' } : { op: 'add', a: refs(n >> 1), b: refs(n - (n >> 1)) });
    const density = { root: refs(76), defs: { n: { op: 'noise', id: 'detail' } } };
    expect(brief(validateParamTrees(trees(density)))).toEqual(['density.defs COLUMN_COST']);
    // 1,414 rule and condition nodes without a fast path (a steep condition is neither Y-only nor floor-bounded).
    const entry = { kind: 'condition', if: { kind: 'steep', min: 1 }, then: { kind: 'block', state: 'stone' } };
    const rules = { kind: 'sequence', rules: Array.from({ length: 471 }, () => entry) };
    expect(brief(validateParamTrees(trees(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, rules)))).toEqual(['surface.rules COLUMN_COST']);
  });
});

describe('the default trees pass both tiers (spec §1.8 invariant)', () => {
  test('every profile', () => {
    for (const id of PROFILE_IDS) expect(validateParamTrees(resolveProfile(id)), id).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('the U2 variants of both leaves (spec §7) and the uiSmoke trees (spec §6: islands −10, terrain muted)', () => {
    const variants = [
      ...perturbations(leafInfo('density.defs'), DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE).map((v) => trees(v)),
      ...perturbations(leafInfo('surface.rules'), DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES).map((v) => trees(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, v)),
      trees(islandsAt(-10)), trees(terrainMuted(0)), trees(islandsAt(-10), gradientTop(12)),
    ];
    expect(variants).toHaveLength(5);
    for (const p of variants) expect(validateParamTrees(p)).toEqual([]);
    expect(canonicalJSON(variants[0]!.density.defs)).toBe(canonicalJSON(terrainMuted(0)));
    expect(canonicalJSON(variants[1]!.surface.rules)).toBe(canonicalJSON(gradientTop(12)));
  });

  test('the edited trees of the round trips (spec §1.11)', () => {
    expect(validateParamTrees(trees(editedDensity(), editedRules()))).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('the contexts read the leaves (spec §1.6)', () => {
  test('density: resolveDensity(params.density.defs, params)', () => {
    expect((createDensityContext(ctxFor('42')).expr.root as unknown as { b: { x: { v: number } } }).b.x.v).toBe(-1000000);
    const dc = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42', { density: { defs: islandsAt(-10) } } as ParamsPatch));
    expect(dc.expr.root).toMatchObject({ op: 'max', b: { op: 'tap', name: 'islands', x: { op: 'const', v: -10 } } });
    expect(Object.isFrozen(dc.expr.root)).toBe(true);
    // The muted terrain tap's child is the mute value (§1.5).
    const muted = createDensityContext(ctxFor('42', { density: { defs: terrainMuted(0) } } as ParamsPatch));
    expect(muted.expr.root).toMatchObject({ a: { a: { op: 'tap', name: 'terrain', x: { op: 'const', v: 0 } } } });
  });

  test('surface: resolveRules(params.surface.rules, params), refs read from the same params', () => {
    const sc = surfaceContextOf(ctxFor('42', { surface: { rules: gradientTop(12), cliffSteep: 2 } } as ParamsPatch));
    expect((sc.rules as unknown as { rules: { if: unknown }[] }).rules[2]!.if).toMatchObject({ kind: 'verticalGradient', trueAtAndBelow: 0, falseAtAndAbove: 12 });
    expect(findKind(sc.rules, 'steep')).toMatchObject({ min: 2 });
  });

  test('a tier-1-valid tree that fails tier 2 throws at context creation, with its source paths', () => {
    const cycle = { root: { op: 'ref', name: 'a' }, defs: { a: { op: 'ref', name: 'b' }, b: { op: 'ref', name: 'a' } } };
    const ctx = ctxFor('42', { density: { defs: cycle } } as ParamsPatch);
    expect(() => createDensityContext(ctx)).toThrow(ExprValidationError);
    try { createDensityContext(ctx); } catch (e) { expect((e as ExprValidationError).issues.map((i) => i.code)).toContain('REF_CYCLE'); }
    const air = rulesTree();
    findKind(air, 'block').state = 'air';
    const sctx = ctxFor('42', { surface: { rules: air } } as ParamsPatch);
    expect(() => createSurfaceContext(sctx)).toThrow(RuleValidationError);
  });
});

describe('a depth-48 tree through every canonical wrapper (spec §1.7)', () => {
  const density = deepDensity(48);
  const rules = deepRules(48);
  const patch = { density: { defs: density }, surface: { rules } } as ParamsPatch;

  test('the trees are at container depth 48 and pass tier 1; one level more is JSON_TOO_DEEP', () => {
    expect([jsonDepth(density), jsonDepth(rules), jsonDepth(deepDensity(49)), jsonDepth(deepRules(49))]).toEqual([48, 48, 49, 49]);
    expect(applyPatch(SCHEMA, DEFAULTS, patch).ok).toBe(true);
    const over = applyPatch(SCHEMA, DEFAULTS, { density: { defs: deepDensity(49) }, surface: { rules: deepRules(49) } } as ParamsPatch);
    expect(!over.ok && over.issues.map((i) => i.code)).toEqual(['JSON_TOO_DEEP', 'JSON_TOO_DEEP']);
  });

  test('encodeMapState, exportPreset, encodeLabState (B patch), draftKeyOf, stageHashes and paramsHash', () => {
    const params = paramsWith(patch);
    const map = decodeMapState(`#${encodeMapState({ ...DEFAULT_MAP_STATE, patch })}`);
    expect(map.error).toBeNull();
    expect(canonicalJSON(map.state.patch)).toBe(canonicalJSON(patch));
    const preset = importPreset(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(exportPreset('Deep', 'default', params))) as unknown);
    expect(preset.ok && canonicalJSON(preset.value.params)).toBe(canonicalJSON(params));
    const lab = decodeLabState(`#${encodeLabState({ ...DEFAULT_LAB_STATE, b: { patch } })}`);
    expect(lab.error).toBeNull();
    expect(canonicalJSON(lab.state.b?.patch)).toBe(canonicalJSON(patch));
    expect(draftKeyOf({ seedText: '42', profile: 'default', patch })).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{16}$/);
    expect(stageHashes(params, STAGES).terrain).not.toBe(stageHashes(DEFAULTS, STAGES).terrain);
    expect(paramsHash(params)).not.toEqual(paramsHash(DEFAULTS));
  });
});
```

Create `src/gen/trees.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Tier 2 of a params document's two trees (SP3d spec §1.8, D2, D3): `validateParamTrees(params)` runs
 * `validateDensitySource` on `params.density.defs` and `validateRulesSource` on `params.surface.rules` and returns their
 * issues, density first, each with its leaf path prefixed: the leaf path, a dot and the node path
 * (`density.defs.root.a.x`, `surface.rules.root.rules[1].then.if.min`); an issue at the value itself (empty node path)
 * carries the leaf path alone (`surface.rules`). Both validators are memoised by tree identity, so a document whose trees
 * are the registered (frozen) values it had before costs two WeakMap lookups. Never throws; `[]` means both trees are
 * valid. The session (constructor option), the worker's configure, the editors and the invariant tests call it; the
 * resolvers run the same validators themselves. Follows the gen determinism rules.
 */
import type { Issue } from '../core/params/kit';
import type { Params } from '../core/params/schema';
import { validateDensitySource } from './density/source';
import { validateRulesSource } from './surface/source';

const DENSITY = validateDensitySource;
const RULES = validateRulesSource;

/** The leaf paths of the two trees. */
const DENSITY_LEAF = 'density.defs';
const RULES_LEAF = 'surface.rules';

/** `<leaf>.<node path>`; the leaf path alone for an issue at the value itself, `<leaf>[i]` for an array item. */
function prefixed(leaf: string, path: string): string {
  if (path === '') return leaf;
  return path.startsWith('[') ? `${leaf}${path}` : `${leaf}.${path}`;
}

/** Tier 2 of both trees of `params`, issues prefixed by their leaf path (density first); `[]` when both are valid. */
export function validateParamTrees(params: Params): Issue[] {
  const out: Issue[] = [];
  for (const i of DENSITY(params.density.defs)) out.push({ path: prefixed(DENSITY_LEAF, i.path), code: i.code, message: i.message });
  for (const i of RULES(params.surface.rules)) out.push({ path: prefixed(RULES_LEAF, i.path), code: i.code, message: i.message });
  return out;
}
```

```diff
+const JSON_VARIANTS: ReadonlyMap<string, JsonVariant> = new Map<string, JsonVariant>([

+/** A copy of `v` (plain objects and arrays copied along `at`, the rest shared) with `key` of the node at `at` set. */
+function withJsonField(path: string, v: unknown, at: readonly (string | number)[], key: string, value: number): unknown {
+  if (typeof v !== 'object' || v === null) throw new Error(`U2: no node at ${path} ${JSON.stringify(at)}`);
+  if (at.length === 0) return { ...(v as Record<string, unknown>), [key]: value };
+  const [k, ...rest] = at;
+  if (Array.isArray(v)) {

+  if (typeof k !== 'string' || !Object.hasOwn(o, k)) throw new Error(`U2: no node at ${path} ${JSON.stringify(at)}`);

+  if (!fits) throw new Error(`U2: ${path} has no ${JSON.stringify(spec.is)} node at ${JSON.stringify(spec.at)}`);
```
