```ts
describe('planFieldSlice: the one split and refusal math (SP3d spec §5.2, P3)', () => {
  const accepted = (p: FieldSlicePlan) => {
    if (p.refused) throw new Error(`refused, limit ${p.limit}`);
    return p;
  };
  /** §5.2's column cost of a density/node sample column of per-sample work cost c. */
  const vertical = (n: number, c: number) => n * c + COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST;
  const horizontal = (n: number, c: number) => n * (c + CORNER_SAMPLE_COST);

  test('the acquisition costs and budgets are core\'s, re-exported once', () => {
    expect([COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST, CORNER_SAMPLE_COST, CORNER_STEEP_COST, PART_BUDGET, DRAFT_BUDGET, REQUEST_BUDGET, SLICE_RULE_NA])
      .toEqual([core.COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST, core.CORNER_SAMPLE_COST, core.CORNER_STEEP_COST, core.PART_BUDGET, core.DRAFT_BUDGET, core.REQUEST_BUDGET, core.SLICE_RULE_NA]);
    expect([PART_BUDGET, DRAFT_BUDGET, REQUEST_BUDGET]).toEqual([2 ** 23, 2 ** 24, 2 ** 27]);
  });
  test('at the defaults (c = 569): k = 79 vertical and 25 horizontal; parts max(poolSize, ⌈n / k⌉), equal contiguous ranges of at most k', () => {
    const v = accepted(planFieldSlice(128, vertical(128, 569), 6, REQUEST_BUDGET));
    expect([vertical(128, 569), v.k, v.ranges]).toEqual([105_600, 79, [[0, 21], [21, 42], [42, 64], [64, 85], [85, 106], [106, 128]]]);
    expect(accepted(planFieldSlice(128, vertical(128, 569), 1, REQUEST_BUDGET)).ranges).toEqual([[0, 64], [64, 128]]);
    const h = accepted(planFieldSlice(128, horizontal(128, 569), 2, REQUEST_BUDGET));
    expect([horizontal(128, 569), h.k, h.ranges.length]).toEqual([334_976, 25, 6]);
    expect(h.ranges).toEqual([[0, 21], [21, 42], [42, 64], [64, 85], [85, 106], [106, 128]]);
    expect(accepted(planFieldSlice(32, vertical(32, 569), 3, DRAFT_BUDGET)).ranges).toEqual([[0, 10], [10, 21], [21, 32]]);
  });
  test('refusal limits: a 128² slice above c = 7,936 vertical / 6,144 horizontal, a draft above 15,360 / 14,336; the limit is the largest column cost accepted', () => {
    for (const [n, budget, cost, c] of [
      [128, REQUEST_BUDGET, vertical, 7936], [128, REQUEST_BUDGET, horizontal, 6144], [32, DRAFT_BUDGET, vertical, 15_360], [32, DRAFT_BUDGET, horizontal, 14_336],
    ] as const) {
      expect(planFieldSlice(n, cost(n, c), 6, budget).refused, `${n} c ${c}`).toBe(false);
      expect(planFieldSlice(n, cost(n, c + 1), 6, budget), `${n} c ${c + 1}`).toEqual({ refused: true, limit: Math.floor(budget / n) });
    }
    // One sample column above PART_BUDGET is refused whatever the budget.
    expect(planFieldSlice(4, PART_BUDGET + 1, 2, 2 ** 40)).toEqual({ refused: true, limit: PART_BUDGET });
    expect(accepted(planFieldSlice(4, PART_BUDGET, 2, 2 ** 40)).ranges).toEqual([[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]]);
  });
  test('a steep-reading tree of default weight: its horizontal 128² slice and draft are planned, never refused with limit 0', () => {
    const steep = (n: number, c: number) => n * (c + CORNER_STEEP_COST);
    const p = paramsWith({ density: { defs: steepTree() } } as never);
    expect(workCost(evaluatedExpression(p, 'density', ''), p)).toBe(571);
    const full = accepted(planFieldSlice(128, sliceCostOf(p, 'density', '', 'horizontal', 128), 4, REQUEST_BUDGET));
    expect([sliceCostOf(p, 'density', '', 'horizontal', 128), full.k, full.ranges.length]).toEqual([steep(128, 571), 11, 12]);
    expect(accepted(planFieldSlice(32, sliceCostOf(p, 'node', 'root.b', 'horizontal', 32), 4, DRAFT_BUDGET)).ranges.length).toBe(4);
    // The steep refusal limits: 3,072 per sample for a 128² slice, 11,264 for a draft; above them the limit is planFieldSlice's.
    for (const [n, budget, c] of [[128, REQUEST_BUDGET, 3072], [32, DRAFT_BUDGET, 11_264]] as const) {
      expect(planFieldSlice(n, steep(n, c), 6, budget).refused, `${n} c ${c}`).toBe(false);
      expect(planFieldSlice(n, steep(n, c + 1), 6, budget), `${n} c ${c + 1}`).toEqual({ refused: true, limit: Math.floor(budget / n) });
    }
    // Every acquisition leaves a per-sample room of at least 1 under every budget (the notice never says "limit 0").
    for (const [n, budget] of [[32, DRAFT_BUDGET], [128, REQUEST_BUDGET]] as const) {
      const limit = Math.min(PART_BUDGET, Math.floor(budget / n));
      for (const per of [CORNER_SAMPLE_COST, CORNER_STEEP_COST]) expect(Math.floor(limit / n) - per, `${n} ${per}`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
      expect(Math.floor((limit - COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST) / n), `${n} vertical`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    }
  });
  test('budget null (blocks, rule) is never refused: k = 1 and one part per sample column above PART_BUDGET / 2', () => {
    expect(['density', 'node', 'blocks', 'rule'].map((f) => isRefusableField(f as never))).toEqual([true, true, false, false]);
    const t = accepted(planFieldSlice(32, 5_006_893, 6, null));
    expect([t.k, t.ranges.length, t.ranges[31]]).toEqual([1, 32, [31, 32]]);
    expect(accepted(planFieldSlice(128, 64 * 5_006_893, 2, null)).ranges.length).toBe(128);
  });
  test('the parts are contiguous, cover [0, n), never exceed k, and each passes the handler\'s bound check', () => {
    for (const n of [32, 128]) {
      for (const size of [1, 2, 3, 6]) {
        for (const cc of [1, 569, 50_976, 105_600, PART_BUDGET / 4, 2_796_203, PART_BUDGET / 2 + 1, PART_BUDGET, 2 ** 31]) {
          for (const field of ['density', 'blocks'] as const) {
            const p = planFieldSlice(n, cc, size, field === 'density' ? 2 ** 40 : null);
            if (p.refused) { expect(cc).toBeGreaterThan(PART_BUDGET); continue; }
            expect(p.ranges[0]![0]).toBe(0);
            expect(p.ranges.at(-1)![1]).toBe(n);
            expect(p.ranges.length).toBe(Math.min(n, Math.max(size, Math.ceil(n / p.k))));
            p.ranges.forEach(([from, to], i) => {
              expect(to - from).toBeGreaterThan(0);
              expect(to - from).toBeLessThanOrEqual(p.k);
              if (i > 0) expect(from).toBe(p.ranges[i - 1]![1]);
              expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(to - from, cc, field), `${n} ${size} ${cc} ${field}`).toBeNull();
            });
          }
        }
      }
    }
  });
  test('the handler\'s bound: a density or node part of w columns above PART_BUDGET, a blocks or rule part of more than k columns', () => {
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(79, 105_600, 'density')).toBeNull();
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(80, 105_600, 'node')).toBe(`too heavy: 80 × 105600 work units exceed the part budget ${PART_BUDGET}`);
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(1, PART_BUDGET + 1, 'density')).toMatch(/^too heavy: /);
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(1, 2 ** 31, 'blocks')).toBeNull();
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(2, 5_006_893, 'rule')).toBe('too heavy: 2 sample columns of cost 5006893, at most 1 per part');
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(3, 2_000_000, 'blocks')).toBeNull();
    expect(fieldSlicePartProblem(5, 2_000_000, 'blocks')).toMatch(/^too heavy: /);
  });
  test('bad arguments are RangeErrors', () => {
    const cases: Array<[number, number, number, number | null]> = [[0, 1, 1, null], [1.5, 1, 1, null], [32, 0, 1, null], [32, Number.NaN, 1, null], [32, Infinity, 1, null], [32, 1, 0, null], [32, 1, 1.5, null], [32, 1, 1, 0], [32, 1, 1, Number.NaN]];
    for (const args of cases) {
      expect(() => planFieldSlice(...args), JSON.stringify(args)).toThrow(RangeError);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
 * The fieldSlice and fieldProbe jobs' message handling (SP3d spec §5.1, §5.3): the arguments' checks (the handler's
 * BAD_ARGS), the vertical plane's points (`segmentPointAt` and `segmentProblem` of `metrics/crossSection.ts`, which gen
 * cannot import), the work bound's part check (`fieldSlicePartProblem` on `sliceCostOf`, recomputed from the configured
 * params: the client's column cost is not trusted), the call into gen's evaluation (`gen/inspect/fieldSlice.ts`) and the
 * reply. The `blocks` field reads its T columns from the handler's slice job (its store and LRU, `sliceJob.ts`).
 */
import { MAX_Y } from '../core/coords';
import { COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST, MIN_Y } from '../core/constants';
import type { GenContext } from '../gen/context';
import {
  evaluatedExpression, evaluateFieldSlice, fieldSliceProblem, probeField, sliceCostOf, sliceGeometryProblem, type SliceGeometry, type TColumnSource,
} from '../gen/inspect/fieldSlice';
import { workCost } from '../gen/inspect/cost';
import { segmentPointAt, segmentProblem } from '../metrics/crossSection';
import { fieldSlicePartProblem, surfaceProbeProblem, type FieldProbeMsg, type FieldProbeResultMsg, type FieldSliceMsg, type FieldSliceResultMsg } from './protocol';
import type { SliceJob } from './sliceJob';

const POINT_AT = segmentPointAt;
const SEGMENT_PROBLEM = segmentProblem;
const GEOMETRY_PROBLEM = sliceGeometryProblem;
const FIELD_PROBLEM = fieldSliceProblem;
const EVALUATE = evaluateFieldSlice;
const PROBE = probeField;
const SLICE_COST = sliceCostOf;
const EXPRESSION = evaluatedExpression;
const WORK_COST = workCost;
const PART_PROBLEM = fieldSlicePartProblem;
const VOXEL_PROBLEM = surfaceProbeProblem;
const SAMPLE_COST = COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST;

/** A job's reply and the buffers it transfers, its BAD_ARGS text, or null when `stop()` fired (ABORTED). */
export type FieldJobReply<T> = { readonly msg: T; readonly transfer: readonly ArrayBuffer[] } | { readonly badArgs: string } | null;

/** The T columns of the `blocks` field: the slice job's proto views, claimed with `epoch`. */
export const sliceJobColumns = (slices: SliceJob, ctx: GenContext, epoch: number): TColumnSource => (cx, cz, stop) => slices.column(ctx, epoch, cx, cz, stop);

/**
 * The plane of a fieldSlice message, or why it has none: n ∈ SLICE_NS, then the segment (`segmentProblem`) or the square
 * (integer centre, extent, inside the window), then y an integer in −64 … 319 (required on both planes, unused by the
 * vertical one).
 */
export function fieldSliceGeometry(m: FieldSliceMsg): SliceGeometry | string {
  const g: SliceGeometry = m.plane === 'vertical'
    ? { plane: 'vertical', n: m.n, pointAt: (i) => POINT_AT(m, i, m.n) }
    : { plane: 'horizontal', n: m.n, cx: m.cx, cz: m.cz, y: m.y, extent: m.extent };
  const problem = GEOMETRY_PROBLEM(g)
    ?? (m.plane === 'vertical' ? SEGMENT_PROBLEM(m) : null)
    ?? (Number.isInteger(m.y) && m.y >= MIN_Y && m.y <= MAX_Y ? null : `y ${m.y} is not an integer in [${MIN_Y}, ${MAX_Y}]`);
  return problem ?? g;
}

/**
 * Every BAD_ARGS case of a fieldSlice message in `ctx` (spec §5.1), or its geometry: the plane, the range [from, to)
 * (integers, 0 ≤ from < to ≤ n), the field on its plane and the path in the configured source trees, then the part bound.
 */
export function fieldSliceArgs(ctx: GenContext, m: FieldSliceMsg): SliceGeometry | string {
  const g = fieldSliceGeometry(m);
  if (typeof g === 'string') return g;
  const { from, to, n } = m;
  if (!(Number.isInteger(from) && Number.isInteger(to) && from >= 0 && from < to && to <= n)) return `samples [${from}, ${to}) are not integers with 0 ≤ from < to ≤ ${n}`;
  return FIELD_PROBLEM(ctx, m.field, m.path, m.plane) ?? PART_PROBLEM(to - from, SLICE_COST(ctx.params, m.field, m.path, m.plane, n), m.field) ?? g;
}

/** Runs a fieldSlice job in `ctx`: its reply (values, and fluid for blocks, transferred), its BAD_ARGS, or null when stopped. */
export function runFieldSlice(ctx: GenContext, m: FieldSliceMsg, stop: () => boolean, tColumns: TColumnSource): FieldJobReply<FieldSliceResultMsg> {
  const g = fieldSliceArgs(ctx, m);
  if (typeof g === 'string') return { badArgs: g };
  const r = EVALUATE(ctx, { geometry: g, field: m.field, path: m.path, from: m.from, to: m.to }, stop, m.field === 'blocks' ? tColumns : undefined);
  if (r === null) return null;
  const values = r.values.buffer;
  const fluid = r.fluid === null ? null : r.fluid.buffer;
  const msg: FieldSliceResultMsg = { type: 'fieldSliceResult', jobId: m.jobId, epoch: m.epoch, n: m.n, field: m.field, from: m.from, to: m.to, values, fluid };
  return { msg, transfer: fluid === null ? [values] : [values, fluid] };
}

/**
 * Every BAD_ARGS case of a fieldProbe message in `ctx` (spec §5.3), or null: the position (integers, in the window, y in
 * −64 … 319), the path, and for density and node the bound: one sample's work cost with its ColumnSample (§5.2) within
 * PART_BUDGET (a rule probe, one T column bounded by tier 2, is never refused, as rule slices).
 */
export function fieldProbeArgsProblem(ctx: GenContext, m: FieldProbeMsg): string | null {
  const problem = VOXEL_PROBLEM(m.x, m.y, m.z) ?? FIELD_PROBLEM(ctx, m.field, m.path, 'vertical');
  if (problem !== null || m.field === 'rule') return problem;
  return PART_PROBLEM(1, WORK_COST(EXPRESSION(ctx.params, m.field, m.path), ctx.params) + SAMPLE_COST, m.field);
}

/** Runs a fieldProbe job in `ctx`: the value (any number), its BAD_ARGS, or null when stopped. */
export function runFieldProbe(ctx: GenContext, m: FieldProbeMsg, stop: () => boolean): FieldJobReply<FieldProbeResultMsg> {
  const problem = fieldProbeArgsProblem(ctx, m);
  if (problem !== null) return { badArgs: problem };
  const value = PROBE(ctx, m.field, m.path, m.x, m.y, m.z, stop);
  return value === null ? null : { msg: { type: 'fieldProbeResult', jobId: m.jobId, epoch: m.epoch, value }, transfer: [] };
}
```

```bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(workers): the fieldSlice and fieldProbe jobs, planFieldSlice and the pool's split

SP3d spec §4.5, §5.1-§5.3, D17, P1, P3. protocol.ts gains the four messages and
their guards (the reply's n, field, range and exact byte lengths), re-exports the
work bound's costs and budgets from core/constants.ts, and holds the one
implementation of the split and refusal math (planFieldSlice) with the handler's
part check (fieldSlicePartProblem). A job reply whose envelope reads but whose
body fails its guard parses as {bad, jobId, reason}: the pool rejects that job
with BAD_MESSAGE and frees the worker instead of wedging it.

workers/fieldSliceJob.ts checks the arguments (BAD_ARGS, including the work
bound recomputed from the configured params), computes the vertical points with
segmentPointAt and calls gen/inspect/fieldSlice.ts; blocks read the slice job's
store and LRU (sliceJob.column). The handler dispatches through an exhaustive
switch and the surfaceProbe job polls stop() before its column build.

The pool's fieldSlice(req, {priority, columnCost, budget}) splits by
planFieldSlice (refused density/node requests reject with SliceTooHeavy before
any job), runs the parts as one group, merges them by index and cross-checks each
part; cancel() drops the queued parts and discards the running ones.
fieldProbe(req, priority = -1) is a single job. instrumentPool forwards both.
Master §1: workers/ adds fieldSliceJob.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JbkJNEMpTrQS68LobuogBc
EOF
```

```ts
import { Worker } from 'node:worker_threads';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import type { Params } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { seedFromInput } from '../../src/core/seed';
import { createWorkerPool, type WorkerLike } from '../../src/engine/workerPool';
import { createGenContext, type GenContext } from '../../src/gen/context';
import { evaluateFieldSlice, sliceCostOf, type FieldSliceValues, type SliceField, type SliceGeometry, type TColumnSource } from '../../src/gen/inspect/fieldSlice';
import { segmentPointAt, type Segment } from '../../src/metrics/crossSection';
import { fillColumnT } from '../../src/metrics/region';
import { createStore } from '../../src/world/store/store';
import { DRAFT_BUDGET, PART_BUDGET, planFieldSlice, type FieldSliceSpec } from '../../src/workers/protocol';
import { ask, buildNodeTaskWorker } from '../harness/nodeWorker';
import { paramsWith } from '../harness/gen';
import { partWorstParams } from '../harness/sliceTrees';
import { heavyDetailPatch } from '../unit/fixtures/editedTrees';

/**
 * The fieldSlice job in real worker threads (SP3d spec §5.2, §10 "Workers"):
 * - the pool's split over N `worker_threads` running `src/workers/taskHandler.ts` merges into exactly the single
 *   evaluation (every field and plane; pool sizes 1, 2, 3 and 6), the values and fluid arriving as transferred buffers;
 * - a configure (a new epoch in the abort cell) stops an in-flight part within 50 ms, with the default tree and with
 *   `slice.partWorst`'s tree at the part bound (`test/harness/sliceTrees.ts`), and a `rule` part on a heavy valid tree
 *   (`heavyDetailPatch`) whose probe column takes about 0.1 s to fill, as `abort.test.ts` times tiles: from
 *   `Atomics.store` here to `handle` returning in the worker (`handledAt`, on the clock every thread shares). The
 *   evaluation polls the cell once per sample and the probe column's density fill every 8 corner rows, so the bound is
 *   one sample's time or one eighth of a column fill; the timing tests retry twice.
 */
const MOUNTAIN: Segment = { ax: -1664, az: 8, bx: -640, bz: 8 };
const COAST: Segment = { ax: -27136, az: -31992, bx: -26113, bz: -31992 };
const NEVER = (): boolean => false;

let plain = '';
let stamped = '';
const threads: Worker[] = [];

beforeAll(async () => {
  plain = await buildNodeTaskWorker('fieldSliceThreads');
  stamped = await buildNodeTaskWorker('fieldSliceAbort', { stamp: true });
}, 120_000);

afterAll(async () => {
  await Promise.all(threads.map((t) => t.terminate()));
});

const start = (script: string): Worker => {
  const t = new Worker(script);
  threads.push(t);
  return t;
};

/** A worker thread behind the pool's WorkerLike interface. */
function threadWorker(): WorkerLike {
  const t = start(plain);
  const w: WorkerLike = {
    onmessage: null,
    onerror: null,
    postMessage(msg, transfer) { t.postMessage(msg, (transfer ?? []) as never); },
    terminate() { void t.terminate(); },
  };
  t.on('message', (data: unknown) => w.onmessage?.({ data }));
  t.on('error', (e) => w.onerror?.(e));
  return w;
}

const bytes = (v: ArrayBufferView): Buffer => Buffer.from(v.buffer, v.byteOffset, v.byteLength);
const freshCtx = (params: Params): GenContext => createGenContext(seedFromInput('42'), params);

function storeColumns(ctx: GenContext): TColumnSource {
  const store = createStore({ shared: false, maxBlockBytes: 32 << 20, maxByteBytes: 16 << 20 });
  return (cx, cz, stop) => (store.proto(cx, cz) === null && !fillColumnT(store, ctx, cx, cz, stop) ? null : store.proto(cx, cz));
}

const vReq = (s: Segment, field: SliceField, path = '', n = 32): FieldSliceSpec => ({ plane: 'vertical', ...s, y: 63, n, field, path });
const hReq = (field: SliceField, path = '', n = 32): FieldSliceSpec => ({ plane: 'horizontal', cx: -1152, cz: 8, y: 100, extent: 8192, n, field, path });
const geometryOf = (r: FieldSliceSpec): SliceGeometry => (r.plane === 'vertical'
  ? { plane: 'vertical', n: r.n, pointAt: (i) => segmentPointAt(r, i, r.n) }
  : { plane: 'horizontal', n: r.n, cx: r.cx, cz: r.cz, y: r.y, extent: r.extent });

/** The samples [from, to) evaluated in this thread on a fresh context. */
function inProcess(params: Params, r: FieldSliceSpec, from = 0, to = r.n): FieldSliceValues {
  const ctx = freshCtx(params);
  return evaluateFieldSlice(ctx, { geometry: geometryOf(r), field: r.field, path: r.path, from, to }, NEVER, r.field === 'blocks' ? storeColumns(ctx) : undefined)!;
}

const REQUESTS: Array<[string, FieldSliceSpec]> = [
  ['vertical density', vReq(MOUNTAIN, 'density')],
  ['vertical node', vReq(MOUNTAIN, 'node', 'root.a.a.x.x')],
  ['horizontal density', hReq('density')],
  ['horizontal node', hReq('node', 'root.a.b')],
  ['vertical blocks', vReq(COAST, 'blocks')],
  ['vertical rule', vReq(COAST, 'rule', 'root.rules[1].then')],
];

describe('fieldSlice in real worker threads (SP3d spec §5.2, §10)', () => {
  const wants = new Map(REQUESTS.map(([name, r]) => [name, inProcess(DEFAULTS, r)]));

  test.each([[1], [2], [3], [6]])('pool of %i threads: every field and plane merges bit-identical to the single evaluation, split by planFieldSlice', async (size) => {
    const pool = createWorkerPool(size, threadWorker);
    await pool.configure('42', DEFAULTS);
    for (const [name, req] of REQUESTS) {
      const refusable = req.field === 'density' || req.field === 'node';
      // The real column cost, then (density and node) a client cost PART_BUDGET / 4 that forces parts of 4 sample columns.
      for (const columnCost of refusable ? [sliceCostOf(DEFAULTS, req.field, req.path, req.plane, req.n), PART_BUDGET / 4] : [sliceCostOf(DEFAULTS, req.field, req.path, req.plane, req.n)]) {
        const budget = columnCost === PART_BUDGET / 4 ? 2 ** 40 : DRAFT_BUDGET;
        const plan = planFieldSlice(req.n, columnCost, size, refusable ? budget : null);
        if (plan.refused) throw new Error(`${name}: refused`);
        const r = await pool.fieldSlice(req, { priority: 500, columnCost, budget }).promise;
        const want = wants.get(name)!;
        expect([r.n, r.field, plan.ranges.length >= Math.min(size, req.n)], name).toEqual([32, req.field, true]);
        expect(bytes(r.values).equals(bytes(want.values)), `${name} values, ${plan.ranges.length} parts`).toBe(true);
        expect(r.fluid === null ? null : bytes(r.fluid).equals(bytes(want.fluid!)), `${name} fluid`).toBe(want.fluid === null ? null : true);
      }
    }
    pool.terminate();
  }, 180_000);
});

/** Milliseconds on the clock the worker's `handledAt` uses (test/harness/nodeWorker.ts). */
const clock = () => Number(process.hrtime.bigint()) / 1e6;
/** Blocks this thread for `ms` without using a CPU, as a loaded runner delays the delivery of the worker's reply here. */
const stall = (ms: number) => { Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms); };
const configure = (epoch: number, params: Params, abort: SharedArrayBuffer | null) => ({ type: 'configure', epoch, seedText: '42', params, abort });

describe('a configure stops an in-flight fieldSlice part within 50 ms (SP3d spec §4.5, §10)', () => {
  // A part as large as the work bound allows: the default tree's 128² vertical part of k = 79 sample columns
  // (8,342,400 units), and partWorst's one 32-sample column (8,387,616 units, one sample ≈ 2 ms).
  const CASES: Array<[string, Params, FieldSliceSpec, number]> = [
    ['the default tree, a 128² vertical part of 79 sample columns', DEFAULTS, vReq(MOUNTAIN, 'density', '', 128), 79],
    ['partWorst\'s tree at the part bound, one 32-sample column', partWorstParams(), vReq(MOUNTAIN, 'density', '', 32), 1],
  ];

  test.each(CASES)('%s: ABORTED within 50 ms of Atomics.store; the next epoch\'s part equals the in-process evaluation', { retry: 2, timeout: 120_000 }, async (_name, params, req, to) => {
    expect(sliceCostOf(params, 'density', '', 'vertical', req.n) * to).toBeLessThanOrEqual(PART_BUDGET);
    expect(sliceCostOf(params, 'density', '', 'vertical', req.n) * to).toBeGreaterThan(PART_BUDGET * 0.99);
    const cell = new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4));
    const w = start(stamped);
    Atomics.store(cell, 0, 1);
    expect((await ask(w, configure(1, params, cell.buffer)))['type']).toBe('ready');
    const part = (jobId: number, epoch: number) => ({ type: 'fieldSlice', jobId, epoch, ...req, from: 0, to });
    // The part takes ≈ 65-90 ms on one thread (the calibration's p50s); the store lands within its first samples.
    const reply = ask(w, part(1, 1));
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 15));
    const storedAt = clock();
    Atomics.store(cell, 0, 2);
    stall(60);
    const m = await reply;
    expect(m).toMatchObject({ type: 'error', jobId: 1, epoch: 1, code: 'ABORTED' });
    const stopMs = (m['handledAt'] as number) - storedAt;
    expect(stopMs, 'the stamp is after the store on the shared clock').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(stopMs, `the handler returned ${stopMs.toFixed(1)} ms after the store`).toBeLessThan(50);

    expect((await ask(w, configure(2, params, cell.buffer)))['type']).toBe('ready');
    const next = await ask(w, part(2, 2));
    expect(next).toMatchObject({ type: 'fieldSliceResult', jobId: 2, epoch: 2, n: req.n, field: 'density', from: 0, to });
    expect(Buffer.from(next['values'] as ArrayBuffer).equals(bytes(inProcess(params, req, 0, to).values))).toBe(true);

  test('a heavy valid tree (heavyDetailPatch), a vertical rule part of one sample column: ABORTED within 50 ms of Atomics.store while its probe column fills', { retry: 2, timeout: 120_000 }, async () => {

    expect(m).toMatchObject({ type: 'error', jobId: 1, epoch: 1, code: 'ABORTED' });
    const stopMs = (m['handledAt'] as number) - storedAt;
    expect(stopMs, 'the stamp is after the store on the shared clock').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(stopMs, `the handler returned ${stopMs.toFixed(1)} ms after the store`).toBeLessThan(50);

    expect((await ask(w, configure(2, params, cell.buffer)))['type']).toBe('ready');
    const next = await ask(w, part(2, 2));
    expect(next).toMatchObject({ type: 'fieldSliceResult', jobId: 2, epoch: 2, n: 32, field: 'rule', from: 0, to: 1 });
    expect(Buffer.from(next['values'] as ArrayBuffer).equals(bytes(inProcess(params, req, 0, 1).values))).toBe(true);
```

```ts
import { loadavg } from 'node:os';
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST, CORNER_SAMPLE_COST, CORNER_STEEP_COST, PART_BUDGET } from '../../src/core/constants';
import { DEFAULTS } from '../../src/core/params/defaults';
import type { Params } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { seedFromInput } from '../../src/core/seed';
import { createGenContext, type GenContext } from '../../src/gen/context';
import { workCost } from '../../src/gen/inspect/cost';
import { createCornerSampler, evaluatedExpression, evaluateFieldSlice, horizontalCoord, sliceCostOf, type SliceGeometry } from '../../src/gen/inspect/fieldSlice';
import { surfaceContextOf } from '../../src/gen/surface/context';
import { validateParamTrees } from '../../src/gen/trees';
import { segmentPointAt, type Segment } from '../../src/metrics/crossSection';
import { noiseSumTree, PART_WORST_LEAVES, partWorstParams } from '../harness/sliceTrees';

/**
 * The work bound's calibration (SP3d spec §5.2 "Calibration", §9 `slice.partWorst`).
 *
 * Always run: `slice.partWorst`'s tree (`test/harness/sliceTrees.ts`) — an `interpolated` `add` of PART_WORST_LEAVES
 * `noise detail` leaves at 16 octaves, double — passes tier 2, and 253 is the largest leaf count whose 32-sample vertical
 * column fits PART_BUDGET.
 *
 * Run on demand on a quiet machine (`SLICE_CALIBRATION=1 npx vitest run --project integration
 * test/integration/fieldSliceCalibration.test.ts`): one thread, in-process, p50 of 9 runs, each on a fresh GenContext
 * (cold caches: the case right after an edit). It measures the unit (ns per work unit of reference evaluation, the
 * ColumnSamples already cached) on the default tree and on partWorst's tree, the time of a part at PART_BUDGET (the
 * default's 128² vertical part of k = 79 sample columns, its 128² horizontal part at extent 8192 of k = 25 rows, and
 * partWorst's one 32-sample column), and the three acquisition costs (a ColumnSample per chunk column along the mountain
 * line; a corner sample without and with steep at extent 8192, where no two samples share a corner) in units of the
 * default tree's unit. It prints `MEASUREMENT:` lines and fails — the spec's STOP — when a part at PART_BUDGET takes more
 * than 250 ms p50 or an acquisition cost differs from its constant by more than 2 ×.
 */
const CALIBRATE = process.env['SLICE_CALIBRATION'] === '1';
const MOUNTAIN: Segment = { ax: -1664, az: 8, bx: -640, bz: 8 };
const NEVER = (): boolean => false;
const RUNS = 9;
const PART_P50_MAX_MS = 250;

/** A sample column's work cost per sample of partWorst's tree with L leaves: 1 + 8 × (L − 1 adds + 128 L). */
const worstSampleCost = (leaves: number) => 1 + 8 * (leaves - 1 + 128 * leaves);

describe('slice.partWorst\'s tree (SP3d spec §9)', () => {
  test(`${PART_WORST_LEAVES} leaves: passes tier 2, and is the largest count whose 32-sample vertical column fits PART_BUDGET`, () => {
    const p = partWorstParams();
    expect(validateParamTrees(p)).toEqual([]);
    expect(p.density.noises.detail).toMatchObject({ octaves: 16, double: true });
    expect(workCost(evaluatedExpression(p, 'density', ''), p)).toBe(worstSampleCost(PART_WORST_LEAVES));
    expect(worstSampleCost(PART_WORST_LEAVES)).toBe(261_089);
    expect(sliceCostOf(p, 'density', '', 'vertical', 32)).toBe(32 * 261_089 + COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST);
    expect(sliceCostOf(p, 'density', '', 'vertical', 32)).toBe(8_387_616);
    expect(sliceCostOf(p, 'density', '', 'vertical', 32)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(PART_BUDGET);
    const more = partWorstParams(PART_WORST_LEAVES + 1);
    expect(validateParamTrees(more)).toEqual([]);
    expect(sliceCostOf(more, 'density', '', 'vertical', 32)).toBe(8_420_640);
    expect(sliceCostOf(more, 'density', '', 'vertical', 32)).toBeGreaterThan(PART_BUDGET);
  });
  test('the tree is a balanced add: its depth is ⌈log2 L⌉ adds under the interpolated', () => {
    let depth = 0;
    let level: unknown[] = [(noiseSumTree() as { root: { x: unknown } }).root.x];
    let leaves = 0;
    while (level.length > 0) {
      const next: unknown[] = [];
      for (const e of level as Array<Record<string, unknown>>) {
        if (e['op'] === 'add') next.push(e['a'], e['b']);
        else { expect(e).toEqual({ op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }); leaves++; }
      }
      if (next.length > 0) depth++;
      level = next;
    }
    expect([leaves, depth]).toEqual([PART_WORST_LEAVES, 8]);
  });
});

const now = () => Number(process.hrtime.bigint()) / 1e6;
const p50 = (xs: number[]): number => [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b)[(xs.length - 1) >> 1]!;
const fresh = (params: Params): GenContext => createGenContext(seedFromInput('42'), params);
const vertical = (n: number): SliceGeometry => ({ plane: 'vertical', n, pointAt: (i) => segmentPointAt(MOUNTAIN, i, n) });
const HORIZONTAL_8192: SliceGeometry = { plane: 'horizontal', n: 128, cx: 0, cz: 0, y: 63, extent: 8192 };

interface Part { readonly name: string; readonly params: Params; readonly geometry: SliceGeometry; readonly to: number }
const PARTS: readonly Part[] = [
  { name: 'default vertical 128² part [0, 79)', params: DEFAULTS, geometry: vertical(128), to: 79 },
  { name: 'default horizontal 128² part at extent 8192 [0, 25)', params: DEFAULTS, geometry: HORIZONTAL_8192, to: 25 },
  { name: `partWorst (${PART_WORST_LEAVES} leaves) vertical 32² part [0, 1)`, params: partWorstParams(), geometry: vertical(32), to: 1 },
];

/** Times evaluateFieldSlice of [0, to): cold (fresh context) and, for vertical planes, warm (the same part again). */
function timePart(part: Part): { cold: number; warm: number } {
  const ctx = fresh(part.params);
  const req = { geometry: part.geometry, field: 'density' as const, path: '', from: 0, to: part.to };
  let t = now();
  evaluateFieldSlice(ctx, req, NEVER);
  const cold = now() - t;
  t = now();
  evaluateFieldSlice(ctx, req, NEVER);
  return { cold, warm: now() - t };
}

describe.runIf(CALIBRATE)('calibration of the work unit and the acquisition costs (SP3d spec §5.2) — SLICE_CALIBRATION=1', () => {
  test('a part at PART_BUDGET takes ≤ 250 ms p50 on one thread; the acquisition costs are within 2 × of their constants', () => {
    const lines: string[] = [`load average at start ${loadavg().map((v) => v.toFixed(2)).join(' ')}`];
    const units: Record<string, number> = {};
    const partP50: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const part of PARTS) {
      const runs = Array.from({ length: RUNS }, () => timePart(part));
      const columnCost = sliceCostOf(part.params, 'density', '', part.geometry.plane, part.geometry.n);
      const c = workCost(evaluatedExpression(part.params, 'density', ''), part.params);
      const cold = p50(runs.map((r) => r.cold));
      partP50[part.name] = cold;
      lines.push(`${part.name}: ${part.to} × ${columnCost} = ${part.to * columnCost} units (${((100 * part.to * columnCost) / PART_BUDGET).toFixed(1)} % of PART_BUDGET), cold p50 ${cold.toFixed(1)} ms (min ${Math.min(...runs.map((r) => r.cold)).toFixed(1)}, max ${Math.max(...runs.map((r) => r.cold)).toFixed(1)})`);
      if (part.geometry.plane === 'vertical') {
        const warm = p50(runs.map((r) => r.warm));
        const evalUnits = part.to * part.geometry.n * c;
        units[part.name] = (warm * 1e6) / evalUnits;
        lines.push(`  unit: warm p50 ${warm.toFixed(1)} ms for ${part.to} × ${part.geometry.n} samples × ${c} units = ${evalUnits} units → ${units[part.name]!.toFixed(2)} ns/unit`);
      }
    }
    const unit = units[PARTS[0]!.name]!;

    // A ColumnSample per chunk column along the mountain line (z = 8: chunk row 0), on a fresh context, after one warm-up column.
    const columnRuns: number[] = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < RUNS; r++) {
      const columns = surfaceContextOf(fresh(DEFAULTS)).density.columns;
      columns.get(-200, 0);
      const t = now();
      for (let cx = -104; cx < -40; cx++) columns.get(cx, 0);
      columnRuns.push((now() - t) / 64);
    }
    // Corner samples at the 128² horizontal plane of extent 8192 centred on (0, 0), rows [0, 25): 3,200 samples 64 blocks apart.
    const cornerRuns = (steep: boolean): number[] => Array.from({ length: RUNS }, () => {
      const sampler = createCornerSampler(fresh(DEFAULTS), steep);
      sampler.sample(4096, 4096);
      const t = now();
      for (let j = 0; j < 25; j++) {
        const z = horizontalCoord(0, 8192, j, 128);
        for (let i = 0; i < 128; i++) sampler.sample(horizontalCoord(0, 8192, i, 128), z);
      }
      return (now() - t) / 3200;
    });
    const acquisitions: Array<[string, number, number]> = [
      ['COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST', p50(columnRuns), COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST],
      ['CORNER_SAMPLE_COST', p50(cornerRuns(false)), CORNER_SAMPLE_COST],
      ['CORNER_STEEP_COST', p50(cornerRuns(true)), CORNER_STEEP_COST],
    ];
    const ratios: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const [name, ms, constant] of acquisitions) {
      const measured = (ms * 1e6) / unit;
      ratios[name] = measured / constant;
      lines.push(`${name}: ${(ms * 1000).toFixed(1)} µs p50 = ${Math.round(measured)} units at ${unit.toFixed(2)} ns/unit (constant ${constant}, ratio ${ratios[name]!.toFixed(2)})`);
    }
    lines.push(`load average at end ${loadavg().map((v) => v.toFixed(2)).join(' ')}`);
    for (const l of lines) console.log(`MEASUREMENT: ${l}`);

    for (const [name, ms] of Object.entries(partP50)) expect(ms, `${name}: p50 ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(PART_P50_MAX_MS);
    for (const [name, r] of Object.entries(ratios)) expect(r >= 0.5 && r <= 2, `${name}: ratio ${r.toFixed(2)}`).toBe(true);
  }, 600_000);
});
```

Create `test/harness/sliceTrees.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The heavy density tree of the slice work bound's calibration (SP3d spec §5.2 "Calibration", §9 `slice.partWorst`):
 * an `interpolated` `add` of `noise detail` leaves with `density.noises.detail` at 16 octaves, double (the noise's
 * static maximum weight, 4 × 16 × 2 = 128 work units). Its work cost per sample is 1 + 8 × (129·L − 1) for L leaves
 * (L − 1 `add` nodes and L noises of 128 under `interpolated`), so with `PART_WORST_LEAVES` = 253 one 32-sample vertical
 * sample column costs 32 × 261,089 + COLUMN_SAMPLE_COST = 8,387,616 units, the largest that fits PART_BUDGET (254
 * leaves: 8,420,640). The `add` nodes form a balanced binary tree (depth ⌈log2 L⌉), so tier 2's depth bounds hold.
 * Used by the real-thread abort test (a part at the part bound) and the calibration (`test/integration/fieldSliceCalibration.test.ts`);
 * Task 28's `slice.partWorst` bench row reads the same tree.
 */
import type { Params } from '../../src/core/params/schema';
import { paramsWith } from './gen';

/** The leaf count of `slice.partWorst`'s tree: the largest L whose 32-sample vertical column fits PART_BUDGET. */
export const PART_WORST_LEAVES = 253;

type Node = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

/** A balanced binary `add` of `leaves` `noise detail` nodes (built level by level: no recursion). */
function noiseSum(leaves: number): Node {
  if (!Number.isInteger(leaves) || leaves < 1) throw new RangeError(`noiseSum: ${leaves} leaves`);
  let level: Node[] = Array.from({ length: leaves }, () => ({ op: 'noise', id: 'detail' }));
  while (level.length > 1) {
    const next: Node[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i + 1 < level.length; i += 2) next.push({ op: 'add', a: level[i]!, b: level[i + 1]! });
    if (level.length % 2 === 1) next.push(level[level.length - 1]!);
    level = next;
  }
  return level[0]!;
}

/** The `density.defs` source `{root: interpolated(noiseSum(leaves)), defs: {}}`. */
export function noiseSumTree(leaves: number = PART_WORST_LEAVES): Node {
  return { root: { op: 'interpolated', x: noiseSum(leaves) }, defs: {} };
}

/** DEFAULTS with `density.noises.detail` at 16 octaves, double, and `density.defs` = `noiseSumTree(leaves)`. */
export function partWorstParams(leaves: number = PART_WORST_LEAVES): Params {
  return paramsWith({ density: { noises: { detail: { octaves: 16, double: true } }, defs: noiseSumTree(leaves) } } as never);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The Density tab's JSON editor model (SP3d spec §3.5, §6 `inspectorEditor.test.ts`): validate-as-you-type issues with
 * their node paths after the 150 ms debounce (injected clock), the 50-issue cap, the 512 KiB buffer cap, Apply / Reset /
 * Escape (a successful Apply or Reset leaves a clean buffer with the caret on the same node path), and the dirty-buffer
 * rule for changes from elsewhere. Runs on a real `WorldSession` with `validateParamTrees`, as the page wires it.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import type { Seed64 } from '../../src/core/hash';
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import type { SessionResult } from '../../src/engine/session';
import { WorldSession } from '../../src/engine/session';
import { validateParamTrees } from '../../src/gen/trees';
import {
  createEditorModel, EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS, EDITOR_ISSUE_LINES, EDITOR_TEXT_MAX, issueLines, mapOffset, stripLeaf, TREE_LEAVES,
  type EditorClock, type EditorSession, type TreeLeaf,
} from '../../src/ui/inspector/editorModel';
import { nodeAt, printTree } from '../../src/ui/inspector/jsonText';

/** A clock whose timers run only when the test advances it. */
function fakeClock(): EditorClock & { advance(ms: number): void; pending(): number } {
  let now = 0;
  let next = 1;
  const timers = new Map<number, { at: number; fn: () => void }>();
  return {
    setTimeout(fn, ms) { const id = next++; timers.set(id, { at: now + ms, fn }); return id; },
    clearTimeout(id) { timers.delete(id); },
    advance(ms) {
      const end = now + ms;
      for (;;) {
        const due = [...timers].filter(([, t]) => t.at <= end).sort((a, b) => a[1].at - b[1].at)[0];
        if (due === undefined) break;
        timers.delete(due[0]);
        now = due[1].at;
        due[1].fn();
      }
      now = end;
    },
    pending: () => timers.size,
  };
}

const random = (): Seed64 => [5, 11];
const session = (): WorldSession => new WorldSession(random, { validateParams: validateParamTrees });

/** A model on `w` whose `sessionChanged` is called on every notification, as the page binds it. */
function open(w: WorldSession, leaf: TreeLeaf = 'density.defs') {
  const clock = fakeClock();
  const model = createEditorModel(leaf, w, clock);
  w.subscribe(() => model.sessionChanged());
  return { model, clock };
}

const DENSITY_TEXT = printTree(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density').text;
const RULES_TEXT = printTree(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules').text;
const ISLANDS = '{ "op": "const", "v": -1000000 }';

describe('the buffer and validation as you type', () => {
  test('opens clean on the session tree, for both leaves', () => {
    const w = session();
    const d = open(w).model.state;
    expect([d.text, d.clean, d.status, d.issues, d.stale, d.revision]).toEqual([DENSITY_TEXT, true, 'clean', [], false, 0]);
    expect(d.ranges).toEqual(printTree(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density').ranges);
    const r = open(w, 'surface.rules').model.state;
    expect([r.text, r.clean, r.status]).toEqual([RULES_TEXT, true, 'clean']);
    expect(TREE_LEAVES).toEqual(['density.defs', 'surface.rules']);
  });

  test('a typed tree is validated 150 ms after the last keystroke, with tier-2 issues at node paths', () => {
    const w = session();
    const { model, clock } = open(w);
    const seen: string[] = [];
    model.subscribe((s) => seen.push(s.status));
    const broken = DENSITY_TEXT.replace(ISLANDS, '{ "op": "bogus" }');
    model.edit(broken.slice(0, -1), 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS - 1);
    model.edit(broken, 0);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(model.state.clean).toBe(false);
    expect(model.state.ranges).toBeNull();
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS - 1);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('pending');
    clock.advance(1);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('invalid');
    expect(model.state.issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['root.b.x UNKNOWN_OP']);
    expect(issueLines(model.state)[0]).toMatch(/^root\.b\.x: UNKNOWN_OP — /);
    expect(model.state.ranges).not.toBeNull();
    expect(seen).toEqual(['pending', 'pending', 'invalid']);
    // Nothing was applied.
    expect(w.state.params.density.defs).toBe(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
    expect(w.canUndo).toBe(false);
  });

  test('tier-1 issues (−0, a "__proto__" def, Infinity) at node paths; syntax errors with line and column', () => {
    const { model, clock } = open(session());
    model.edit(DENSITY_TEXT.replace('"defs": {}', '"defs": { "__proto__": { "op": "y" } }').replace(ISLANDS, '{ "op": "const", "v": -0 }'), 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['defs."__proto__" BAD_KEY', 'root.b.x.v NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
    model.edit(DENSITY_TEXT.replace(ISLANDS, '{ "op": "const", "v": 1e999 }'), 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.issues.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['root.b.x.v NOT_FINITE']);
    model.edit('{\n  "root": { "op": "y" }\n  "defs": {}\n}', 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('syntax');
    expect(model.state.ranges).toBeNull();
    expect(issueLines(model.state)).toEqual(["line 3, column 3: expected ',' or '}', got '\"'"]);
    // A value-level issue shows the leaf path.
    model.edit('[]', 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(issueLines(model.state)[0]).toMatch(/^density\.defs: NOT_OBJECT — /);
  });

  test('rule trees: NOT_SOLID at the block state; a valid edit is valid', () => {
    const { model, clock } = open(session(), 'surface.rules');
    const at = RULES_TEXT.indexOf('"state": "stone"');
    model.edit(`${RULES_TEXT.slice(0, at)}"state": "air"${RULES_TEXT.slice(at + '"state": "stone"'.length)}`, 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.issues).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(model.state.issues[0]!.code).toBe('NOT_SOLID');
    expect(model.state.issues[0]!.path).toMatch(/^root\.rules\[\d+\](\.then|\.rules\[\d+\])*\.state$/);
    model.edit(RULES_TEXT.replace('"trueAtAndBelow": 0, "falseAtAndAbove": 8', '"trueAtAndBelow": 0, "falseAtAndAbove": 12'), 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect([model.state.status, model.state.issues]).toEqual(['valid', []]);
  });

  test('at most 50 issue lines and one "N more" line, the validators\' own "N more" included', () => {
    const { model, clock } = open(session());
    model.edit(`{ "root": { "op": "y" }, "defs": {}, "pad": [${Array(60).fill('1e999').join(', ')}] }`, 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.issues).toHaveLength(EDITOR_ISSUE_LINES);
    expect(model.state.more).toBe(10);
    const lines = issueLines(model.state);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(51);
    expect(lines[0]).toBe('pad[0]: NOT_FINITE — expected a finite number, got Infinity');
    expect(lines[50]).toBe('10 more');
    // Tier 2: 60 unknown ops in one tree (its validator caps at 50 + TOO_MANY_ISSUES).
    const ops = Array.from({ length: 30 }, () => '{ "op": "add", "a": { "op": "bogus" }, "b": { "op": "bogus" } }');
    let root = ops[0]!;
    for (let k = 1; k < ops.length; k++) root = `{ "op": "max", "a": ${root}, "b": ${ops[k]} }`;
    model.edit(`{ "root": ${root}, "defs": {} }`, 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.issues).toHaveLength(EDITOR_ISSUE_LINES);
    expect(model.state.issues.every((i) => i.code === 'UNKNOWN_OP')).toBe(true);
    expect(issueLines(model.state).at(-1)).toBe('10 more');
  });

  test('a buffer over 512 KiB is not parsed ("too large to validate") and cannot be applied; 512 KiB is', () => {
    const w = session();
    const { model, clock } = open(w);
    const valid = DENSITY_TEXT.replace(ISLANDS, '{ "op": "const", "v": -10 }');
    const padded = valid + ' '.repeat(EDITOR_TEXT_MAX - valid.length);
    expect(padded).toHaveLength(512 * 1024);
    model.edit(padded, 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('valid');
    model.edit(`${padded} `, 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);
    expect(model.state.status).toBe('tooLarge');

    expect(model.apply()).toBe(false);
    expect(w.state.params.density.defs).toBe(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE);
  });

  test('typing the printed text back makes the buffer clean again and cancels the pending validation', () => {
    const { model, clock } = open(session());
    model.edit(`${DENSITY_TEXT} `, 3);
    expect(clock.pending()).toBe(1);
    model.edit(DENSITY_TEXT, 3);
    expect([model.state.clean, model.state.status, clock.pending()]).toEqual([true, 'clean', 0]);
    expect(model.state.ranges).toEqual(printTree(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density').ranges);
  });
});

describe('Apply, Reset and Escape', () => {
  test('Apply sends the tree as one session step and re-prints it clean, the caret on the same node path', () => {

      reset: (p) => w.reset(p),

    expect(stripLeaf('surface.rules.root.rules[1]', 'surface.rules')).toBe('root.rules[1]');
    expect(stripLeaf('density.defs[0]', 'density.defs')).toBe('[0]');
    expect(stripLeaf('climate.scaleMul', 'density.defs')).toBe('climate.scaleMul');
  });

  test("Reset restores the profile's tree, clean, the caret on the same node path", () => {
    const w = session();
    const { model, clock } = open(w);
    model.edit(DENSITY_TEXT.replace(ISLANDS, '{ "op": "const", "v": -10 }'), 0);
    clock.advance(EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS);

  test('Escape reverts a dirty buffer, broken or not, to the current tree', () => {
    const w = session();

    model.edit('{ "root": ', 4);

    expect(model.state.caret).toBe(4);
    expect(w.canUndo).toBe(false);

  test('changes of other leaves never touch the buffer, clean or dirty', () => {
```

Create `test/unit/jsonText.test.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The inspector's JSON printer and parser (SP3d spec §3.5, D18): `printTree` writes `op`/`kind` first, the scalar fields
 * in table order, the children in evaluation order, `defs` keys sorted, a node without child nodes and a number array on
 * one line, and a −0 as `-0`; `parseTree` is an iterative parser that returns the value, the text range of every node
 * path and syntax errors with line and column, refuses duplicate keys and keeps a `"__proto__"` key for tier 1 to refuse.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkJson, type JsonFormat } from '../../src/core/params/json';
import { DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES } from '../../src/core/params/defaultTrees';
import type { Issue } from '../../src/core/params/kit';
import { CONDITION_KINDS, FIELDS, RULE_KINDS } from '../../src/gen/surface/rules';
import { lineColumn, nodeAt, parseTree, pathRange, printTree, type TreeRanges } from '../../src/ui/inspector/jsonText';
import { randomDensityExpr, SCHEMA_DENSITY_NOISES } from '../harness/densityFuzz';
import { testRng } from '../harness/stats';
import { randomSurfaceRules } from '../harness/surfaceFuzz';

/** Deep equality with `Object.is` on every primitive (so −0 ≠ +0) and equal own key sets (order ignored). */
function same(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof a !== 'object' || a === null || typeof b !== 'object' || b === null) return Object.is(a, b);
  if (Array.isArray(a) !== Array.isArray(b)) return false;
  const ka = Object.keys(a), kb = Object.keys(b);
  if (ka.length !== kb.length) return false;
  for (const k of ka) {
    if (!Object.hasOwn(b, k)) return false;
    if (!same((a as Record<string, unknown>)[k], (b as Record<string, unknown>)[k])) return false;
  }
  return true;
}

/** Every value of `v` by its node path in the format's syntax (test-local oracle: `''`/`root` top, `.key`, `[i]`). */
function valuesByPath(v: unknown, format: JsonFormat): Map<string, unknown> {
  const out = new Map<string, unknown>();
  const walk = (x: unknown, path: string): void => {
    out.set(path, x);
    if (Array.isArray(x)) x.forEach((c, i) => walk(c, `${path}[${i}]`));
    else if (typeof x === 'object' && x !== null) for (const k of Object.keys(x)) walk((x as Record<string, unknown>)[k], path === '' ? k : `${path}.${k}`);
  };
  walk(v, format === 'surfaceRules' ? 'root' : '');
  return out;
}

/** The node paths of `v` in pre-order (objects carrying the format's tag as a string), keys in printing order not needed. */
function nodePaths(v: unknown, format: JsonFormat): Set<string> {
  const tag = format === 'density' ? 'op' : 'kind';
  const out = new Set<string>();
  for (const [p, x] of valuesByPath(v, format)) {
    if (typeof x === 'object' && x !== null && !Array.isArray(x) && typeof (x as Record<string, unknown>)[tag] === 'string') out.add(p);
  }
  return out;
}

/** print ∘ parse is the identity, both ways, and the ranges of printed and parsed text agree and cover their values. */
function roundTrip(value: unknown, format: JsonFormat): void {
  const printed = printTree(value, format);
  const parsed = parseTree(printed.text, format);
  if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`printed text does not parse: ${parsed.error.message} at ${parsed.error.line}:${parsed.error.column}`);
  expect(same(parsed.value, value)).toBe(true);
  expect(printTree(parsed.value, format).text).toBe(printed.text);
  expect([...parsed.ranges.byPath]).toEqual([...printed.ranges.byPath]);
  expect(parsed.ranges.nodes).toEqual(printed.ranges.nodes);
  coverage(printed.text, printed.ranges, value, format);
}

/** Every value has a range, and the range's text parses to that value. */
function coverage(text: string, ranges: TreeRanges, value: unknown, format: JsonFormat): void {
  const values = valuesByPath(value, format);
  expect(new Set(ranges.byPath.keys())).toEqual(new Set(values.keys()));
  for (const [p, r] of ranges.byPath) {
    expect(r.start).toBeLessThan(r.end);
    expect(same(JSON.parse(text.slice(r.start, r.end)), values.get(p))).toBe(true);
  }
  expect(new Set(ranges.nodes)).toEqual(nodePaths(value, format));
  const starts = ranges.nodes.map((p) => ranges.byPath.get(p)!.start);
  expect(starts).toEqual([...starts].sort((a, b) => a - b));
}

describe('printTree', () => {
  test('the default density tree: op first, scalars, children in evaluation order, leaf nodes and knots on one line', () => {
    const { text } = printTree(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density');
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    expect(lines.slice(0, 5)).toEqual(['{', '  "root": {', '    "op": "max",', '    "a": {', '      "op": "add",']);
    expect(lines.at(-2)).toBe('  "defs": {}');
    expect(lines.at(-1)).toBe('}');
    expect(text).toContain('"knots": [[-64, 0], [-40, 1], [240, 1], [320, 0]]');
    expect(text).toMatch(/"op": "recip",\n\s*"x": \{ "op": "param", "path": "density.noises.jag.clampSigma" \}/);
    expect(text).toContain('"a": { "op": "col", "field": "offset" }');
    expect(text).toContain('"x": { "op": "const", "v": -1000000 }');
    // tap: name before its child; clamp: lo, hi before x; slide: knots before x.
    expect(text).toMatch(/"op": "tap",\n\s*"name": "islands",\n\s*"x": /);
    expect(text).toMatch(/"op": "clamp",\n\s*"lo": 0,\n\s*"hi": 1,\n\s*"x": \{/);
    expect(text).toMatch(/"op": "slide",\n\s*"knots": \[\[-64, 0\], .*\],\n\s*"x": \{ "op": "noise", "id": "overhang" \}/);
    expect(text.endsWith('\n')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('defs keys are sorted, refs and mutes print in place, a −0 prints as -0', () => {
    const tree = {
      defs: { zeta: { op: 'y' }, alpha: { op: 'const', v: -0 }, Mid: { op: 'neg', x: { op: 'ref', name: 'alpha' } } },
      root: { x: { op: 'ref', name: 'zeta' }, mute: { neg: true, param: 'density.detailAmpLo' }, name: 't', op: 'tap' },
    };
    const { text } = printTree(tree, 'density');
    expect(text).toBe([
      '{',
      '  "root": {',
      '    "op": "tap",',
      '    "name": "t",',
      '    "mute": { "param": "density.detailAmpLo", "neg": true },',
      '    "x": { "op": "ref", "name": "zeta" }',
      '  },',
      '  "defs": {',
      '    "Mid": {',
      '      "op": "neg",',
      '      "x": { "op": "ref", "name": "alpha" }',
      '    },',
      '    "alpha": { "op": "const", "v": -0 },',
      '    "zeta": { "op": "y" }',
      '  }',
      '}',
    ].join('\n'));
  });

  test('rules: kind first, the fields in FIELDS order, conditions before then, a node without children on one line', () => {
    const { text } = printTree(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules');
    expect(text.startsWith('{\n  "kind": "sequence",\n  "rules": [\n    {\n')).toBe(true);
    expect(text).toContain('{ "kind": "block", "state": "stone" }');
    expect(text).toMatch(/"kind": "condition",\n\s*"if": \{ "kind": "verticalGradient", "trueAtAndBelow": 0, "falseAtAndAbove": 8 \},\n\s*"then": /);
    expect(text).toContain('{ "kind": "noiseThreshold", "noise": "surface.noises.patch", "min": { "param": "surface.patchThreshold" }, "max": 8 }');
    const one = printTree({ kind: 'condition', then: { state: 'sand', kind: 'block' }, if: { kind: 'biome', biomes: ['desert', 'beach'] } }, 'surfaceRules').text;
    expect(one).toBe('{\n  "kind": "condition",\n  "if": { "kind": "biome", "biomes": ["desert", "beach"] },\n  "then": { "kind": "block", "state": "sand" }\n}');
    expect(printTree({ kind: 'sequence', rules: [] }, 'surfaceRules').text).toBe('{ "kind": "sequence", "rules": [] }');
  });

  test('unknown keys print after the known ones, sorted; a value that is not JSON throws', () => {
    expect(printTree({ root: { zz: 1, op: 'y', aa: [true, 'x'] }, defs: {}, extra: 2 }, 'density').text)
      .toBe('{\n  "root": { "op": "y", "aa": [true, "x"], "zz": 1 },\n  "defs": {},\n  "extra": 2\n}');
    expect(() => printTree({ root: { op: 'const', v: Number.NaN }, defs: {} }, 'density')).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => printTree({ root: null, defs: {} }, 'density')).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  test('FIELDS is exported frozen with every rule and condition kind, names only', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(FIELDS)).toEqual([...RULE_KINDS, ...CONDITION_KINDS]);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(FIELDS)).toBe(true);
    for (const k of Object.keys(FIELDS)) {
      const f = FIELDS[k as keyof typeof FIELDS];
      expect(Object.isFrozen(f)).toBe(true);
      for (const name of f) expect(typeof name).toBe('string');
    }
    expect(FIELDS.stoneDepth).toEqual(['side', 'offset', 'addSurfaceDepth']);
  });
});

describe('print ∘ parse', () => {
  test('is the identity on both default trees, with equal ranges that cover their text', () => {
    roundTrip(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density');
    roundTrip(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules');
  });

  test('is the identity on 200 fuzz trees (100 density, −0 included; 100 rule trees of the three styles)', () => {
    const next = testRng(2020);
    let negZero = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < 100; k++) {
      const tree = randomDensityExpr(next, { noises: SCHEMA_DENSITY_NOISES });
      if (printTree(tree, 'density').text.includes('-0,') || /-0 \}/.test(printTree(tree, 'density').text)) negZero++;
      roundTrip(tree, 'density');
    }
    expect(negZero).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (let k = 0; k < 100; k++) roundTrip(randomSurfaceRules(next, { style: (['free', 'fastPath', 'nearMiss'] as const)[k % 3]! }), 'surfaceRules');
  });

  test('a −0 is printed and parsed back as −0, and tier 1 refuses it at its path', () => {
    const tree = { root: { op: 'clamp', x: { op: 'const', v: -0 }, lo: -0, hi: 1 }, defs: {} };
    const { text } = printTree(tree, 'density');
    expect(text).toContain('"lo": -0');
    expect(text).toContain('{ "op": "const", "v": -0 }');
    const r = parseTree(text, 'density');
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.error.message);
    const root = (r.value as { root: { lo: number; x: { v: number } } }).root;
    expect(Object.is(root.lo, -0)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.is(root.x.v, -0)).toBe(true);
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkJson(r.value, '', out, 'density')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['root.lo NEGATIVE_ZERO', 'root.x.v NEGATIVE_ZERO']);
  });
});

describe('parseTree', () => {
  test('ranges of typed text: any whitespace and key order, rule paths start with root', () => {
    const text = '{"rules":[ {"state":"stone","kind":"block"} ,\n{"kind":"condition","then":{"kind":"bandlands"},"if":{"kind":"not","if":{"kind":"skyOpen"}}}],"kind":"sequence"}';
    const r = parseTree(text, 'surfaceRules');
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.error.message);
    coverage(text, r.ranges, r.value, 'surfaceRules');
    expect(r.ranges.nodes).toEqual(['root', 'root.rules[0]', 'root.rules[1]', 'root.rules[1].then', 'root.rules[1].if', 'root.rules[1].if.if']);
    expect(text.slice(r.ranges.byPath.get('root.rules[1].if')!.start, r.ranges.byPath.get('root.rules[1].if')!.end)).toBe('{"kind":"not","if":{"kind":"skyOpen"}}');
    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(r.value)).toBe(Object.prototype);
  });

  test('syntax errors carry their offset, line and column (1-based)', () => {
    const err = (text: string) => {
      const r = parseTree(text, 'density');
      if (r.ok) throw new Error('parsed');
      return `${r.error.line}:${r.error.column} ${r.error.message}`;
    };
    expect(err('{\n  "root": { "op": "y" },\n  "defs": {\n}')).toBe('4:2 unexpected end of text');
    expect(err('{ "root": [1, 2,] }')).toBe("1:17 expected a value, got ']'");
    expect(err('{ "root": { "op": "y" } "defs": {} }')).toBe("1:25 expected ',' or '}', got '\"'");
    expect(err('[1 2]')).toBe("1:4 expected ',' or ']', got '2'");
    expect(err('{ root: 1 }')).toBe("1:3 expected a string key, got 'r'");
    expect(err('{ "root" 1 }')).toBe("1:10 expected ':', got '1'");
    expect(err('{\n\t"a": "x\ny" }')).toBe('2:9 control character in a string');
    expect(err('{ "a": "abc }')).toBe('1:8 unterminated string');
    expect(err('{ "a": "\\q" }')).toBe('1:9 bad escape \\q');
    expect(err('{ "a": "\\u12G4" }')).toBe('1:9 bad escape \\u12G4');
    expect(err('{ "a": 01 }')).toBe("1:9 expected ',' or '}', got '1'");
    expect(err('{ "a": -x }')).toBe('1:8 bad number');
    expect(err('{ "a": tru }')).toBe("1:8 expected a value, got 't'");
    expect(err('{} {}')).toBe("1:4 unexpected text after the value, got '{'");
    expect(err('')).toBe('1:1 unexpected end of text');
    expect(err('  \n ')).toBe('2:2 unexpected end of text');
  });

  test('numbers, escapes and literals parse as JSON.parse does; 1e999 is Infinity for tier 1 to refuse', () => {
    const text = '{"a":[0,-0,1.5e3,-2E-2,1e999,true,false,null],"s":"q\\"\\\\\\/\\b\\f\\n\\r\\t\\u00e9\\ud83d\\ude00"}';
    const r = parseTree(text, 'density');
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.error.message);
    expect(same(r.value, JSON.parse(text))).toBe(true);
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    checkJson(r.value, '', out, 'density');
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['a[1] NEGATIVE_ZERO', 'a[4] NOT_FINITE', 'a[7] NOT_JSON']);
  });

  test('a duplicate key is a syntax error at its position', () => {
    const r = parseTree('{\n  "root": { "op": "y" },\n  "root": { "op": "y" }\n}', 'density');
    expect(r.ok).toBe(false);
    if (r.ok) return;
    expect(r.error).toEqual({ offset: 29, line: 3, column: 3, message: 'duplicate key "root"' });
  });

  test('"__proto__" survives parsing as an own key of a plain object, and tier 1 refuses it at the path its range has', () => {
    const text = '{ "root": { "op": "ref", "name": "a" }, "defs": { "__proto__": { "op": "y" }, "a": { "op": "y" } } }';
    const r = parseTree(text, 'density');
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.error.message);
    const defs = (r.value as { defs: object }).defs;
    expect(Object.keys(defs)).toEqual(['__proto__', 'a']);
    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(defs)).toBe(Object.prototype);
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(defs, '__proto__')?.value).toEqual({ op: 'y' });
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkJson(r.value, '', out, 'density')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual(['defs."__proto__" BAD_KEY']);
    const range = r.ranges.byPath.get('defs."__proto__"')!;
    expect(text.slice(range.start, range.end)).toBe('{ "op": "y" }');
    expect(r.ranges.nodes).toEqual(['root', 'defs."__proto__"', 'defs.a']);
  });

  test('a 100,000-deep array parses without a stack overflow (ranges to depth 48) and tier 1 refuses it', () => {
    const deep = '['.repeat(100_000) + ']'.repeat(100_000);
    const r = parseTree(deep, 'density');
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(r.error.message);
    expect(r.ranges.byPath.size).toBe(49);
    expect(r.ranges.byPath.get('')).toEqual({ start: 0, end: 200_000 });
    expect(r.ranges.byPath.get('[0]'.repeat(48))).toEqual({ start: 48, end: 200_000 - 48 });
    const out: Issue[] = [];
    expect(checkJson(r.value, '', out, 'density')).toBeUndefined();
    expect(out.map((i) => `${i.path} ${i.code}`)).toEqual([`${'[0]'.repeat(48)} JSON_TOO_DEEP`]);
    const open = parseTree('['.repeat(100_000), 'density');
    expect(open.ok ? null : `${open.error.offset} ${open.error.message}`).toBe('100000 unexpected end of text');
  });
});

describe('ranges', () => {
  test('nodeAt is the innermost node whose range holds the offset; pathRange falls back to the longest named prefix', () => {
    const { text, ranges } = printTree(DEFAULT_DENSITY_TREE, 'density');
    const islands = text.indexOf('{ "op": "const", "v": -1000000 }');
    expect(nodeAt(ranges, islands)).toBe('root.b.x');
    expect(nodeAt(ranges, islands + 10)).toBe('root.b.x');
    expect(nodeAt(ranges, text.indexOf('"name": "islands"'))).toBe('root.b');
    expect(nodeAt(ranges, 0)).toBeNull();
    expect(nodeAt(ranges, text.length)).toBeNull();
    expect(pathRange(ranges, 'root.b.x.v')).toEqual(ranges.byPath.get('root.b.x.v'));
    expect(pathRange(ranges, 'root.b.x.nope')).toEqual(ranges.byPath.get('root.b.x'));
    expect(pathRange(ranges, 'defs.gone.x')).toEqual(ranges.byPath.get('defs'));
    expect(pathRange(ranges, 'nowhere')).toEqual(ranges.byPath.get(''));
    const rules = printTree(DEFAULT_SURFACE_RULES, 'surfaceRules').ranges;
    expect(pathRange(rules, 'root.rules[2].if.falseAtAndAbove')).toEqual(rules.byPath.get('root.rules[2].if.falseAtAndAbove'));
    expect(pathRange(rules, 'root.rules[99]')).toEqual(rules.byPath.get('root.rules'));
  });

  test('lineColumn counts lines and columns from 1', () => {
    expect(lineColumn('ab\ncd', 0)).toEqual({ line: 1, column: 1 });
    expect(lineColumn('ab\ncd', 2)).toEqual({ line: 1, column: 3 });
    expect(lineColumn('ab\ncd', 3)).toEqual({ line: 2, column: 1 });
    expect(lineColumn('ab\ncd', 5)).toEqual({ line: 2, column: 3 });
  });
});
```
